## **Why this role exists**
Every city, county, and school district buys things. Roads, software, cleaning services, IT infrastructure. The total is somewhere north of two trillion dollars a year. And almost all of it moves through procurement processes designed for a different era: slow; paper-heavy; opaque and exhausting for everyone involved.
Civic Marketplace was built to fix that. We're a modern, data-driven platform where government agencies discover, evaluate, and engage suppliers. Where businesses, especially smaller and growing ones, can actually find and win public sector work without needing a dedicated contracts team to navigate the maze.
We're past the point of proving this works. Agencies are live on the platform, real money moves through it, and we're now combining that marketplace infrastructure with AI in ways that could genuinely transform how procurement works. Not just incrementally but structurally.
None of it works without data that can be trusted. Procurement is a data problem before it is a software problem: who the suppliers actually are, what they can genuinely deliver, which contracts an agency is already entitled to buy from, what this thing cost the county next door. That information exists, scattered across thousands of agency portals, state registries and PDF attachments, in no agreed format, and nobody has assembled it properly. Whoever does gets to define how public money is spent for the next decade. That's this role.
## **The problem you'd own**
The hard part isn't moving data from one place to another. Any engineer here will tell you the pipelines are the easy half.
The hard part is that public procurement has no shared vocabulary. The same supplier turns up as four different legal entities across three registries, and two of the spellings are wrong. Commodity codes are applied inconsistently, or not at all. A cooperative contract one agency can buy from today is invisible to the agency next door because it was published as a PDF on a portal with no API. Every source you touch is incomplete, inconsistent, or both, and most of it is public record, so you can't quietly correct it. You have to model the mess honestly.
And the bar just moved. We recently launched an MCP integration that lets agencies request quotes through Claude, GPT and Copilot. When an agent answers a procurement question, a wrong answer doesn't read like a bug, it reads like advice, and in public spending, bad advice ends up in a council meeting. That puts weight on freshness, lineage and provenance that most product data layers never carry. As we build out our agentic procurement capabilities, the reliability of that data, and how we prepare it for retrieval, becomes our most critical engineering challenge.
So this is an entity resolution and data trust problem dressed as a pipeline problem, and it's yours to solve. You'd work out what is actually wrong with the data, which is rarely what everyone assumes, then build the fix so it holds for every source we add next. Not a script per source held together by whoever wrote it.
## **About the role**
You would be our first dedicated data engineering hire, reporting to Mikey Mo, our Head of Engineering. Data work today sits with the product engineering team and gets done alongside shipping features. It works, but it belongs to whoever last touched it, and that isn't a foundation for what comes next.
To give you a sense of the gap: awarded quotes that slip through the platform get manually caught by our commercial team and hand-entered into HubSpot instead. Supplier onboarding data follows the same pattern. So as and when the platform and HubSpot become out of sync, it makes it difficult to say with confidence which one is right.
This is a build-and-do role. You'd collaborate closely with our Head of Engineering to shape the architecture, and you'd also write the pipelines, carry the pager for them, and go and read the raw source when a number looks wrong. If you're looking for a role where you set direction in isolation and hand implementation to other people, this isn't it. If you want substantial responsibility and scope as a function lead alongside our Head of Engineering while still enjoying the craft yourself, it very much is.
You would not be starting from nothing. There's a live platform with real transactions running through it, a product engineering team who know where the bodies are buried, and access most people in this field would have to scrape for: Civic Marketplace is a member of the NIGP Business Council, with real partnerships across councils of governments. Most people doing this job spend their first year getting the data access. You'd start with the door already open.
## **What you'd own**
Five things, and the freedom to decide how.
1. **Trust in the data.** The north star. A golden, trusted dataset that powers Civic Marketplace's analytics, so when someone asks how many quotes were awarded last quarter, or how much GMV we've captured, there's one number, and it's right. You'd own the diagnosis and the fix.
2. **Ingestion.** Pipelines that pull supplier, agency, solicitation and contract data out of sources never designed to be read by anything but a person. Reliable, observable, and cheap enough to add the next source without a meeting about whether it's worth it.
3. **The canonical model.** One supplier, one record, across every spelling, trading name, subsidiary and registry identifier. One shared definition of a contract vehicle, a commodity, an agency, that product, sales and customer success all use and none of them argue with. This is the unglamorous part that makes everything downstream possible.
4. **The system underneath.** Testing, lineage and freshness, so when the platform tells an agency something we know where it came from and when. And self-serve data for product, customer success and analytics, so nobody queues behind an engineer for a number. Everything you build should work for the next source without you in the loop. This is where AI earns its place, turning what is currently hand-checked into something repeatable.
5. **Agentic data infrastructure.** As we scale our use of AI-native procurement, you will own the data layer that powers our agentic workflows. This goes beyond standard retrieval. You will design ingestion and storage strategies, including optimizing vector pipelines like Pinecone for RAG, to ensure our agents have the high-fidelity, context-aware data necessary to perform reliably in production.
You'd work closely with product engineering, customer success and our Growth Lead. Application feature work stays with the product engineering team, so you're not competing for that ground. You own the layer they build on top of.
## **How we use AI**
We use Claude daily, across content pipelines, community response and internal knowledge, and increasingly inside the product itself. That's real, not a line in a job ad.
For this role it cuts two ways. There's how you work: source profiling, schema mapping, test generation, the documentation that otherwise never gets written. Most of that is now automatable, and we expect you to automate it. And there's what you build: the data layer that decides whether agentic procurement is trustworthy or embarrassing. The second is the harder and more interesting problem.
What we care about is not whether you can use it. Everyone says they can. It's whether you reach for it to make something repeatable. The difference between someone who writes pipelines faster and someone who builds the tooling that means the next hundred sources don't each need hand-holding is the difference we're hiring for.
If you've built data quality tooling, evaluation harnesses, retrieval pipelines or automated documentation from scratch, tell us about them. If AI has changed how you think about the work and not just how fast you produce it, we especially want to hear that.
Our stack: Snowflake, Postgres, dbt, Fivetran, HubSpot, PostHog, Metabase.
## **What you bring**
### **You'll need:**
* Data engineering experience in a startup or scale-up, where you've built the platform rather than inherited one
* Strong SQL and Python, and the judgement to know when the warehouse is the wrong place to solve a problem
* A data model you designed that other people had to live with, including the parts you would do differently now
* Real experience of messy external sources: half-documented APIs, flat-file drops, scraped pages, PDFs, and data you neither control nor can correct
* Entity resolution or record linkage experience, or clear evidence you'd be good at it. This is the centre of the job, not an edge case
* A commercial head. You can tell the difference between a data problem that's blocking revenue and one that's merely interesting, and you sequence accordingly
* The instinct to find out why a number is wrong before proposing a fix. Sometimes it's the pipeline, sometimes the model, sometimes the source was always like that, and those need different answers
* The instinct to build systems that scale rather than pipelines that run once
* Genuine AI fluency, in the sense above
* The determination to stay positive through the ups and downs of a fast-moving startup, and to find a path through problems rather than wait for conditions to be right
* Comfort operating remotely across timezones with real autonomy and not much oversight
* Curiosity about why public sector data is different. You don't need to have done it. You do need to want to understand it
### **You'll stand out if you have:**
* Govtech, public sector or civic tech background, or experience working with public records and open data
* Familiarity with supplier and procurement data: SAM.gov and UEI, DUNS, NAICS or UNSPSC, cooperative purchasing, COG or NIGP
* Experience with search and retrieval, whether OpenSearch, Elasticsearch or vector pipelines (like Pinecone or Milvus) feeding an LLM product.
* Bilingual English and Spanish, especially valuable for supplier data quality and onboarding
* Experience being the first data hire on a team that had been doing it themselves
## **Why you'll love this role**
**The problem is genuinely important.** Public procurement touches every road, school and hospital. Getting it right matters in ways most B2B SaaS doesn't. And you'd be widening access for small and local businesses, which is the part of this that keeps us up at night in a good way.
**The dataset doesn't exist yet.** Most data engineering jobs are being the fifth person to tidy the same warehouse. This one is assembling something nobody has assembled properly: a clean, current picture of who supplies the public sector and what public money actually buys.
**The scope is unusual.** First dedicated data hire, reporting to Mikey, taking substantial responsibility for the function and co-designing the architecture decisions that come with it.

**People who care.** Small team, direct access to founders, genuine investment in doing things well. We move fast, but we don't move sloppy.
## **How we work**
**Build bridges to help customers win.** We are obsessively focused on helping both agencies and suppliers succeed. That's not a value statement. It's the job.
**High velocity, high ownership.** We move quickly, make decisions, and take responsibility for outcomes. There's no one to hand things off to and no one to hide behind.
**In the arena.** We stay close to our users. We learn from them directly. We build based on what we see, not what we assume.
**Learning quotient.** Rapid iteration isn't just a process. It's a mindset. We'd rather be wrong fast and right eventually than slow and cautious throughout.
And because we work in public procurement, how we do things matters as much as what we achieve. We hold ourselves to the standards our agencies are held to.
## **The interview process**
All interviews are via video conferencing by default.
We'll ask you to walk us through something you've built and the decisions you'd make differently now. We'll also set you a short exercise on genuinely messy source data rather than an abstract algorithm puzzle, because reasoning about real data is the job. ## The Role
Clio is building an agentic Security Operations Center. Instead of staffing a room of analysts to watch dashboards, we're building the AI-driven system that does the watching: it triages alerts, investigates, and takes the first response action, so the humans on the team spend their time on the work that needs a human. Our goal is to automate every event we can, and we mean every event.
We're looking for the manager who builds both the Blue Team's software and the team itself. This is an engineering leadership role first. The team writes software: detection pipelines, automated response, the agents, and the integrations that tie them into Clio's products and infrastructure. You'll lead that team, set its technical direction, and stay close enough to the code to review it and contribute. Beyond leading, you'll get into the codebase and make changes in the agentic SOC and Clio's core applications, accelerated by Claude and Codex.
You won't be working alone. Clio's Red Team finds and exploits weaknesses; the Threat Intelligence function tracks who is targeting us and how. The Blue Team takes what both of them learn and turns it into defenses that hold: hardened infrastructure, hardened product, and detection that catches the next attempt automatically.
## Building the Team
As you onboard, one of the first tasks will be building out the team. We care much more about finding the right people than filling seats quickly, and you'll own that search: defining what great looks like, interviewing, and selling the work to people who have plenty of options.
The people we want are builders who are curious about security, or security people who build. You'll set the culture for a small, senior-leaning team that ships, owns the results, and makes its work visible to the rest of the company.
## A Day in the Life
* AI-assisted code writing in core Clio applications to add observability to the system
* Sitting with the Red Team after an exercise to turn their findings into detections and fixes, then confirming the fixes hold on retest
* Reading a new threat intel brief on a technique being used against SaaS companies, and deciding which part of the infrastructure to harden first
* Working with a product engineering team to ensure incoming changes do not weaken the security posture of the application
* Spotting a spike in suspicious account activity, and asking why a human noticed it before the automation did
* Interviewing a candidate, then writing up honest feedback the same afternoon
* Reviewing PRs from SOC agents, and developers from engineering teams at Clio to ensure changes are securely implemented

### Build the agentic SOC
* Lead the design and build of an AI-driven SOC that monitors, triages, investigates, and responds with as little human toil as possible
* Treat every manual alert-handling step as a candidate for automation, and measure how much of the queue the system closes on its own
* Own detection engineering: detection-as-code, testing, tuning
* Make sure the automation is trustworthy: clear guardrails on what it can do unattended, audit trails for what it did, and a human escalation path when it isn't sure
* Work with the wider security team on incident response when something real happens, and feed what you learn back into the system
### Harden against new adversary techniques
* Work with Threat Intelligence to turn new tactics, techniques, and procedures into concrete hardening work and detection coverage
* Prioritize infrastructure hardening across cloud, identity, and endpoints based on observed attacker behaviour rather than benchmarks alone
### Harden Clio's products
* Work directly on the core security functionality of Clio's fleet of products, alongside the product engineering teams that own them
* Push security controls into the platform itself, so every product team gets them without having to rebuild them
### Close the loop with the Red Team
* Partner with the Red Team to find vulnerabilities, fix them, and verify the fixes
* Run exercises to measure detection coverage against real attack paths, and close the gaps they expose
### Detect and stop product abuse
* Build automated detection for abuse of Clio's products: account takeover, fraud, scripted misuse, and patterns we haven't named yet
* Automate the response as well as the detection, so confirmed abuse is contained without waiting for someone to notice
* Work closely with SecDev to build preventative code generation paths, agent.md guides, and create pre-commit hooks
### Lead the team
* Hire, grow, and retain a team of engineers

* Help define how the team scales toward follow-the-sun coverage
## What You Bring

* Experience leading engineers, as a people manager or a tech lead who has grown into the role
* Hands-on security experience: secure development, and finding and fixing vulnerabilities
* Comfort making decisions about automation and AI where the cost of being wrong is a locked out lawyer that can sue us for free, and designing systems that fail safely

As Senior Product Manager, Software Delivery, you will sit at the handoff point between ideas and engineering — taking a raw idea or ask and shaping it into a well-formed request the software team can build against. You own the what: defining the problem, scope, and acceptance criteria behind every request. * Advocate for how and when work should happen: partner with the Project Manager, who owns sprint planning and delivery mechanics, to make sure sequencing and timing reflect genuine priority rather than convenience.

# Product Designer
London, England, United Kingdom
**About CreativeX**
CreativeX is B2B SaaS technology platform that helps global marketing teams make smarter creative decisions and elevate creative expression through the clarity of data. Our technology powers creative decision-making at some of the biggest brands in the world, including Google, Unilever, Pepsi, Bayer, Mondelez, Heineken, and more.
We use computer vision and other machine learning techniques to extract creative data from our client's digital advertising copy and transform those previously dark signals into a standardised data model at industrial scale. This creates a new, unique and powerful first party data set that represents the last and most impactful untapped reservoir of advertising performance.
That's because multiple studies have shown that the "Creative" itself is responsible for half of sales lift online, higher than reach, targeting, brand, & recency combined. But creative impact has always been the least analysed and least understood component of a complex set of marketing variables.
This is the problem CreativeX is focussed on solving. We're an end-to-end solution to ingest, process, and analyse content at scale. We help brands isolate creative elements so they can be analysed against downstream ad impact metrics, from clickthrough rates to brand lift.
Our objective is to help marketing organisations power every creative decision with data.
**Product Design Team**
As a Product Designer, you'll help shape the next generation of the CreativeX platform, taking problems from discovery through to shipped experiences across defined areas of the product. You'll be the design lead in a product trio alongside a Product Manager and an Engineering Lead, owning whether users want what we build and whether they can figure out how to use it, while sharing discovery, outcomes and trade-offs with your partners. CreativeX is a complex product with rich data, multiple user types and increasingly sophisticated AI capabilities, and as AI increases the volume and speed of creative production, you'll make that complexity work for marketers, helping them measure performance fast, find the patterns behind what's working and see whether their full set of ads is delivering the strategy. Our roadmap is framed as problems to solve, not screens to make, so we expect you to bring a point of view. Product Design is a small, hands-on team in a scale-up: you'll be trusted with real ownership early, and this hire is an important step in growing the team.
**What you will do**
* Own design for defined product areas, from understanding the problem through to working with Product and Engineering to ship the right experience
* Get close to marketers and creative teams through customer conversations, research and usability testing, using what you learn to inform design decisions
* Partner with Product and Engineering in discovery to validate real problems, challenge assumptions and make sensible trade-offs between customer value, business needs and technical constraints
* Turn creative data, insights and AI-powered capabilities into intuitive workflows, dashboards and decision-making tools
* Design for the platform, not just the feature, building on existing patterns and connecting experiences across CreativeX
* Use and extend our design system, creating and documenting patterns and components so they're implemented consistently
* Raise the quality bar through strong interaction and visual design craft, and by giving and receiving feedback in critiques
* Learn from what you ship, using customer feedback, product data and research to improve the experience
**What success looks like**
*In your first 90 days*
* Learn the CreativeX platform, our customers and our design system, and work as the design lead in your product trio
* Take ownership of a defined product area and ship, or get build-ready, your first piece of work
* Contribute to our AI-powered product work and add to or improve patterns in our design system
* Join customer conversations and use what you hear to shape your design decisions
*In your first year*
* Own design for one or more product areas, taking work from discovery through to launch with little direction
* Ship work you can point to, using customer feedback and product data to show whether it solved the problem
* Help build out new parts of our design system and make the product feel more coherent across areas
* Shape how design works at CreativeX as the team grows, including supporting newer designers
**Who you are**
* 3–5 years of product design experience, with a portfolio that shows how you framed problems, explored options, made trade-offs and learned from what shipped
* Strong interaction and visual design craft, confident in Figma, prototyping and design systems, and familiar with Slack and Linear
* Experience using research, usability testing and customer feedback to inform design decisions
* A systems mindset and the ability to make complex information, workflows and data easy to understand
* Clear, collaborative communication: you challenge ideas constructively, take feedback well and know when to ship and learn
* Experience working closely with Product and Engineering in a product trio or small team, with real ownership
* *Nice to have:* B2B SaaS, data-heavy or analytics products; marketing, advertising or martech; AI-powered products; mentoring junior designers; scale-up experience
At CreativeX, we encourage applicants of all backgrounds and identities to apply for roles that align with their own interests and career trajectory. If you fit the description above and see yourself in this role, we would love to see your application! *Unfortunately, we are unable to offer visa sponsorship at this time.*
**What we offer**
🍎 Private Medical Insurance and Health Cash Plan ✈️ Generous time off + bank holidays 📚 Education budget to be used for individual learning experiences or grouped with your team for joint learning 🧘 Annual subscription to Calm and Headspace for your mental wellbeing 🎟 Monthly coaching to talk to a trained professional about career goals, relationships, and personal development 💵 Competitive salary including stock options, as we believe that everyone should have a stake in the business 🍼 4-month full pay parenting leave for all employees who have been with the company for one (1) year
***CreativeX provides equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees.***

**Location: Glasgow**
### We are looking for experienced **Transaction Monitoring CDD Analyst** to provide independent assurance across a range of Financial Crime activities, including **Transaction Monitoring, Customer Due Diligence (CDD/KYC), Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD), Sanctions and Screening**.
The role will assess whether Financial Crime risks have been appropriately identified, investigated, evidenced, documented and managed in line with relevant policies, procedures, regulatory requirements and Quality Assurance standards.
Following appropriate training and accreditation, you will complete accurate, evidence-based QA reviews, identify control or quality gaps, support remediation and provide constructive feedback to operational teams. You will work closely with Quality Assurance colleagues, Financial Crime Operations and subject matter experts to drive consistent quality standards and continuous improvement across the Financial Crime control environment.
## Job requirements
**Key Responsibilities**
* Perform independent **Quality Assurance reviews** across Financial Crime processes, which may include:
+ Transaction Monitoring investigations
+ CDD/KYC onboarding, periodic reviews and trigger events
+ Enhanced Due Diligence and High-Risk Customer reviews
+ PEP individual and entity assessments
+ Customer and Payment Screening
+ Sanctions and enhanced screening investigations
+ Transactional analysis and Financial Crime Exit decisions
* Assess cases against relevant policies, standards, procedures and QA methodologies to determine whether risks have been appropriately identified, investigated, evidenced and concluded.
* Review customer and transactional information to identify **AML, terrorist financing, sanctions and wider Financial Crime risks and red flags**.
* Identify gaps in investigation quality, documentation, evidence, rationale or decision-making and record clear, accurate and proportionate QA findings.
* Apply a risk-based approach when assessing the severity and impact of issues, escalating complex or material findings through the appropriate channels.
* Support remediation activities and provide constructive feedback, coaching and challenge to operational and Quality Control teams.
* Participate in calibration activities to promote consistency in QA assessments and decision-making.
* Conduct or contribute to **root-cause analysis, trend identification and thematic reviews** to identify recurring issues and potential control weaknesses.
* Maintain accurate QA records and contribute to management information, reporting and governance updates.
* Work collaboratively with Operations, Compliance, Quality Control, Policy and Financial Crime subject matter experts to support quality improvement initiatives.
* Contribute to process enhancements, procedure reviews, training and continuous improvement initiatives.
**Essential Skills & Experience**
* Previous experience within **Financial Crime, AML or Financial Crime Operations**, with experience in one or more of the following:
+ Transaction Monitoring
+ CDD / KYC
+ Enhanced Due Diligence
+ High-Risk Customer Reviews
+ PEP assessments
+ Customer or Payment Screening
+ Sanctions investigations
+ Financial Crime investigations
* Experience within **Quality Assurance, Quality Control, Audit, Testing, Oversight or other risk-based review activities**.
* Strong understanding of **AML, terrorist financing, sanctions and Financial Crime risk management principles**.
* Ability to interpret and apply policies, standards and procedures to customer, transactional or investigation scenarios.
* Strong analytical and investigative skills, with the ability to identify Financial Crime risks, red flags, control weaknesses and gaps in evidence or rationale.
* Strong attention to detail and sound judgement and decision-making skills.
* Ability to clearly document findings and provide evidence-based conclusions.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to provide constructive feedback and appropriately challenge stakeholders.
* Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver high-quality work within agreed timelines.
**Experience in one or more of the following would be advantageous:**
* Retail, Business, Corporate, Investment or Wholesale Banking.
* Complex corporate entities, financial institutions, funds or trusts.
* Beneficial ownership and ownership/control assessments.
* Source of Wealth and Source of Funds reviews.
* Structuring/smurfing, mule activity, cash-intensive businesses and unexplained third-party payments.
* Complex corporate structures, shell companies, high-risk jurisdictions and trade-based money laundering risks.
* Customer and Payment Screening, including sanctions alert investigation and escalation.
* PEPs, adverse media, sanctions and enhanced screening.
* Understanding of relevant sanctions regimes and associated ownership and control requirements.
* QA sampling, checklists, error classification, remediation, issue management and appeals.
* Root-cause analysis, thematic reviews, trend analysis and management information.

This role sits within Deltatre's Technical Operations Center (TOC), a 24/7 global operation that acquires signals and streams linear channels and live events via satellite, IP, and fiber. ## **Responsibilities**
#### **Live signal acquisition and streaming**
* Acquire signals via IP, satellite, or fiber
* Stream 24/7 linear channels and live events using a variety of encoders
* Support the video encoding technologies used by the company
* Assist with daily system checks
#### **Monitoring, troubleshooting, and incident management**
* Monitor 24/7 linear channels, systems, and alerts, including UXQA checks as needed
* Mitigate basic issues and carry out L1 troubleshooting
* Escalate issues effectively, and track and report incidents clearly
* Regularly review and report on incident management performance, ensuring tickets are resolved in a timely and effective way
#### **Team oversight and scheduling**
* Oversee and manage the TOC Operators, ensuring effective day-to-day operations
* Maintain schedules for broadcasts and staff
* Maintain rosters for sickness and annual leave to ensure adequate team coverage and compliance with business needs
#### **Procedures, automation, and team development**
* Define and improve procedures and best practices for linear channel and system monitoring
* Define and improve procedures and best practices for signal acquisition via IP, satellite, or fiber
* Drive automation initiatives to streamline recurring tasks, reducing manual effort and errors
* Facilitate cross-training within the team to build flexibility and capability
* Own the onboarding and training of new starters, equipping them with the knowledge and skills to succeed
#### Requirements
This is the experience that will help you hit the ground running.
#### **Required**
* 2+ years' experience in live transmission and/or 24/7 OTT broadcast environments or similar
* 2+ years' experience of B2C and B2B live streaming at scale
* Excellent knowledge of broadcast systems, broadcast IT systems, and their supporting networks, including basic network configuration and troubleshooting
* Hands-on experience with satellite downlinking and fiber acquisition
* Experience with IP formats such as HLS, RTMP, and SRT, and general use of streaming protocols and encoders/transcoders
* Experience analyzing service operations data to support incident management, and identifying service issues, following standard procedure or establishing workarounds on the fly

# Director, Market Growth Strategy, Molecule to Market (Lab Automation)
Remote - United Kingdom
**Our Why At Dotmatics**
At Dotmatics, a Siemens company, we believe science, data, and decision-making must be deeply intertwined for innovation to thrive. Our Portfolio includes Luma, LumaLab Connect, ELN Platform, Graphpad Prism, Geneious, SnapGene, Protein Metrics, OMIQ, FCS Express, LabArchives, NQuery, EasyPanel, SoftGenetics and Virscidian.
**We have a vision for a new Lab of the Future that will change the future of scientific research.**
We have created the world’s most comprehensive digital science platform – best-of-breed software applications already used by more than 2 million scientists, together in a single ecosystem united by a powerful, flexible enterprise data platform. This is not flat data buried away in digital graveyards. This is dynamic, multi-dimensional decision-making.
Scientific enterprises need a new level of effectiveness to achieve tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Illness will not wait. The biosphere will not wait. We are tireless in our vision, because the time for innovation is now.
**Shaping the Future of Science At Dotmatics**
Our global team of more than 800 colleagues are dedicated to supporting our customers in over 180 countries. Together, with our scientific community of users, we accelerate scientific innovation in order to make the world a healthier, cleaner, and safer place to live.
You’ll join a collaborative, global team pushing the boundaries of scientific innovation. Your ideas and efforts will have a tangible impact, accelerating scientific progress and discovery. We offer a dynamic, remote-friendly environment that fosters high integrity and collaboration, empowering you to excel. Dotmatics is a company built by scientists, for scientists. Combined, we are now the world’s largest cloud-based scientific research R&D platform. We need your help to keep growing and pioneering the future.
**We are Science Driven. We are Customer Centric. We are Better Together.**
**What do we need**
We are looking for an experienced market leader, thought leader and SME in Lab Automation and Orchestration. Lab automation is where science meets engineering. Robotics, liquid handlers, instruments, and scheduling software are moving labs from manual work toward automated, data driven, and eventually autonomous operation. While we are supporting fully automated labs, most labs still run as islands. Instruments speak different languages, workflows are hard to change, and the data that comes off the line rarely arrives ready for analysis or AI.
We’re building Luma, a Scientific Intelligence Platform for life sciences and materials science. Lab Orchestration and automation are core to our Molecule to Market story, and they connect directly to the strengths of Siemens in industrial automation. We need someone to own the market strategy for it.
This is a customer and market facing role. You’ll spend real time with lab automation leaders at pharma, biotech, CDMOs, and research institutes across the UK and Europe, hearing what they need and bringing it back to the business. You’ll also support teams around the world across Siemens, including sales, product, services, customer success, and the Siemens Solution Marketing team, so everyone can speak to the lab automation market with confidence and one consistent story. You’ll work with industry thought leaders to shape the conversation on autonomous labs and AI. Your job is to drive software adoption and AI use cases in lab automation. You will shape where we play, who we sell to, how we position, and how we win.
**How you’ll spend your time**
* Customer engagements: meeting automation leaders, scientists, and engineers, joining pursuits, and bringing what you hear back to the business
* Market analysis: sizing segments, tracking competitors and automation vendors, and spotting trends early
* Sales enablement: giving teams across regions the talk tracks, battlecards, demo narratives, and proof points to win
* Solution marketing: partnering with the Siemens Solution Marketing team on content, campaigns, events, and messaging for the lab automation audience
* Thought leadership: working with industry thought leaders, inside and outside Siemens, to shape the conversation on self driving labs and the future of the automated lab
* Adoption and AI use cases: identifying, proving, and spreading the use cases that get labs running on Luma and putting AI to work on automated workflows and data
* Partner and ecosystem engagement: working with instrument makers, robotics providers, and integrators so our joint story is clear to customers
* Cross organization alignment: working across Siemens DISW and DI Automation teams so we show up as one company with one story for the lab automation market
The goal is simple. Drive excellence in how we represent ourselves to lab automation buyers, and turn that into real software adoption.
**What you’ll do**
* Own the market strategy for Luma in lab automation, including workflow orchestration, scheduling, instrument integration, data capture, and autonomous lab concepts
* Define target segments, buyer personas, and priority accounts, including Heads of Lab Automation, Automation Engineers, Discovery Technologies, Research IT, Core Facilities, and Operations leaders
* Build positioning and messaging that speaks to automation engineers, scientists, IT leaders, and executives
* Drive software adoption by working with customers and field teams to find the workflows where Luma delivers value fastest, and by capturing what works so others can repeat it
* Define and prove AI use cases for lab automation, including closed loop experimentation, smarter scheduling, and data prepared for tools like NVIDIA BioNeMo
* Translate automation pain points into clear value, including less integration work, faster workflow changes, better use of instruments, trusted data, and a clear path from automation islands to connected labs
* Partner with the Siemens Solution Marketing team to build content, campaigns, and events for the lab automation market
* Work with industry thought leaders, analysts, and partners to build credibility and bring outside voices into our story
* Create the competitive view against other informatics vendors, scheduling and orchestration tools, automation vendors, and in house builds
* Develop the business case, pricing inputs, and value story with Finance and Sales
* Equip global teams with talk tracks, battlecards, demo narratives, and customer proof points
* Partner with DISW and DI Automation teams to align messaging, joint offers, and customer conversations
* Partner with Product on roadmap priorities based on what automation teams tell us
* Connect lab automation to the bigger Molecule to Market narrative, including ELN, Biologics, and Tech Transfer
* Support strategic pursuits and executive conversations with customers and partners
* Track market trends, including autonomous labs, AI driven discovery, robotics, and data standards, and turn them into action
**We are looking for people who have** 10 or more years in life sciences, lab automation, or scientific technology, with hands on experience in a pharma, biotech, CDMO, research institute, or automation vendor setting. You will bring Strong analytical skills, including sizing markets and building a business case excellent writing and presentation skills. job_title: Senior Quality Manager - Fuel Cell Stack Production
job_description:
About EHG
EH Group (EHG) is a rapidly growing fuel cell power platform delivering onsite power to AI data centers, defense, and industry. Our fuel-agnostic proton exchange membrane (PEM) systems scale from kW-scale units to GW-scale power plants, and we design, manufacture, and deploy them for customers worldwide.
Founded in Switzerland, EHG is now expanding into the United States, fueled by exponential AI data center power demand and a soon-to-be-announced major investment round. This is a defining, high-growth chapter for the company.
The opportunity
We're hiring a Quality Manager to own a single quality system across both of our production streams — our established MW-scale facility in Nyon, Switzerland and our new US operation in Houston, Texas.
You'd be based in Nyon, where our production and process knowledge sits today, and own quality for the US operation as it stands up. The requirement is explicit: quality must be identical at both sites. Same specifications, same control plans, same acceptance criteria, same records. A customer taking delivery of a system should not be able to tell which site built the stack inside it, and our certification and warranty position depends on being able to demonstrate that.
Our customers are data center operators, defense programs, and industrial sites where reliability is the product. In your first year you'd harmonize our quality management system across both entities, establish controls in Houston that match those proven in Nyon as manufacturing technology transfers, build supplier quality alongside Supply Chain for a shared global supply base, and support certification of our systems for both European and US markets.
Location & travel: Nyon-based. Regular travel to Houston is expected as the US operation stands up, along with travel to supplier and partner sites in Europe and the US.
What you'll own
One quality management system across both entities — a common QMS covering Nyon and Houston, including the path to ISO 9001 certification in the US and alignment with what is already established in Switzerland.
Equivalence between sites. A single set of product specifications, control plans, inspection criteria, and acceptance standards, with a defined process for how any change is applied at both sites rather than one.
In-process quality for fuel cell stack production at both locations, including the process controls that matter most in stack assembly — cleanliness and contamination control, leak testing, torque and compression control, and alignment.
Supplier quality for a shared global supply base, working with Supply Chain on qualification, audits, first article inspection, part submission, and ongoing performance, with one qualification standard regardless of which site a supplier serves.
Quality oversight of contract manufacturing and assembly partners building balance of plant and containerized systems on our behalf in both regions — audits, quality agreements, source inspection, and acceptance criteria.
Nonconformance and corrective action across both sites, including NCR and CAPA processes and structured problem solving, with findings at one site systematically applied at the other.
Traceability and product records — a common lot genealogy model from raw material through stack serial to delivered system, and the test and inspection data that supports warranty, certification, and customer acceptance, held consistently across both entities.
Certification across regions, working with external certification partners on the standards applicable to stationary hydrogen power systems in Europe and the US, authority having jurisdiction approvals, and marine classification where relevant.
Quality culture on both floors, including operator training, work instruction discipline, and establishing the habits in Houston that are already proven in Nyon, as US headcount grows quickly.
Building the US quality capability, defining what needs to sit on the ground in Houston versus what is run centrally from Nyon, and recruiting into it as volumes grow.
What we're looking for
Core experience
Owning quality across more than one manufacturing site, ideally in more than one country, with a demonstrated ability to hold two sites to genuinely the same standard from a distance.
Establishing or substantially rebuilding a quality function, including authoring a quality management system rather than administering an existing one.
Hands-on in-process and incoming quality in a production setting, with real familiarity with control plans, inspection methods, measurement systems, and process capability.
Supplier quality experience, including auditing suppliers and holding them to standard.
Structured problem solving and root cause analysis, with a track record of permanently closing out recurring defects.
Working knowledge of product certification processes and the evidence they require, ideally in energy, power equipment, or another regulated product category. Exposure to both European and US regimes is a strong advantage.
The judgment to know which controls are essential at low volume and which can wait, and the confidence to hold a quality position under schedule pressure.
Comfort working across time zones and influencing a site you are not physically based at, including building quality capability remotely.
Especially compelling
Fuel cell, battery cell, or similar electrochemical assembly experience.
Experience with cleanliness-critical or contamination-sensitive assembly processes.
Experience supporting a technology transfer between sites or countries, and establishing quality at the receiving end.
Experience qualifying and auditing contract manufacturers or system integrators.
Startup or scale-up experience as an early hire during hyper-growth.
Experience working between Europe and the US, and with US codes and certification practice in particular. French is useful but not required.
What we offer
Competitive compensation and meaningful equity, calibrated to the market and discussed directly with you.
Relocation support to Nyon, Switzerland.
The opportunity to build EHG's global quality function during a defining phase of hyper-growth.
Note: Swiss work authorization or eligibility is required for this role, along with the ability to travel to the United States.

## Offer Description
Photocatalysis offers a powerful route to use light energy to drive chemical transformations under mild conditions, potentially replacing energy-intensive thermal processes and enabling more sustainable pathways to fuels and value-added chemicals. This PhD project will develop photocatalysts for selective chemical transformations of renewable and abundant carbon-containing feedstocks using solar irradiation or tailored artificial light sources.
The project will focus on semiconductor photocatalysts, including metal chalcogenides, perovskites, organic semiconductors and heterostructured materials, combined with cocatalysts and interfacial engineering strategies to control charge separation and surface reactivity. A central objective will be to understand how photogenerated electrons, holes and radical intermediates can be directed towards desired chemical pathways while suppressing competing reactions. Particular attention will be given to controlling reaction selectivity through catalyst composition, electronic structure, interfaces and reaction conditions. The student will combine materials synthesis, photocatalytic testing, spectroscopy, microscopy and photoelectrochemical characterisation with mechanistic studies of reaction intermediates.
Target reactions may include C–C bond-forming transformations, selective oxidation and reduction reactions, and the upgrading of small oxygenates or biomass-derived molecules into higher-value chemicals. The influence of irradiation wavelength, intensity and reactor configuration will also be investigated, enabling the development of photocatalytic processes compatible with both intermittent solar irradiation and continuous LED operation. The ultimate goal is to establish design principles for efficient and selective photocatalytic chemical synthesis, linking catalyst properties, light delivery and reaction pathways to routes that can ultimately be translated towards scalable chemical production.
This scholarship is open to all applicants regardless of their fee status. It covers both tuition fees and a tax-free contribution to maintenance costs of £25,000 per annum for 42 months.
The Department of Chemical Engineering at Imperial College London offers an advanced 3-4-year research degree that provides in-depth specialist training and knowledge in a topical area pertaining to Chemical Engineering and related Engineering and Science disciplines. The Department has state-of-the-art experimental and computational facilities and is the home of the Automated high-throughput platform suite, the Sargent Centre for Process Systems Engineering and the Sustainable Futures Lab.
The Department holds a Silver Athena Swan award for good practice in supporting academic women and gender equality renewed in 2024. This award recognises the good practices already in place for supporting women at all stages as well as our commitment to removing barriers to equal progress and achievement.

# Our Vision & Products
***🚀 EverAI — Building the Future of AI Companionship***
*One of the Top 15 Largest & Fastest-Growing AI Companies in the World*

# Your Role
We are looking for a Trust & Safety Product Manager to own the product and technical delivery of our compliance and safety initiatives across our platforms.
You will turn safety requirements into effective product features, moderation capabilities, third-party integrations, and measurable improvements. Working closely with Compliance, Engineering, AI/ML, Product, and Customer Support, you will help us identify risks earlier, build safeguards into new features, and continuously improve how our safety systems perform.
This is a newly created role within our Product team, working directly with our **CTO, Michael Monin** and our **Legal & Safety Lead, Maxwelle Sokol**. You will have significant ownership from the outset and the opportunity to shape how the safety product function develops as the company continues to grow.
Our platform serves adults and permits lawful adult content. We are looking for someone who can navigate sensitive, context-dependent issues thoughtfully, protecting users and enforcing clear boundaries without unnecessarily restricting legitimate expression.
Here’s what you can expect:
## **Key Responsibilities**
* **Safety & legal product strategy and delivery.** Translate safety policies, legal requirements (e.g., in online safety and AI-specific laws such as the EU AI Act), incident findings, and user feedback into clear product requirements, acceptance criteria, and engineering work. Drive initiatives from problem definition through implementation, testing, launch, and ongoing improvement.
* **Internally developed moderation technologies**. Own the product side of improvements to our in-house moderation systems, including our proprietary LLM technology EverGuard. Partner with Engineering and AI/ML teams on, e.g., detection capabilities, moderation rules and thresholds, and appropriate interventions across user inputs and AI-generated outputs.
* **Third-party safety partnerships and integrations**. Lead the technical and product lifecycle of third-party safety partnerships, from identifying needs and evaluating providers to implementation, testing, rollout, and ongoing performance management.
* **Safety dashboards, monitoring, and quality assurance**. Establish dashboards and a recurring QA that help us proactively identify emerging issues, prevent harmful content, and ensure that our T&S measures are working as intended.
* **Red teaming and adversarial testing**. Own our testing for how moderation systems and product safeguards respond to deliberate misuse and difficult edge cases. Track findings through remediation, retesting, and closure—not just delivery of a report.
* **Trust and safety reviews for new features**. Establish and run a dedicated T&S review for new features, with proportionate reviews for material changes to existing features, models, and integrations. Engage early in product design to identify foreseeable misuse, affected users, and appropriate safeguards.
* **Incident follow-through and continuous improvement**. Coordinate the product and engineering response to significant safety issues, working with colleagues responsible for incident management, policy, and user support.
Learn more about our Trust & Safety infrastructure in our Trust & Safety Hub.
# Your Qualifications
* **Data-driven product decisions that align with legal/ethical standards:** You can name the metrics you want to influence, explain why it matters, and say whether your work actually moved them. You’ve run A/B tests, product experiments, data deep-dives, or lightweight user research and used the findings to shape what was built next. You can assess risks associated with user-generated content, transactions, and interactions, and translate these into policies that align with legal and ethical standards, trackers/dashboards, and strategic planning;
* **Content moderation and AI guardrails**: You understand how product realities and safety requirements interact on a tech platform; you explore strategies for efficient and scalable content moderation, including automation, machine learning, human review and user reporting.
* **Legal/safety work experience**: You have worked closely with trust and safety and compliance requirements and understand how to translate and implement these for a consumer-facing product;
* **Collaborative mindset and communication**: You work cross-functionally with engineering, legal, operations, and customer support teams — these are your partners and support system, not your adversaries or a box to be checked. You ask the right questions, challenge assumptions constructively, and are fully fluent and comfortable in English;
* **AI fluency:** You are completely comfortable working with and leveraging AI tools. You actively seek out and experiment with new tools and techniques without waiting for a project or manager to require them;
* **You are point person for third-party partnerships:** You proactively test and can autonomously handle discussions with third-party tools and integrations that affect our compliance and safety posture;
* **You take ownership and move without waiting for certainty:** Comfortable with ambiguity, you create clarity by investigating, building, testing, and learning rather than waiting for a complete brief. You balance execution against planning, address blockers early, and take responsibility for the outcome rather than waiting to be told what to do, caring more about reaching the right result than following a fixed process;
* **You are comfortable with the product category:** you are fully comfortable building products based on uncensored models and content;
### Bonus points
* You have previous legal/compliance education
* Professional experience or interest in AI
* Experience with consumer-facing features, particularly in the entertainment or gaming industry
## **Soft Skills**
🗣 Strong communication & collaborative skills (perfectly fluent in English)
🎯 Goal-oriented, ownership and commitment
⚡️ Doer mindset - we are moving fast and need people who can balance execution, planning, and strategy
🧢 Humble - willing to learn, open to feedback
🍭 #NSFW - Comfortable reviewing and discussing uncensored AI-generated content and NSFW material
***We believe strongly that information can be learned, but effort and motivation cannot. If this role appeals to you but you don’t have hands-on experience in all the fields listed in this job description, apply anyway and tell us why you’d be a good fit!***

📈 **Exponential Growth**: From 50M users in 2 years, to 100M next — and 500M beyond
🚀 **Track Record of Category-Creating Innovation**: We consistently launch **world-first AI applications** — setting the pace, not following it

We’re a fully remote group of **A-players from Tier 1 tech**, led by an exec team who’ve **launched, scaled, and exited multiple companies**. We move fast, and care deeply about what we build — and who we build it with.

Working closely with the Founder and Sales Lead, you will create new sales opportunities by researching target markets, identifying relevant companies and decision-makers, and starting thoughtful commercial conversations across phone, email, LinkedIn and other outbound channels.
This is not a high-volume, script-led position built around sending identical messages. You will be expected to understand each market, personalise your approach and use commercial judgement to work out which organisations matter, who to contact and how best to engage them.
Your initial focus will be building qualified pipeline and booking high-quality meetings. As your product knowledge develops, you will have the opportunity to support demonstrations, engage with existing customers and progress towards owning more of the sales process. As part of a small startup team, you will also be encouraged to contribute beyond your core responsibilities, including marketing content, customer support and data-led projects.

* Research and identify companies that match defined target customer profiles.
* Build and prioritise target account lists using the company’s own platform and modern go-to-market tools.
* Identify relevant decision-makers, champions and commercial stakeholders within target organisations.
* Generate outbound opportunities through cold calling, email, LinkedIn and other appropriate channels.
* Create thoughtful, personalised outreach rather than relying on blanket messaging.
* Understand prospective customers’ current workflows, priorities and commercial challenges.
* Qualify opportunities and book high-quality meetings for the wider sales team.
* Follow up consistently and professionally, balancing tenacity with an intelligent, considered approach.
* Experiment with messaging, audiences and routes to market, sharing insight with sales, marketing and product colleagues.
* Maintain accurate, organised and useful CRM records and pipeline activity.
* Support occasional customer queries and data projects once fully trained on the platform.
* Contribute to LinkedIn content and wider go-to-market growth activity.

We are looking for a hardworking, resilient and entrepreneurial salesperson who wants to build a long-term career in technology sales. You will be comfortable initiating conversations with people you have never met, but equally capable of listening for signals, adapting your approach and pushing conversations forward professionally. You will be naturally curious about how businesses operate and why they buy. The right person will enjoy learning new technology, testing different approaches and working in an environment where they can take ownership, wear multiple hats and make a visible contribution to the company’s growth.

* 1-2 years’ experience in outbound sales, business development, account management or another commercially focused role.
* Experience generating opportunities through cold calling, email, LinkedIn or wider outbound activity.
* Confidence speaking with new prospects and the resilience to manage rejection constructively.
* Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to personalise outreach effectively.
* Commercial curiosity and a genuine interest in understanding different businesses, markets and buying drivers.
* A technology-led mindset and the ability to learn new platforms quickly.
* Familiarity with modern go-to-market tools such as CRMs, prospecting platforms, sequencing tools, enrichment software or LinkedIn Sales Navigator.
* Strong organisation and attention to detail, including the ability to maintain accurate CRM and pipeline data.
* A self-motivated, hardworking and tenacious approach, with the judgement to balance persistence and professionalism.
* The confidence to work effectively in a fast-moving startup environment where priorities may evolve.

# Engineering Manager – Commercial Technology
London
## **About Us**
The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.
At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Together, we help audiences stay better informed and deepen their understanding of the world around them.

With a supportive culture, entrepreneurial spirit and opportunities at every turn, there are no limits to where your FT career can take you.
*Build a newsworthy career at the FT.*
## **Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion**
We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.
## **About you**
You are an experienced engineering leader with a strong software engineering background and a track record of leading teams responsible for business-critical products and platforms.
You combine strong people leadership with credible technical judgement. You are comfortable setting direction, helping teams make complex engineering decisions and remaining close enough to the technology to understand the health, risks and opportunities within the platforms you own.
You understand that engineering leadership is about more than delivery. You think about the long-term health of technology: architecture, reliability, security, scalability, developer experience, operational performance and the ability of teams to evolve their systems sustainably.
You are comfortable working closely with Product and business stakeholders, translating priorities into engineering plans and making thoughtful trade-offs between new capabilities, technical investment and operational needs.
You are also motivated by developing people and teams. You create clear ownership, coach engineers, build capability and create an environment where people can challenge, learn and take increasing responsibility.
## **About the team**
Commercial Technology is part of the Internal Products group within FT Product & Technology. We are a multidisciplinary group of Engineers, Product Managers and Business Analysts responsible for building and operating the technology platforms that support the FT’s commercial capabilities across Marketing, Sales, Service and Commercial Data.
We are undertaking a significant evolution of our commercial technology landscape, bringing these capabilities together around a more connected Salesforce platform and establishing a strong foundation for how our commercial teams engage with customers and use data.
In **Marketing & Commercial Dat**a, we are evolving our marketing technology landscape towards Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next and Data 360, while continuing to operate and transition from established platforms including Bloomreach, Marketo and Legacy Salesforce Marketing Cloud products for B2B & B2C marketing.
In **Sales & Service**, we are consolidating a number of Salesforce CRM orgs with their associated processes and procedures into a leaner Commercial Technology estate, utilising data available to us via Data 360, into a setup that aligns with the FT’s future commercial capabilities and setup. In **Commercial Platform**, we are establishing a centre of excellence at the heart of the commercial workflow, tasked with ensuring the security, health and viability of our day-to-day commercial operation and providing a primary support route for our business users The Engineering Manager will lead one of the engineering teams within Commercial Technology, working closely with Product, Senior Engineers, other Engineering Managers and the wider Commercial Technology leadership team.
## **What you’ll work on**
As **Engineering Manager** within Commercial Technology, you will lead the engineering team responsible for the delivery, performance and continuous evolution of the FT’s **Marketing & Commercial Data** capability. You will be accountable for ensuring the engineering team is effectively organised, supported and resourced to deliver business outcomes. This includes leading delivery and planning, managing engineering capacity and priorities, building strong relationships with Product, Programme and business stakeholders, and ensuring risks, dependencies and resource constraints are understood and actively managed.
You will be leading a team through a significant transformation of the FT's commercial technology landscape, balancing the delivery of new capabilities with the operational health of existing platforms, the development of engineering capability and the longer-term evolution of the Commercial Technology estate.
You will remain close to the technology and provide credible engineering leadership. You will support technical decision-making, challenge approaches where appropriate and ensure the team understands the architecture, risks and operational health of the systems it owns.
You will also work with Principal Engineers and other senior technical leaders on decisions that extend beyond your team's boundaries, ensuring local engineering decisions contribute to a coherent and sustainable Commercial Technology landscape.
You will report to the Principal Engineer for the Commercial Technology domain.
## **Your responsibilities will include**
### **Engineering Delivery & Planning**
* Own engineering delivery across the Marketing & Commercial Data capability, ensuring agreed business outcomes are delivered effectively and sustainably.
* Work with Product, Programme, the Technical Lead and wider Commercial Technology leadership to shape priorities, roadmaps and achievable delivery plans.
* Own the allocation of engineering capacity, balancing delivery commitments with operational needs, technical improvement, team capacity and longer-term capability development.
* Identify and actively manage delivery risks, dependencies, resource constraints and capability gaps, escalating where necessary.
* Continuously improve engineering processes, development workflows, documentation and ways of working.
**People Leadership & Team Health**
* Leading, supporting and developing engineers, admins and specialists across Marketing Technology and Commercial Data through regular 1:1s, coaching, feedback and career development.
* Setting clear expectations for individual and team performance
* Create an inclusive, supportive and psychologically safe environment, building a strong engineering culture based on ownership, collaboration, continuous learning and shared accountability.
* Manage team capacity and sustainable workloads, supporting the wellbeing, effectiveness and long-term development of the team.
* Identify skills and capability gaps and work with engineers and wider engineering leadership to develop the capabilities required for our future platform.
* Lead recruitment, onboarding and organisational change within the capability, ensuring engineers are supported through changes to technology, roles and ways of working.
### **Technical Leadership & Collaboration**
* Partner closely with the Technical Lead – Marketing & Commercial Data, Together you will provide the complementary people, delivery and technical leadership required to operate and evolve our Marketing & Commercial Data capability successfully.
* Own the organisational conditions required to execute the technical strategy, ensuring teams have the skills, capacity and ways of working required to deliver it successfully.
* Contribute to technical discussions and decisions while maintaining clear accountability with the Technical Lead for technical direction, architecture, engineering standards and solution design.
* Build strong relationships with Product, Programme, business stakeholders and other technology teams, providing clear visibility of delivery, capacity, operational health, risks and dependencies.
* Work closely with Engineering Managers and Technical Leads across Commercial Technology to coordinate shared priorities, dependencies and engineering practices.
* Work effectively with external technology partners and delivery vendors where required, ensuring they integrate successfully with FT engineering teams and delivery practices.
* Represent the needs, constraints and capabilities of the engineering team in programme, planning and stakeholder discussions.
### **Operational Readiness & Engineering Excellence**
* Be accountable for ensuring Marketing & Commercial Data capabilities are operationally ready, supportable and sustainable throughout their lifecycle.
* Ensure operational requirements are built into delivery, including observability, monitoring, resilience, documentation, support models, knowledge transfer and clear ownership.
* Work closely with the Commercial Platform team to ensure new and changed capabilities can be effectively supported within the wider Commercial Technology operating model.
* Ensure the team remains engaged in the ongoing health of the capabilities it owns, providing specialist domain or engineering expertise when required.
* Lead the Marketing & Commercial Data team's response to incidents affecting capabilities it owns, working within the Commercial Technology incident-management model led by Commercial Platform.
* Ensure operational health, capability risks, technical debt and engineering improvements are visible and prioritised alongside product and programme delivery.
* Ensure learning from incidents, operational issues and business-user feedback is incorporated into future delivery and continuous improvement.

* Full-time
* Workplace type: On-site
## Company Description
**About FRP**
At FRP, we are a leading national business advisory firm based in the UK. With over 950 team members, including more than 100 partners, we specialise in **Corporate Finance, Debt Advisory, Forensic Services, Financial Advisory, Restructuring Advisory, and Real Estate Advisory**. Operating from 35 offices across the UK, Isle of Man and Cyprus, we are dedicated to helping clients navigate complex and difficult situations to create, preserve, and recover value.
Our approach is known for being honest, clear, and considered. We provide strategic solutions that cater to a broad range of businesses, from multinational organisations to small enterprises. Our commitment is to deliver expert advice and support, ensuring our clients can make informed decisions and achieve their goals.
## Job Description
The Service Desk Analyst acts as the first point of contact for all IT-related incidents and service requests within FRP Advisory. This role is critical in ensuring smooth technology operations across a fast-paced professional services environment. You will deliver timely, effective resolutions and exceptional customer service to maintain high user satisfaction and support FRP’s commitment to operational excellence.
**Location:** Fully on-site, flexible across FRP Advisory offices (Chelmsford, Brentwood, London, and other UK sites)
**Reports To:** Service Desk Manager
**Working Hours**
Coverage between 08:00 and 18:00, with staggered shifts to ensure early and late support as required.
**Key responsibilities:**
* Serve as the initial contact for IT support via phone, email, or ticketing system.
* Log, categorize, and prioritize incidents and service requests using the ITSM platform.
* Diagnose and resolve technical issues related to hardware, software, and network connectivity.
* Escalate complex issues to second-line support or specialist teams, ensuring thorough documentation.
* Provide guidance and support for core business applications (e.g., Microsoft 365, collaboration tools, and FRP-specific systems).
* Maintain accurate records of all interactions and resolutions in line with compliance standards.
* Follow ITIL-aligned best practices for incident, problem, and request management.
* Assist in creating and maintaining knowledge base articles to support self-service and team efficiency.
* Ensure adherence to FRP’s security policies and regulatory requirements.
* Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives within the Service Desk function.
## Qualifications
**Essential:**
* Strong customer service and communication skills, with a professional and client-focused approach.
* Solid understanding of Windows OS, Microsoft 365, and common business applications.
* Ability to troubleshoot hardware and software issues effectively.
* Familiarity with ITSM tools (e.g., ServiceNow, Remedy).
**Desirable:**
* ITIL Foundation certification.
* Previous experience in a Service Desk or IT support role within a professional services or financial environment.
**Key Competencies**
* Analytical thinking and problem-solving skills.
* Ability to work under pressure and manage multiple priorities in a deadline-driven environment.
* Collaborative team player with a proactive attitude.
* Strong attention to detail and documentation accuracy.
* Flexibility and adaptability to changing business needs.
## Additional Information
**Our Values**
* **Straightforward**: We provide clear, no-nonsense advice
* **Confident**: Our guidance is backed by expertise and evidence
* **Pragmatic**: We focus on practical solutions and tangible outcomes
* **Real**: We are professional yet approachable, understanding the challenges our clients face
**Our Commitment to You and the Environment**
At FRP, sustainability is integral to our strategy and operations. Our sustainability depends on building and maintaining meaningful, long-term relationships with all our stakeholders – including our employees, clients, and local communities – while also reducing our impact on the natural environment.
We are always striving to improve in all areas – whether it’s our people, our clients, our planet or our governance. Our ongoing success as a business depends on our sustainability and agility in a changing and challenging global landscape.
We are committed to fostering an inclusive, equitable, and diverse culture for our people. We maintain an Equal Opportunities Policy, ensuring that recruitment and employment decisions are based solely on the skills and experience required for our professional services — regardless of ethnicity, race, sexual orientation, disability, or any other protected characteristic. We believe every individual should have the opportunity to thrive.
Our learning and development programmes enable us to invest in growing our employees’ careers. We aim to empower our team members to each achieve their potential.
We are committed to growing long-term relationships with our clients and supporting them in achieving their objectives. We understand that our clients’ sustainability and success lead to our sustainability and success. We are emotionally invested in our clients right from the beginning.
