# Principal Technical Project Manager (we have office locations in Cambridge, Leeds & London)
London, England
Apply now
## Company Description
Genomics England is a global leader in enabling genomic medicine and research, focused on creating a world where everyone benefits from genomic healthcare. Building on the 100,000 Genomes Project, we support the NHS’s world-first national whole genome sequencing service and run the growing National Genomic Research Library, alongside delivering numerous major genomics initiatives. By connecting research and clinical care at national scale, we enable immediate healthcare benefits and advances for the future.
Our mission is to provide the evidence and digital systems so that by 2035 genomics could play a role in up to half of all healthcare interactions, whilst securing the UK’s position as the best place to discover, prove and benefit from genomic innovations.
We are accelerating our impact and working with patients, doctors, scientists, government and industry to improve genomic testing, and help researchers access the health data and technology they need to make new medical discoveries and create more effective, targeted medicines for everybody.
Behind the Healthcare and Research outcomes, Genomics England delivers through designing, developing and operating complex healthcare software systems.
We're on the cusp of big changes with the real prospect of genomics becoming the fabric of everyday healthcare through the lifetime – from birth to old age.
## Job Description
We are seeking a Principal Technical Project Manager to support our Engineering Chapter in driving improvements to tooling, platforms and ways of working within the Software Delivery Lifecycle (SDLC) and live operations across the service and company.
In this position you will work closely with the Director of Engineering and core Engineering Chapter teams: Developer Platform, Test Enablement and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE).
You will play a vital role in ensuring that the objectives of those teams (and the initiatives which support them) are clearly identified and prioritised with the product managers and delivered effectively. You will engage with stakeholders across the business, ensuring that central Engineering Chapter work aligns with business needs, is communicated effectively and that outcomes are aligned with expectations.
This principal role requires someone with strong understanding of modern SDLC practices, excellent stakeholder engagement skills, who can bring a collaborative and agile approach to driving delivery across multiple strands of work.
Candidates should be highly experienced in working in an ambiguous environment, learning new principles and technologies to be able to work effectively with teams and engage credibly with the wider organisation. They should also be comfortable with balancing between meeting delivery commitments and being responsive to emerging organisational needs and priorities.
**Everyday responsibilities include:**
* Own the end-to-end delivery of key technical workstreams within a programme, taking accountability for the successful completion of critical delivery outcomes.
* Lead the management of OKRs and initiatives across Engineering Chapter teams, including the capture, definition, tracking and reporting of objectives and key results.
* Partner with Product Managers and Service Owners to validate requirements and ensure delivery is aligned to agreed timelines, budgets and OKRs.
* Establish and maintain delivery plans, monitoring progress against roadmaps and communicating or escalating where delivery moves away from agreed commitments.
* Ensure delivery progress is accurately reflected in operational tools, including Monday.com, to support effective planning, visibility and reporting.
* Identify, manage and regularly review risks, actions, issues and dependencies, working collaboratively with teams to resolve challenges and maintain delivery momentum.
* Prepare clear status updates and contribute to programme board reports and governance forums, ensuring progress, risks and decisions are communicated effectively.
* Establish and use appropriate decision-making structures, helping teams make timely, well-informed decisions where uncertainty needs to be resolved.
* Implement effective governance across delivery, cybersecurity, data quality, data protection, IT requirements, accreditations and relevant internal and external standards.
* Build trusted relationships with internal and external stakeholders, adapting communication to reflect different commercial, technical and business considerations.
* Ensure contributors are clear on what needs to be delivered, by when, and that responsible stakeholders remain informed throughout the delivery lifecycle.
* Engage with technical and operational governance groups, including the Engineering Steering Group, to shape, review and ratify key engineering decisions where appropriate.
* Lead, motivate and support contributors to delivery, including in matrix environments where there is no direct line management authority.
* Promote service-oriented thinking across Engineering Chapter teams, helping teams remain focused on user needs, service outcomes and measurable impact.
* Support supplier engagement and procurement activity in line with Genomics England governance, including supplier frameworks and relevant approval routes.
* Contribute to business cases, budget planning and spend monitoring, ensuring items and services are approved, budgeted for and managed through appropriate governance.
* Line manage and support Delivery Chapter colleagues, including pastoral support, performance reviews, development planning, training and performance management where required.
* Contribute as a senior member of the Delivery Chapter, supporting best practice, continuous improvement and active participation in Chapter meetings and away days.
## Qualifications
**Skills and experience for success:**
* Proven track record of project and programme delivery from initiation to business as usual.
* Agile and adaptive project, risk, and issue management with a proactive and outcome-focused approach.
* Strong communication skills, engaging effectively with both technical and non-technical audiences.
* Commercial awareness to support informed decision-making.
* Ability to work in a highly regulated environment with increasing compliance needs.
* Stakeholder management, building trusted relationships across teams and leadership levels.
* Confident decision-making with sound judgement on escalation and risk management.
* Ability to translate complex technical concepts into clear, accessible language for non-technical stakeholders.
* Collaborative approach to problem-solving, balancing delivery priorities with business needs.
* Track record of line management directly or in a matrix organisation.
**Awareness of the following technologies and concepts:**
* The principles and benefits of Internal Developer Platforms and Platform Engineering.
* Quality Assurance best-practices e.g. shift-left, contract-testing and Behaviour-Driven Development (BDD).
* Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) principles and practices.
* Measures of engineering maturity e.g. Developer Experience (DevEx) and DORA.
* Modern CI/CD platforms e.g. GitLab (preferred), GitHub and awareness of the concepts and benefits of Continuous Delivery.
* Observability / monitoring platforms e.g. DataDog (preferred) or New Relic.
* AWS services e.g. EC2, ECS/Fargate, S3, Lambda, RDS, VPC and management tools including AWS Organisations, Identity Center, Inspector and Security Hub.
* Infrastructure-as-code tools e.g. Terraform (preferred) or CloudFormation.
## Additional Information
**Salary from: £77,000**
**Closing date for applications - Thursday 29th October at midnight.**
Being an integral part of such a meaningful mission is extremely rewarding in itself, but in order to support our people, we’re continually improving our benefits package. We pride ourselves on investing in our people and supporting them to achieve their career goals, as well as offering a benefits package including:
* **Generous Leave:** 30 days’ holiday plus bank holidays, additional leave for long service, and the option to apply for up to 30 days of remote working abroad annually (approval required).
* **Family-Friendly:** Blended working arrangements, flexible working, enhanced maternity, paternity and shared parental leave benefits.
* **Pension & Financial:** Defined contribution pension (Genomics England double-matches up to 10%, however you can contribute more if you wish), Life Assurance (3x salary), an Electric Vehicle salary sacrifice scheme and a Give As You Earn scheme.
* **Learning & Development:** Individual learning budgets, support for training and certifications, and reimbursement for one annual professional subscription (approval required).
* **Recognition & Rewards:** Employee recognition programme and referral scheme.
* **Health & Wellbeing:** Subsidised gym membership, a free Headspace account, and access to an Employee Assistance Programme, eye tests, flu jabs.
**Equal opportunities and our commitment to a diverse and inclusive workplace**
Genomics England is actively committed to providing and supporting an inclusive environment that promotes equity, diversity and inclusion best practice both within our community and in any other area where we have influence. We are proud of our diverse community where everyone can come to work and feel welcomed and treated with respect regardless of any disability, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, religion, sexual orientation, or social background.
Genomics England’s policies of non-discrimination and equity and will be applied fairly to all people, regardless of age, disability, gender identity or reassignment, marital or civil partnership status, being pregnant or recently becoming a parent, race, religion or beliefs, sex or sexual orientation, length of service, whether full or part-time or employed under a permanent or a fixed-term contract or any other relevant factor.
Genomics England does not tolerate any form of discrimination, harassment, victimisation or bullying at work. Such behaviour undermines our mission and core values and diminishes the dignity, respect and integrity of all parties. Our People policies outline our commitment to inclusivity.
We aim to remove barriers in our recruitment processes and to be flexible with our interview processes. Should you require any adjustments that may help you to fully participate in the recruitment process, we encourage you to discuss this with us.
**Culture**
We have four key behaviours that represent what we would like Genomics England to feel like and the culture we want to encourage, in order for us to achieve our mission. These behaviours help us all work well together, deliver on our outcomes, celebrate our successes and share feedback with each other. You can read about these and other aspects of our culture here Culture | Genomics England
**Blended working model**
Genomics England operates a blended working model as we know our people appreciate the flexibility that hybrid working can bring. We expect most people to come into the office a minimum of 2 times each month. However, this will vary according to role and will be agreed with your team leader. There is no expectation that people will return to the office full time unless they want to, however, some of our roles require full time on site attendance e.g., lab teams, reception team.
Our teams and squads have, and will continue to reflect on what works best for them to work together successfully and have the freedom to design working patterns to suit, beyond the minimum. Our office locations are: Canary Wharf, Cambridge and Leeds.
**Onboarding background checks**
As part of our recruitment process, all successful candidates are subject to a Standard Disclosure and Barring Service (DBS) check. We therefore require applicants to disclose any previous offences at point of application, as some unspent convictions may mean we are unable to proceed with your application due to the nature of our work in healthcare.

The Training Facilitator is a field-based role within the Quality and Governance Directorate, responsible for delivering mandatory and practice development training to care and support staff across a designated group of HC-One homes. Reporting to the Head of Training and Practice Development, the postholder plays a vital role in ensuring that every member of staff across their allocated homes has the knowledge, skills, and competence to deliver safe, high-quality, and person-centred care — and that all mandatory training obligations are met consistently and on time. This is a practical, people-focused role for an experienced care professional who is passionate about sharing their knowledge, developing others, and making a direct contribution to the quality of care that residents receive. The Training Facilitator delivers training in homes across their area using a mix of face-to-face classroom sessions, practical skills demonstrations, and on-the-job coaching, working closely with Home Managers to ensure training is relevant, well-attended, and embedded in day-to-day practice. Main Activities Duties and Responsibilities Mandatory and Statutory Training Delivery • Deliver the full range of mandatory and statutory training to care and support staff across allocated homes, in line with the Group’s mandatory training framework and the requirements of CQC (England), CIW (Wales), and Care Inspectorate (Scotland) as applicable. • Deliver training across all mandatory topics including — but not limited to — moving and handling, fire safety, safeguarding adults, infection prevention and control, health and safety, food hygiene, medication awareness, basic life support, and DoLS/MCA awareness, using HC-One’s approved materials and session plans. • Ensure training sessions are well-planned, well-resourced, and delivered to a consistently high standard, adapting style and approach to meet the learning needs of a diverse adult care workforce including staff for whom English is not a first language. • Maintain accurate attendance and completion records for all training sessions delivered, ensuring records are promptly entered into the Group’s learning management system (LMS) and that Home Managers have visibility of their team’s training compliance status. • Monitor mandatory training compliance within allocated homes, proactively identifying gaps, working with Home Managers to schedule outstanding training, and escalating persistent non-compliance to the Head of Training and Practice Development. Practice Development and Skills Training • Deliver targeted practice development training within homes in response to needs identified by the Head of Training and Practice Development, Quality Improvement Leads, quality colleagues or Home Managers, covering clinical and care topics including care planning, pressure care and wound management, nutrition and hydration, dementia awareness, end of life care, falls prevention, and continence care. • Deliver practical skills sessions within homes, including moving and handling competency assessments, basic life support refreshers, and other skills-based programmes that require hands-on demonstration and supervised practice rather than classroom learning alone. • Support the completion and review of role-specific competency assessments, working with Home Managers and senior colleagues to ensure staff are observed in practice, assessed against agreed standards, and provided with clear feedback and follow-up support where further development is required. • Provide on-the-job coaching to care staff during home visits where training needs or practice concerns have been identified, working alongside individuals to demonstrate correct technique, give constructive feedback, and build confidence and competence in a supportive way. • Support the induction of new starters within allocated homes, delivering elements of the Group-wide induction programme and working with Home Managers to ensure new employees receive a warm, well-structured, and compliant introduction to their role and to HC-One’s values and care standards. HC-One Job Description V2.0
Training Needs Identification and Home Support • Build effective working relationships with Home Managers across allocated homes, developing a good understanding of each home’s team, training history, and current practice development priorities. • Work with Home Managers to identify training needs within their teams, including gaps highlighted by supervision, competency assessments, incident reviews, complaints, or feedback from Quality Improvement Leads, and plan training activity accordingly. • Provide Home Managers with practical guidance on how to identify and address training needs within their teams between formal training sessions, supporting them to build a culture of continuous learning and development within the home. • Attend or contribute to team meetings, supervisions, and practice development discussions within homes where this would support the embedding of learning or the identification of emerging training priorities. Training Delivery Quality and Evaluation • Collect and review delegate feedback after every training session, using evaluation data to continuously improve delivery approach, session content, and the learning experience for participants. • Assess delegate learning at the end of training sessions where required, using knowledge checks, skills assessments, or competency observations to confirm that learning objectives have been met and that any individuals requiring additional support are identified and followed up. • Conduct follow-up observations of practice in homes after training sessions where appropriate, checking that learning has been transferred into day-to-day working practice and that improvements are being sustained. • Report evaluation findings, attendance data, and any concerns about training uptake or practice embedding to the Head of Training and Practice Development, contributing to the team’s continuous improvement of the training programme. Training Materials and Resource Management • Use HC-One’s approved training materials, session plans, and resources consistently and accurately, maintaining the integrity and quality of the Group’s training programmes across all homes in the designated area. • Keep training equipment — including moving and handling aids, first aid manikins, and other practical training resources — in good working order, reporting any defects or replacement needs to the Head of Training and Practice Development promptly. • Suggest improvements to training materials, session plans, or resources based on practical delivery experience, sharing feedback with the Head of Training and Practice Development to support continuous improvement of the curriculum. • Stay current with changes to mandatory training requirements, clinical best practice, regulatory guidance, and sector developments relevant to the training topics delivered, seeking support and update training from the Head of Training and Practice Development as needed.E-Learning and Blended Learning Support • Support staff within allocated homes to access and complete mandatory e-learning modules through the Group’s learning management system, providing practical assistance to employees who are less confident with technology and ensuring e-learning completion is integrated with face-to-face training activity. • Work with Home Managers to ensure e-learning is embedded within rotas and working patterns, so that online training is treated as a scheduled and priority activity rather than an ad hoc addition to the working day. • Liaise with the Head of Training and Practice Development regarding any technical issues affecting elearning access or completion within allocated homes, ensuring these are escalated and resolved promptly to prevent gaps in compliance. Reporting & Team Contribution • Provide regular updates to the Head of Training and Practice Development on training delivery activity, mandatory compliance status, and any emerging training needs or concerns across allocated homes. • Contribute actively to Training team meetings, sharing delivery experiences, raising questions about training content or approach, and supporting a collaborative and reflective team culture. • Support colleagues within the Training Facilitator team where needed, including covering training sessions in other areas during periods of absence and sharing materials or approaches that have worked well in their own delivery.

**“Great minds** ***don’t*** **think alike”**
From our talented tech teams to our standout clinical expertise, we’re bringing great minds together to build more accessible services.
As the **Coordinator** for our **Needs-Led Pathway** , you will play a pivotal role in our team, which we deliver in partnership with Sirona care & health for families across Bristol, North Somerset and South Gloucestershire (BNSSG). You’ll keep work flowing through the pathway: supporting families to complete their onboarding questionnaires and paperwork, answering their questions, coordinating their appointments, and linking them with their dedicated Care Navigator clinician.
Your primary responsibility will be to make sure every family has a positive, predictable and respectful experience of the clinical pathway – from their first contact with us through to their final ‘Moving Forward’ conversation – and of how the pathway connects with our Integrated Therapeutic Service (ITS) and our neurodevelopmental (ND) teams. The Needs-Led Pathway supports children and young people from early years up to 18, based on what they need rather than whether they have, or are waiting for, a diagnosis.
**Working in a neuro-affirmative way**
Many of the children, young people and parents you’ll speak to are neurodivergent. We work in a neuro-affirmative way: we see autism, ADHD and other neurodevelopmental differences as part of who someone is rather than problems to be fixed, and we adapt how we work instead of expecting families to adapt to us. You don’t need to be an expert on day one – we’ll train and support you – but you’ll need to share these values. In this role, they show up in small, practical ways every day:
* Telling families clearly what will happen next, when, and how long it will take – for many people, predictability is an access need rather than a preference
* Writing in plain, direct language, and following up phone or video conversations in writing so families have something to refer back to
* Asking families how they would like to be contacted, and respecting it – unexpected phone calls can be hard for some people
* Using the language families use about themselves and their children (for example “autistic” or “has autism”) and not correcting them
* Remembering that a parent or carer may be neurodivergent too, and that forms, deadlines and phone calls are harder for some families than others
* Not reading a missed deadline, a short reply or a difficult call as a lack of interest – and understanding distressed behaviour as communication
* Noticing and passing on what is going well for a child, not only what is difficult
**What you’ll be doing**
***Coordinating the pathway***
* Managing the flow of work through the pathway and its service lines, so that referrals from Sirona move promptly and no family gets stuck

***Records, information and quality***

# Forward Deployed Engineer
We usually respond within three days
**Forward Deployed Engineer**
**Type:** Full-time, permanent **Working pattern:** Flexible, home, office or hybrid **Location:** Within 50 miles of Leeds or Manchester We're hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer to lead the earliest, most open stage of our client work.
This is a forward deployed engineering role that combines hands-on technical ownership with a prominent client relationship, working directly with customer teams to solve their hardest challenges
You'll be the first engineer through the door on a new client engagement. Before there's a team, before there's a plan, with no one ahead of you telling you how to build it.
Just a client trusting you to work out what's possible, then build the proof a delivery team can scale from.
Most engineering roles start once the hard decisions are made. This one starts before them.
If that sounds exciting rather than daunting, this could be for you. **Why you'd want this**
You decide how the work gets done.
Most companies wrap their AI accounts in governance and access controls that block half of what's useful. We don't. Swap one AI tool for another, wire them into your stack, whatever suits the problem. No permission needed.
The work spans sectors, from healthcare and commerce to media and education, and it's live transformation that ships.
On a recent 19-week build, an AI insights platform turning complex data into clear, multilingual analysis, AI was embedded from day three and 80.5% of authored commits carried verifiable AI co-authorship.
We call the approach Run: deliver something the business needs now, use that work to set better engineering practices, and leave the team stronger than you found it. You're close to clients from the start, so the effect of your decisions is visible. **About hedgehog lab**
We're a UK digital product consultancy and a certified B Corp, with 20 years behind us and teams in Edinburgh, Newcastle, Leeds, Manchester and London.
AI reaches beyond the engineering floor. Around 40 people across the business, recruitment and operations included, are working out how AI changes their own roles. **What you'll do**
* Turn customer goals into a solution architecture and technology choices
* Build proofs of concept that validate your design and hand off cleanly
* Define the agentic engineering pipeline: tooling, workflows and guardrails for AI coding agents
* Shape the quality strategy, including test approach and code review
* Make other engineers more capable, pairing on real work and leaving patterns client teams can own
* Own the architectural decision records
**Who's this is for**
You'll be in front of clients from the first week, not just building behind the scenes. Shaping ambiguous problems and explaining your thinking to non-technical people is core to the job. If you'd rather keep your head down and code, this isn't for you.
**Experience you'll need to be considered**
* Real experience using AI agents to build production software, not copy-pasting from ChatGPT
* The ability to break down a complicated, poorly defined problem and ship something that works
* Strong TypeScript or Python, comfortable across the full stack, with frameworks such as NestJS or FastAPI
* Experience meeting and presenting to clients directly
* Strong written communication, especially for ADRs and docs others rely on
* Experience in consulting, professional services or a forward-deployed role
* A pragmatic take on architecture, sized to POC, pilot or production
**Where you'll work**
Whilst there's no set number of days you're required to be in the office each week, we really value spending time together in person, both as a team and with our clients.
There will be times when we'll need you to be in one of our offices or at a client site for important meetings, workshops and key moments.
To make that work, you'll need to be based within 50 miles of either our Leeds or Manchester offices.

**We're Heidi.**
We're building the future of healthcare by giving every clinician the earth's finest AI Care Partner. Our platform has absorbed the administrative chaos of 175 million patient visits and supported 67 million clinical hours. Today, we support 2.8 million patient sessions a week across 190+ countries, in 110 languages and over 200 specialties.
Healthcare systems are failing us; clinicians spend more time on documentation than on patients, and the human connection that makes medicine worth practicing is eroding. Our mission is simple: double the world's capacity for care and strengthen the human connection at its heart.
We found product-market fit with a freemium medical scribe that clinicians love. Now, we're expanding. Every task a clinician hands to Heidi is a patient who feels more attended to, a health system unclogged, and a clinician who gets to be a clinician again.
We've grown annual recurring revenue from $1 million to $50 million in two years.
To go further, we've secured US$340 million: a $100 million Series C led by Blackbird, with Phoenix Court, Point72 Private Investments and Headline, alongside a $240 million growth investment led by General Catalyst's Customer Value Fund.
If you want to join us in doing work worth shipping, jump in.
## **The role**
We're looking for a doctor who has moved into AI and can code, to join Clinical AI R&D as a Clinical AI Engineer. You'll sit inside a product pod and own the evidence for its product: define the evaluation before anyone builds, run it to a standard a journal reviewer would accept, keep watching the product once it ships, publish what the evidence shows, and change the product when the evidence says to.
The pod's engineers can change the product but can't judge whether a discharge summary missed something a consultant would catch. Clinicians can make that call but can't open a pull request. You do both, and you treat the gap between a model's output and good clinical practice as the thing you're here to measure and close.
The loop doesn't end at launch. You stay with the product for its life in market.
**What you'll do**
* **Design the evaluation.** Define evaluations for greenfield products to an academic standard: endpoints, comparators, ground truth, sample size, analysis plan. Set the bar before the result arrives.
* **Build the measurement.** Build, optimize and validate the LLM judges and rubrics that score the product at scale. Report their agreement with clinician ground truth, not their convenience, and retire the ones that drift.
* **Run it and write it up.** Execute the evaluation, do the statistics, and write it up once in a form that serves the pod, the regulatory file and an academic submission.
* **Run post-market surveillance.** Monitor output quality in production and respond to regulatory feedback with data. Our clinical safety team triages complaints and incidents; you're their counterpart in the pod, working out what their findings mean for the product and what should change.
* **Fix what the evidence finds.** Prompt and rubric changes, evaluation harness changes, code changes in the pod's codebase, shipped through the pod's normal review and release process.
* **Publish.** Contribute to peer-reviewed literature on the translational benefit of the product.
* **Be the clinician in the room.** Catch the output that reads well and is wrong. Hold the line on clinical nuance when a shortcut would ship faster.
**What you'll need**
* **A medical degree and clinical practice** with independent clinical judgment. This role runs on medical nuance, and this requirement doesn't flex.
* **Academic depth.** Study design, inferential statistics, agreement and reliability measures, sample size, handling of multiple comparisons. Thesis or publication-level work, not a methods module.
* **Experience evaluating medical software or clinical AI,** including building or validating LLM-as-judge pipelines.
* **Enough engineering to work in a production codebase.** Read it, understand what a change will do, make the change in Python or TypeScript, and get it through review. Prompt engineering and AI-assisted coding are daily tools here, and they're the floor, not the ceiling.
* **Independence.** You can run a project for weeks with light direction, and you say early when it's stuck.
* **Clear writing.** Evaluation reports, surveillance summaries and manuscripts are the primary output of this role.
**Nice to have**
* Post-market surveillance or vigilance work under a medical device framework (TGA, MHRA, FDA or EU MDR). Appetite to learn counts for more than existing depth.
* Peer-reviewed publications on clinical AI or LLM evaluation.
* Machine learning background beyond prompting, such as fine-tuning or classical model evaluation.
* Specialty depth in an area Heidi is moving into.
* An academic or clinical-site network able to host a study.
**How we show up**
* **Build for the next decade, not next quarter**. Our targets are outrageous on purpose. The world's health doesn't have the luxury of incrementalism.
* **Lead, don't wait**. We treat tomorrow's problems today. Sometimes we build what's needed before it's wanted, and we're fine with that.
* **Follow the evidence**. Trust the patient. We pursue truth relentlessly. But when the subjective and objective disagree, we treat the patient, not the numbers. Ego is a comorbidity we can't afford.
* **Own the outcome**. Everyone here carries the company. Raise problems with solutions, solve them end-to-end, and never be a bystander.
* **Ship, measure, go again**. A button today, a workflow tomorrow. More iterations beat better planning. We're precise at pace, not reckless.
* **Live in clinicians' reality**. Not the ideal workflow, the twenty-patients-before-lunch actual one. We build for exhausted humans, and we'd better be decent ones while we do it.
You'll join a team measured on real-world impact, not press cycles. We live and breathe the challenges of modern health systems, and are laser-focused on exacting the change we'd like to see. We're medicos, engineers, builders and designers who've felt (on every side of the equation) what non-care feels like, the moral and practical toll as a provider or receiver.
Building what we're building isn't always easy. Standard tech playbooks routinely fail in healthcare, and the friction of the medical system will test your perseverance. But we didn't choose easy, we chose a purpose-driven mission that actually matters. We hold ourselves to a higher standard because healthcare demands it. If you join Heidi, you recognize that the deeper question isn't whether AI can solve the global healthcare crisis, but whose hands will shape it.
True A-players progress extremely fast here. The nature of the scale-up game is demanding, but we value sustainable performance and mental health. You're trusted to perform, and you set your schedule. We operate on outcomes > inputs, not process theatre. We all take the bins out, metaphorically and literally.
**Our Benefits**
* **Equity from day one.** When Heidi wins, you win. You'll share directly in the success you help create.
* **Your health, covered.** Comprehensive private medical and dental cover through Bupa, plus 24/7 mental health, coaching and wellbeing support through Sonder and a £100/month Healthy Heidi's stipend.
* **Global parental leave**. 26 weeks paid for primary carers and 18 weeks for secondary carers, subject to eligibility.
* **Fertility support**. £7,000 one-off payment, eligibility applies.
* **Learning & development.** £700 per year for courses, books, memberships, conferences and more.
* **Home office budget** of £500 one-off to set up a workspace you actually want to work in.
* **Recharge days** after major milestones and busy periods so you can reset and come back strong.
* **Work from anywhere** for up to 4 weeks per year, wherever the world takes you.
* **Clinical leave**. 10 days per year for eligible clinical roles

Scaling humanoid robots from hundreds to tens of thousands of units takes several hundred million dollars of new capital, and much of it will come from partners, not just funds. Our biggest investors are also our supplier, manufacturer and customer. That makes capital formation and strategic partnerships one job.
You will be the senior operator who connects them. You will lead our next equity rounds alongside the CFO, open doors to the strategic and institutional investors who can carry Humanoid to a public exit, and turn partnerships with industrial, compute and supply-chain leaders into capital, contracts and access. **Capital formation (with the CFO and CBO)**

2. Build and run a single investor CRM and pipeline across VC, growth equity, private equity, crossover funds, sovereign wealth, family offices and corporate venture arms.
3. Cultivate a core group of long-term foundational investors ahead of each round, with a regular cadence of updates and meetings.

* Precision CNC machining.
* Fabrication and welding.
* Composite manufacture.
* Electronics and PCB assembly.
* Additive manufacturing.
* Heat treatment.
* Surface treatments and coatings.
* NDT.

You turn “we can’t do that” into “here’s how,” and the strongest prototypes go on to shape our roadmap.
You own the technical outcome from discovery through production adoption. Your job is to win deals by delivering fast and with value in the current production environment, prototyping and articulating value from customer requirements, measuring and proving value across customer workflows, and continuously coordinating field-observed customer needs, ideas, roadmaps, and visions with the product and sales organizations. * Own discovery, technical scoping, architecture, implementation, evaluation, productionization, adoption, and handoff for strategic customer solutions. Deploy and prove value.
* Prototype aggressively; productionize deliberately.
* For sales and product management validation, build the smallest safe prototype that tests the hypothesis inside the deal’s timeline. For production use, engineer for security, reliability, observability, maintainability, and integration with the customer’s architecture.
* Build, deploy, and evaluate with customer data; measure adoption, workflow impact, reliability, and time-to-value; iterate with technical and business stakeholders.
* Partner closely with Product and R&D to turn validated customer patterns and production evidence into supported roadmap investments, reusable components, and platform improvements.
* Turn recurring needs into reusable accelerators so the whole team moves faster.
* Develop solution specifications with the customer to feed product and engineering organizational understanding, continuously updating the specification as the solution and outcomes evolve.
* Work with Product continuously as business value emerges and outcomes become known to evaluate business potential, broader market needs, competitive differentiation aspects, and functional/technical specifications.

We are seeking highly organised, proactive and technically skilled IT Coordinators to join our Production Technology ecosystem, supporting a growing slate of UK and EMEA based film and episodic productions.

As an IT Coordinator, you are the primary on-the-ground technology partner for your production - responsible for keeping workstations, networks, editorial infrastructure, streaming and review systems, and communication tools running reliably in fast-paced, high-pressure environments. You will work closely with the Production Technology programme team, studio engineering, third-party vendors and production crew to deliver stable, secure and repeatable technical environments tailored to each show.
The ideal candidate thrives under pressure, remains calm while troubleshooting during critical moments, and understands that production schedules leave no room for ambiguity or downtime. You will join a team that values clear documentation, defined ownership, and proactive problem-solving over reactive firefighting.
Typical production environments include:
* Purpose-built stage facilities with dedicated network infrastructure
* Location and remote shoots requiring temporary or mobile connectivity solutions
* Editorial suites with specialist storage, playback and review systems
Successful candidates who meet the required criteria may be recommended to productions as freelance IT Coordinators. Assignments may involve supporting a single production or multiple concurrent shows.
***Please note:** These roles are contracted directly by individual productions and are not employed by Disney.*
# Key Responsibilities
## General
You will coordinate with external vendors for hardware procurement, equipment rentals, network provisioning and managed services - ensuring delivery aligns with production milestones. Acting as the production-side technical liaison, you will translate creative and operational requirements into clear, actionable requests for studio engineering, content security and enterprise IT teams.
You will:
* Monitor and manage production technology budgets
* Ensure compliance with content security requirements
* Develop and maintain production-specific IT documentation, including network diagrams, equipment inventories, troubleshooting guides and runbooks
## Production Office & Infrastructure
You will set up, configure and maintain production office workstations and user environments. Responsibilities include supporting production network infrastructure (VLANs, Wi-Fi and wired connectivity), integrating with studio backbone networks and supporting shared storage systems such as Avid Nexis, NAS/SAN platforms and cloud storage used across editorial, VFX and production departments.
You will also:
* Manage user accounts, permissions and software licensing
* Ensure alignment with enterprise identity and access management policies
* Coordinate WAN connectivity, firewall rules and site-wide network integration with studio engineering teams
## On-Set IT Support
You will provide hands-on support for on-set technology, including wireless networks, video village connectivity, data wrangling stations and dailies playback systems. This includes ensuring reliable internet connectivity on location by coordinating with third-party ISPs, venue IT teams and mobile connectivity providers for unit base, hotels and remote sets.
During shooting hours, you will troubleshoot and resolve issues with laptops, monitors, tablets, peripherals and network connectivity - maintaining constant awareness that downtime directly impacts the shooting schedule.
You will also:
* Support camera-to-editorial workflows including data ingest and media management
* Maintain connectivity to post-production pipelines
* Manage radio frequency coordination to avoid on-set interference
## Editorial & Post-Production Technology
You will support editorial environments running Avid Media Composer with shared Nexis storage, including workspace configuration, connectivity troubleshooting and workflow support. You will assist in setting up and maintaining review and approval workflows using streaming platforms and local playback systems.
Additional responsibilities include:
* Supporting VFX review and colour grading signal chains (SDI/HDMI routing, format conversion, calibrated monitoring)
* Assisting with secure remote editorial workflows where required
* Ensuring ongoing compliance with content security standards

* Proven experience in IT support, ideally within film, television, media or live event production

* Solid understanding of networking fundamentals: TCP/IP, VLANs, Wi-Fi deployment, VPNs, firewalls, and basic diagnostics

* Experience with remote viewing and streaming platforms (e.g. ClearView Flex/Pivot, Evercast, Cinesync, Sohonet) preferred
* Understanding of SDI/HDMI signal chains and calibrated monitoring environments
* Experience supporting Avid Media Composer workflows and editorial infrastructure is highly desirable

* Excellent troubleshooting and problem-solving abilities
* Strong documentation habits and attention to detail
* Comfortable working independently while keeping stakeholders informed
* Able to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical crew
* Confident translating production needs into technical requirements for engineering teams
* Experience supporting multi-site or international productions and distributed teams
* Comfortable working across production offices, soundstages, and outdoor locations

* Travel may be required domestically and internationally
* Manual handling of equipment up to 15kg may be required
* A valid driving license and access to a vehicle are essential

Job Purpose:
The Senior Forward Deployed Engineer - SDK Integration is a senior, customer-facing technical contributor responsible for ensuring customers successfully integrate and get value from IMS's mobile SDKs, which power telematics, mobility, and insurance technology solutions. Working primarily post-sales, this role acts as the technical bridge between IMS and its customers' mobile development teams, owning SDK integrations from kick-off through go-live and beyond across native iOS and Android and Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP). The role is expected to operate with a high degree of autonomy, making independent technical and customer-facing decisions, and to proactively shape how IMS supports and delivers SDK integrations.
This position is ideal for an experienced mobile SDK developer, or an experienced app developer with strong SDK integration experience, who also brings consultative, customer-facing experience who enjoys a balance of hands-on coding and advising others. The successful candidate will be comfortable working inside customer codebases to diagnose and resolve integration issues, explaining complex technical concepts clearly to both engineers and non-technical stakeholders, and using real-world customer insight to drive improvements to IMS's SDK, support model, and delivery processes.
Key Responsibilities:
Customer SDK Integration & Delivery
* Independently own the technical delivery of IMS SDK integrations for customers, from technical kick-off and environment setup through testing, go-live, and early-life support.
* Guide customer engineering teams through integrating the IMS SDK into native iOS (Swift) and Android (Kotlin) apps, including SDK components built with Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP).
* Advise customers on SDK configuration for trip detection, crash detection, and related features, including the appropriate setup for phone-only, Bluetooth-enabled device, and OBD-based use cases.
* Support customers in implementing SDK authentication and user session management, including token-based (e.g. JWT) authentication flows.
* Build sample code, reference implementations, and proof-of-concept apps to help customers adopt SDK features quickly and correctly.
* Ensure customers correctly implement platform permissions and background behaviour (location, motion, Bluetooth, notifications) required for reliable data capture.
Technical Troubleshooting & Escalation Support
* Independently diagnose and resolve complex customer integration issues by reviewing customer code, SDK logs, device behaviour, and backend data.
* Reproduce customer-reported issues across devices, OS versions, and frameworks, and determine whether the root cause sits in the customer app, the SDK, or the platform.
* Act as the senior technical point of contact for customer escalations relating to SDK integrations, working with the Service Desk and engineering teams to drive issues to resolution.
* Raise clear, well-evidenced defect reports and feature requests for the SDK engineering teams, including reproduction steps and supporting data.
* Contribute fixes or improvements to SDK wrappers, sample apps, and integration tooling where appropriate.
Customer Consultation & Enablement
* Build trusted technical relationships with customer engineering teams, product owners, and stakeholders.
* Run technical workshops, integration reviews, and onboarding sessions to help customers understand SDK capabilities, best practices, and trade-offs.
* Advise customers on mobile best practices that affect telematics data quality, such as battery optimisation, background execution limits, and OS-specific restrictions.
* Translate customer business requirements into practical technical integration approaches.
* Communicate clearly and confidently with both technical and non-technical audiences, setting realistic expectations on scope, timelines, and outcomes.
Process Improvement & Technical Leadership
* Proactively identify gaps and inefficiencies in SDK support and delivery processes, and propose and drive practical improvements.
* Make independent decisions on integration approaches, issue prioritisation, and customer recommendations, escalating only where business or product impact requires it.
* Define and evolve repeatable integration playbooks, onboarding checklists, and support standards that scale across customers.
* Recommend measures of integration and support effectiveness, such as time-to-integrate and escalation volumes, and use them to guide improvements.
* Share knowledge and mentor colleagues across Engineering, Service Desk, and Customer Success on SDK integration and troubleshooting.
* Influence the SDK roadmap by presenting evidence-based recommendations to Engineering and Product leadership.
Product Feedback & Cross-Functional Collaboration
* Work closely with SDK Engineering, Product, QA, Customer Success, and Account Management to ensure a smooth customer integration experience.
* Capture recurring integration challenges and customer needs, and feed them back into the SDK roadmap and product decisions.
* Partner with engineering teams to validate new SDK releases with customers and support customers through version upgrades and migrations.
Documentation, Tooling & Continuous Improvement
* Create and maintain integration guides, FAQs, troubleshooting playbooks, and knowledge base content for customers and internal teams.
* Identify opportunities to simplify the SDK integration experience and reduce time-to-integrate for new customers.
* Help improve internal processes for customer onboarding, issue triage, and knowledge sharing, including the use of AI-assisted tools where they add value.
Essential Qualifications & Experience
* 5+ years of experience in mobile application development for iOS and/or Android in production environments.
* Strong proficiency in Swift (iOS) and/or Kotlin (Android), with a solid understanding of app lifecycle, permissions, and background processing.
* Experience developing mobile SDKs or libraries for use by other developers (ideal), or substantial experience integrating third-party SDKs into mobile applications.
* Experience working with Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) in production iOS and/or Android projects.
* Proven experience in a customer-facing technical role, such as solutions engineering, technical consulting, integration support, or professional services.
* Experience working with RESTful APIs and authentication mechanisms such as OAuth or JWT.
* Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, including analysing logs and reproducing issues across devices and OS versions.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts to varied audiences.
* Demonstrated ability to work autonomously, make sound independent decisions, and manage multiple customer integrations and priorities at once.
* A track record of proactively improving technical support, delivery, or customer onboarding processes.
Bonus Qualifications:
* Experience with React Native, including native modules and bridges to iOS and Android code.
* Familiarity with Flutter and platform channels.
* Experience in telematics, IoT, insurance technology, fleet management, or connected mobility applications.
* Familiarity with location services, motion sensors, Bluetooth, and other device sensors used for data capture.
* Experience supporting B2B customers or partners integrating a developer platform, SDK, or API product.
* Experience creating developer documentation, sample apps, or technical training materials.
* Familiarity with AWS or other cloud platforms, and with tools for log analysis and monitoring.
* Experience working with global, distributed teams and customers across different time zones.
Other Contextual Information:
* Remote role based in the United Kingdom or Canada (Ontario).
* Primarily post-sales, with occasional involvement in pre-sales technical discussions where needed.
* Occasional travel to IMS offices or customer sites may be required for onboarding, workshops, and stakeholder meetings.
* Some flexibility in working hours may be needed to support customers in different time zones and during critical customer go-lives.

## About this role
You've been designing long enough to have watched tools become essential and then disappear. You know which design skills are timeless and which ones expire. **The human-centered design skills are where your heart is**, and you know that AI will take over much of the tool-based design work soon.
You see the fear around AI, and you understand where it comes from. But you also see the opportunities, and you want to show people how to work with AI in a way that benefits their lives, their users, and the world.
You can name the **ten leading designers** who should be teaching the world’s best courses and Master Classes right now. You know what each of them does better than anyone else, and where their gaps are.
Now you get the opportunity to decide what hundreds of thousands of designers learn next.
The industry leaders whose expertise you'll be turning into courses and Master Classes include **[REDACTED] and [REDACTED]**, as well as Design Leads at **[REDACTED], [REDACTED], [REDACTED], and [REDACTED]**. [REDACTED] also chairs our executive board.
You'll be involved in the entire process of creating our courses and Master Classes, and you'll lead many of the decisions, so there are incredible opportunities for you to **take initiative, make meaningful contributions, and grow**. Forget political struggles or long, pointless debates. You’ll be in a team with minimal distance between idea and action, where decisions are made ultra-fast.
## Join the Global Leader in Online Design and AI Education
[REDACTED] is the world's largest online design and AI education platform, with over 1,150,000 enrollments since 2002. We hold the trust of industry giants like [REDACTED], NASA, and [REDACTED], who rely on our courses to train their teams. Prestigious universities, including MIT and the University of Cambridge, integrate our material into their curricula. Help us **take online education to new heights** and **make a meaningful impact on humankind**.
At [REDACTED], we’re not just a company but a movement dedicated to making high-quality design and AI education accessible to everyone, everywhere.
We've pioneered online design education since 2002. We have over 1,150,000 enrollments and 1,583 company members, with more than 40 courses, 160 Master Classes, and thousands of open-source design resources, created by our team in collaboration with 240 industry leaders.
With learners from over 100 countries, your work will empower people worldwide.
## We're Hiring Three People for Our Editorial Team
We're growing, and three roles are open at the same time to build the next generation of our core educational product. Here's what each role leads on:
* **Our Course Directors, UX, UI, and AI**: lead what we teach and who teaches our courses and Master Classes. You reach out to industry leaders and create the invitation they say yes to. You bring your judgment to a planned course outline: what's missing, what doesn't belong, and whether the structure is solid. You plan and shoot courses with our Education Designers. **This is the role described here.**
* **Our Education Designers, UX, UI, and AI**: lead how design and AI are taught. You plan, structure, and create the core content, and you decide what a course participant should be able to do by the end and how they get there.
* **Our Course Writers and Editors**: lead how our courses and articles read. You make each title engaging, ensure each sentence flows, and edit the written course experience from the user’s perspective.
We're a flexible team, and you'll be able to do what you excel in. Everyone on our team creates courses, and everyone works across these roles. If you're torn between two roles, apply for the one you'd be best at, and tell us in your application which other one you considered and why.
**You, the Course Director**, decide what belongs in our curriculum and who should teach it. You reach out to the world’s leading experts, plan the courses with them, and shoot courses with them. When an Education Designer brings you a course outline, you're the one who says what's missing, what doesn't belong, and how to optimize the learning outcome so designers can succeed today. You'll work closely with our **Co-Founder**, your **Team Lead**, our other **Course Directors**, and the **Education Designers**, and you'll plan and create courses alongside them. Our Course Writers and Editors take the finished material the last mile: the scripts, hooks, headings, on-screen text in videos, quiz wording, and editorial voice. You'll also work closely with the video team and our growth team.

* **Be a core part of our Editorial Team**. You'll collaborate with [REDACTED] editors, video editors, and UX and UI designers as well as external industry leaders to create courses and Master Classes for people worldwide. You'll help them succeed in the age of AI with new skills in AI and in timeless human-centered design.
* You'll research what already exists in a topic area, so that what we build is genuinely unique. You'll look at **where design and AI are heading, what designers need** that nobody has taught well yet, and **what we should retire** because the field has already moved on.
* **Find the people who should teach it.** You decide a topic is worth a course, you work out who should teach it and why, you write the email, and you get the yes. Then you plan the content with the industry leader and agree what the course must leave a learner able to do.
* **Decide what each expert should teach.** The best designers know a great deal, and a course that tries to capture all of it becomes an information dump. You develop a point of view on what a designer genuinely needs from them, and you hold the course to it.
* **You'll decide which skills our courses teach**, both to people entering design and to experienced designers leveling up. Our goal is to help designers thrive in the age of AI and work responsibly, so their users can thrive too.
* Ensure our course participants finish each course with a solid portfolio project they can show a hiring manager.
* **Help us decide what AI should do for our course participants**. Personalized learning paths, constructive AI feedback on portfolio work, practice environments where people run real design tasks and get feedback. You'll also help us improve the user flows on our own platform, so that learning at [REDACTED] is as well designed as what we teach. You'll work on this with our founders, designers, and dev team.
* **Make an impact as you pressure-test the courses** our Education Designers plan. An Education Designer sends you a course outline, and you read it against everything you know about the field and about how people learn design, then give constructive feedback on what's missing, what doesn't belong, and where the structure can be improved. **You know the limits of your own expertise**, and you research your way past them before you weigh in. You'll also plan, structure, and create courses yourself, alongside them.
* You're one of the people **whose judgment the rest of the team leans on.** You show our Education Designers what ten or twenty years in the field taught you to look for. In return, our Co-Founder, your Team Lead, and our other Course Directors give constructive feedback on the courses you lead. You'll work in a **diverse, highly organized, result-driven environment** where you'll grow personally and professionally.
* **Act as guardian of our quality bar**. When a course goes out under our name, it has to be better than anything else available on the topic. On the courses and Master Classes you lead or review, you're the one who spots what's not good enough yet and works with the team to fix it.
* to our writers, community managers, and social media team, so our design thinking stays consistent across everything we publish.

Jacobs have an excellent internship opportunity available to ‘Year in Industry’ students. The role provides the opportunity to work on the TransPennine Route Upgrade (TRU) rail project, a project of huge importance in the North of England. The post is for a full-time Jacobs employee but may also include periods of time working with both Network Rail (the client Jacobs works alongside as part of the Programme Management Organisation) and a number of employees from other rail businesses which form Alliances and make up the Programme Delivery Organisations.
Jacobs is ever evolving and striving for the best and most efficient ways of working and is invested in you and your success. As such, no clearly defined role is provided at this time as candidates will be assessed at interview and roles can be adapted not only to suit the project demands but also to consider the abilities and aspirations of the individual.
Examples of previous roles are provided below.
**What could be your role be on TRU?**
**Role - RSI - Assistant Project Manager:**
The Contract Management Team are a client facing team responsible for engaging with the client (Network Rail) and liaising with both them and the Jacobs Teams to ensure we are compliant and in line with the contract. They support the management and administration of the contract with reporting; financial applications and scheduling/planning.
**Example of Responsibilities include:**
* Responsibility for running Production Meetings and creating new workplans for the week ahead
* Producing reporting dashboards
* Monthly Status Reports
* Updating project financial trackers
* Event Planning
* Keeping records of employee authority to work on project and subcontractor timesheets

* Support to Project Manager, Commercial Manager, Planner and the Wider (Rail System Integration) RSI Team where needed, learning key project management functions whilst managing a large team
* Client facing role, interacting with the client on an almost daily basis. Supporting the client’s needs in regard to the contract
* Publication of key project documentation, and other related materials
* Line Management duties.
**Role - TRU Programme Assurance, Common Safety Method, Technical compatibility and Interoperability:**
This team supports the RSI team and leads on the TransPennine System Assurance Case for the wider programme, allowing for the TRU programme to put sections of the railway into operational use and providing support to the Sponsor team to provide Client level assurance that the requirements for compliance are met at TRU programme level.
This includes supporting the readiness for putting into use, reporting and continuous improvement of the TRU Programme Assurance Register and associated evidence management processes.
**The TRU Programme Safety Team delivers:**
* System Safety: in accordance with the Common Safety Method for Risk Evaluation and Assessment Regulations (CSM RA) 2013.
* Technical Compatibility: in accordance with RIS-8270-RST and Interoperability in accordance with the Railway (Interoperability) Regulations (RIR) 2011
* TransPennine System Assurance Case for the wider programme (managing the Assurance Register tools)
* The role requires a structured, proactive and agile thinker with strong analytical and scenario-based reasoning skills.
**Example of Responsibilities include:**
* Support the programme assurance lead through the management, analysis and continuous improvement of assurance registers and reporting tools
* Support the stakeholder engagement across Network Rail, Delivery Partners, Train Operators, DfT and Independent Assessment Bodies to facilitate programme assurance activities and evidence gathering.
* Support the development of Programme level Safety, Interoperability and Technical Compatibility Documents in accordance with client standards
* Take part in Hazard identification workshops and management of System level hazards - issues relating to the safe integration of the Programme including systemwide interfaces, together with hazards due to the complex nature of the Programme which cannot be appropriately managed at sub-programme or project level.
* Support Programme submissions to the Independent Assessment Body to support acquiring Safety Assessment Reports
* Support submissions to the System Review Panel (SRP) and NRAP Panel to gain endorsement for the major programme stages
* Support the TRU NRAP Panel organisation by managing the Panel agenda, collecting Project Authorisation Strategy required to be obtained by other duty holders, liaise with NRAP secretary and produce minutes; all of which are necessary for the put sections of the railway into operational use.
* Identifying opportunities to improve assurance processes through digital tools, automation, process mapping and continuous improvement initiatives
* Develop digital tool user manual and deliver training to support consistent application of assurance processes across the programme.
* Attend meetings with wider industry partners to support assurance delivery
**Role - Requirements and V&V:**
The Requirements and Validation and Verification (V&V) teams deliver the Transpennine Route Upgrade requirements management process and V&V management process at programme level. The teams create and capture data against programme-level requirements which are produced using various sources to make a coherent and consistent set of programme-level requirements that are aligned with the Department for Transport's (DfT) goals for TRU, as well as Network Rail standards and policies; The Verification and Validation team check that these requirements are being met.
**Example of Responsibilities include:**
* Requirements; capture and manage requirements from the Client Development Agreement with the DfT, through the Enterprise Requirements, to the allocation and apportionment to project level Client Requirements for TRU delivery teams.
* Review delivery teams project detailed requirement to ensure traceability back to the Client Requirements.
* Verification and Validation; making sure that the work carried out by other departments is meeting the specifications requested by the customer.
* Reading technical documents and drawings and automating the formatting of data from Industry Standard Programme tools IBM Doors to Excel using Visual Basic (VBA) (program language for Microsoft applications), creating and managing VVMs (Verification and Validation Matrices).
* Support as required to Requirements and V&V Teams and wider RSI workstreams
* Using ProjectWise and ProjectMapper to verify TRU assets and relevant data
* Displaying V&V data to key stakeholders through Excel and Power BI dashboards.
**Role - Train Service Performance Management:**
The Train Service Performance workstream is a multidisciplinary function within the Railway Systems Integration team working on TRU. The workstream is responsible for understanding, forecasting, and managing the operational performance impacts associated with the delivery of a major railway enhancement programme.
Working collaboratively with Network Rail, Train Operating Companies, Freight Operating Companies, and programme delivery teams, the team ensures that railway performance considerations are embedded throughout programme planning, design, and delivery. This supports the successful implementation of TRU while protecting the performance of the operational railway for passengers and freight customers
**Role Overview:**
As a Train Service Performance intern, you will support the analysis, modelling, and reporting activities undertaken by the Performance team. You will gain experience of working with railway performance data, forecasting tools, and industry-recognised analytical software to help inform operational and strategic decision-making
The role offers an opportunity to develop skills in data analysis, performance modelling, visualisation, stakeholder engagement, and systems thinking within a complex and dynamic railway environment.
**Typical Responsibilities:**
* Supporting the analysis of railway performance data, including train punctuality, delay attribution, cancellations, and service reliability.
* Assisting in the identification of performance trends, risks, and opportunities using a variety of data sources and analytical techniques.
* Developing reports, dashboards, and visualisations using tools such as Power BI, Excel, and other analytical platforms.
* Supporting the collection, validation, and management of performance-related datasets.
* Assisting with the development and maintenance of performance forecasts to assess the potential impacts of railway infrastructure upgrades and operational changes.
* Supporting the application of Performance, Reliability, Availability and Maintainability (PRAM) modelling techniques to assess programme performance outcomes.
* Contributing to the preparation of technical reports, presentations, and performance assessments for a range of stakeholders. Assisting with reliability improvement initiatives and structured problem-solving activities, including the use of Data Reporting and Corrective Action Systems (DRACAS).
* Working collaboratively with engineering, operational, and project delivery teams to understand the relationship between infrastructure projects and railway performance.
* Supporting engagement with industry partners to help improve the sharing of performance information and insights.
**Knowledge and Skills Development Opportunities:**
The successful candidate will have the opportunity to gain experience in:
* Railway operations and performance management.
* Data analytics and performance forecasting.
* Statistical analysis and data visualisation.
* Power BI, Excel, SQL, Python, and other analytical tools.
* PRAM methodologies.
* Reliability engineering and continuous improvement techniques.
* Working within a major infrastructure programme environment.
**Role – Development Projects - Assistant Project Manager (APM)**
The Development portfolio contains a range of projects that are in their earliest stages, primarily seeking to determine whether feasible solutions exist, which options can be considered, and which is the optimum option to be progresses to more detailed design. Working collaboratively with Network Rail our multi-disciplinary teams bring a wide range of deep technical expertise to ensure that the projects developed are effective and efficient. The projects themselves range from more traditional infrastructure projects to studies and recommendations regarding working practices and business change.
As an Assistant Project Manager, you will support the scheme Project Managers and be a key part of the project leadership team. In addition to working directly alongside some of the best Project Managers in industry, you will also interface with the technical team, which gives an unparalleled opportunity to learn from across the spectrum of the various technical disciplines. You will also get to work directly with Network Rail and be instrumental in forming the positive and constructive working relationship we enjoy.

* Drive innovation and efficiencies – establishing regular reviews of where our work has brought efficiencies to the projects so that these can be captured and approved by the client and Jacobs.

JSM Group designs and builds the power networks and digital infrastructure that clients across the UK, Europe and beyond depend on, from high-voltage grid connections and critical utilities to data centres and renewable energy. Our civil, power and digital engineers work under one roof, giving clients one team from design to energisation, with the technical, commercial and consenting risk managed from day one.

• Lead full lifecycle delivery, from FEED and tender through design, procurement, construction, commissioning, energisation and handover on HV/EHV programmes up to 400kV

**Good to know:** hybrid working pattern [confirm base location and expected site travel].

• Technical authority in HV/EHV power engineering substation systems, BESS, HVDC, protection and control, and grid connection processes
• Experience leading multi-disciplinary teams across concurrent projects in live network environments
• Hands-on NEC contract management, including change events and P&L accountability on high-value programmes
**Nice to have**
• Chartered Engineer (CEng) status, or actively working towards it
• Experience with a Tier 1 electrical contractor (e.g. H&MV Engineering, Kier, Hitachi Energy, GE Grid Solutions or equivalent)
• Delivery for hyperscale data centre operators, National Grid or offshore wind end-clients
• Familiarity with Primavera P6, SharePoint or CDE platforms

• Take ownership of your work and your development
• Would rather solve a hard technical problem than avoid it
• Know that good delivery depends on civil, power and digital teams pulling in the same direction

JSM Group is an equal opportunities employer**,** and we welcome applications from everyone.
