# **Building the Future of Open Finance**
Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.
Before you apply, we encourage you to explore our culture page to understand what drives us and how we work.
## **The team**
Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.
Join our Product and Regulatory Legal team, embedded with Kraken's Product, Design and Engineering teams to ship novel products and experiences that accelerate the global adoption of crypto. We are a tight, experienced group of lawyers from a diverse range of tradfi, fintech and crypto backgrounds who move fast, stay curious and take pride in the commercial accountability of our advice, partnering directly with Product, senior leadership and Compliance to chart clear, defensible paths to launch and to keep our licensed entities running smoothly.
This is a senior product-facing legal role for the European Union. You will be the lawyer the business trusts on questions that cut across several regimes at once: for example, a single product such as a tokenised equity, a card, or an institutional custody and prime brokerage service can touch the Markets in Financial Instruments Directive ("MiFID II"), the Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation ("MiCA"), the Payment Services Directive ("PSD2"), the Electronic Money Directive ("EMD2") and banking rules at the same time. You will bring clarity on which regime applies, what it requires, and how to launch within it.
## **The opportunity**
Reporting to the Head of Product Legal, you will act as a senior legal adviser to European leadership on new products, licensing structure and regulatory strategy.
* Own cross-functional product counselling for European Union launches from discovery to design, launch and iteration, giving Product, Engineering, Compliance and leadership decision-ready advice with clear options and risk trade-offs
* Advise on the regulatory perimeter and classification of new offerings across MiFID II and the Markets in Financial Instruments Regulation ("MiFIR"), MiCA, the European Market Infrastructure Regulation ("EMIR"), payment services and electronic money rules, and banking regulation, including where an instrument or service falls between regimes (for example tokenised securities, crypto-asset derivatives, margin and financing, and stablecoin-linked products)
* Advise on payments and electronic money offerings, including the Krak card and account propositions, safeguarding, open banking and account-access obligations, and the developing Payment Services Directive 3 and Payment Services Regulation framework
* Advise on banking-related questions that arise in the European Union, including bank partnerships and sponsor-bank arrangements, deposit-taking and lending perimeter questions, the Capital Requirements Regulation and Directive, and the interaction of these rules with our custody, prime brokerage and financing products
* Monitor and interpret European Union legislative and supervisory developments, take part in consultations and industry association work where appropriate, and translate their significance for the business proactively
* Draft and negotiate client-facing terms and conditions, taking clear, business-aligned positions
* Act as gatekeeper for European Union outside counsel engagements: scope the work, estimate and manage cost, and sign off before matters go externally
* Mentor and develop more junior lawyers in the team, set quality standards for plain-English, risk-based advice, and act as a senior sounding board for colleagues across the Regulatory Legal team
* Use AI-assisted tools (for example Enterprise GPTs) to speed up regulatory analysis, first drafts and matter tracking, and to build self-service tools that let stakeholders answer commoditised legal and regulatory questions themselves
* Advise on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing requirements affecting products, including the Transfer of Funds Regulation ("Travel Rule") and the new European Union anti-money laundering package, and on market abuse, conduct, outsourcing and operational resilience obligations, including the Digital Operational Resilience Act ("DORA")
* Lead or oversee licensing, authorisation and variation workstreams in the European Union, including scoping requirements, mapping pathways, supervising outside counsel, preparing application materials and managing regulator interactions
## **What you bring**
* Qualified lawyer admitted in Ireland, England and Wales, or another European Union Member State
* 15 or more years' post-qualification experience ("PQE") in financial services regulatory law, gained at a regulated financial services institution (for example a bank, payment institution, broker-dealer, exchange, central counterparty or crypto services provider) or at a leading law firm supporting such clients, ideally with in-house or direct product counselling experience
* Deep, current knowledge of several of the following, with real depth in at least two: MiFID II and MiFIR (investment services, market structure, derivatives and conduct), MiCA (crypto-asset services, custody, trading platforms and stablecoins), European Union payment services and electronic money regulation, and European Union banking regulation
* Demonstrated ability to analyse novel products against overlapping regimes and give a clear view on classification and perimeter, including in areas where the rules are unsettled or supervisors have not yet spoken
* Direct experience managing senior regulator relationships, including notifications, information requests, supervisory correspondence and examinations
* Working knowledge of anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing, outsourcing and operational resilience obligations, including DORA
* Proven ability to instruct, supervise and manage the cost of outside counsel across multiple jurisdictions
* Outstanding analytical, drafting and organisational skills, with crisp, plain-English writing
* Ability to distill complex legal and regulatory issues into clear, actionable guidance for non-lawyer stakeholders and for senior leadership
* A pragmatic, commercially accountable approach to legal and regulatory risk that gives stakeholders a useful range of options and a clear recommendation
* Experience mentoring or managing lawyers, and the judgement to know when to escalate
* Comfort operating with a high degree of autonomy in a fast-moving, remote environment
* Familiarity with using AI tools such as Enterprise GPTs to increase the efficiency of legal services
## **Nice to haves**
* Experience advising on tokenised securities and the European Union Distributed Ledger Technology Pilot Regime
* Experience with EMIR, including the clearing obligation, margin for non-centrally cleared derivatives and transaction reporting
* Experience with prime brokerage, securities financing, margin lending or institutional custody
* Experience advising on the United Kingdom cryptoasset regime or other non-European Union frameworks that intersect with European Union operations
* Experience supporting regulatory aspects of corporate transactions, such as change-of-control notifications and entity migrations
* Experience with European Union data protection and consumer protection rules as they apply to financial products
* Fluency in a second European language
* An authentic interest in crypto and digital assets, and familiarity with Payward's and competitors' products

## **Job Title**
**Senior Manager – Product Management Training & Enablement (GG14)**
## **Role Purpose**
The Senior Manager for Product Management Training & Enablement is accountable for **hands‐on design and delivery of product management training across the organisation**, with a primary focus on **bootcamp‐style programmes and instructor‐led learning**.
The role leads the **end‐to‐end delivery of the Product Excellence Bootcamp**, delivers structured training for Product Managers at different stages of development, and ensures that training translates into **observable improvements in product practice and decision quality**.
This role does not own products or delivery teams. Its impact comes through **direct facilitation, instructing, coaching, and practical application of product management skills** at scale.
## **Key Responsibilities**
**Product Management Bootcamp – Primary Accountability**
* Own the **build, facilitation, and delivery** of the organisation’s Product Excellence Bootcamp
* Deliver multiple bootcamp cohorts per year, including:
* Live instructor‐led sessions
* Interactive workshops and simulations
* Practical, role‐based exercises tied to real work
* Ensure bootcamp content is:
* Practical and experience‐led
* Aligned to product maturity and strategy
* Directly applicable in day‐to‐day PM roles
* Continuously improve bootcamp content using participant feedback and observed capability gaps
## **Ongoing Product Management Training Delivery**
* Design and deliver **standalone training modules** across key product rigors, including:
* Product discovery and problem framing
* Strategy, prioritisation, and trade‐off decisions
* Outcome‐based road mapping and metrics
* Customer engagement and influence
* Tailor delivery for different audiences (new PMs, Senior PMs, Product Leads)
* Act as a **lead facilitator**, not just a content owner
* Build credibility as a recognised internal authority through consistent, high‐quality delivery
## **Learning Application & Reinforcement**
* Ensure training converts into **applied capability**, not just knowledge transfer
* Develop follow‐ups, clinics, and reinforcement sessions to support in‐role use of learning
* Use coaching, peer learning, and case reviews to embed behaviours post‐training
* Partner with Product Leaders to support application within teams
**Coaching (in Support of Training Outcomes)**
* Provide **targeted 1:1 or small‐group coaching** to reinforce training themes
* Focus coaching on:
* Applying tools taught in training
* Improving judgement and decision‐making
* Navigating real product challenges raised in sessions
* Use coaching selectively to improve training impact rather than as a standalone service
## **Training Assets, Templates & Materials**
* Own the training‐ready representations of product management templates, tools, and artefacts used in enablement programmes
* Ensure training materials:
* Dedicatedly reflect Enterprise PLM standards and artefacts
* Are easy to understand, instruct, and apply in practice
* Reinforce the behaviours and decision patterns encouraged of Product Managers
* Partner closely with the Senior Manager, Enterprise Product Lifecycle Management as the golden source owner to:
* Ensure accuracy, applicability, and consistency with enterprise standards
* Validate updates before use in training
* Provide structured feedback from training and classroom application to inform ongoing evolution of PLM artefacts
* Regularly refine instructional materials (examples, exercises, case studies) based on:
* Observed learner challenges
* Common misunderstandings
* Practical application gaps surfaced during training delivery
* Does not own the enterprise definition of PLM templates or standards, but enables their effective adoption through high‐quality training and practice
## **Capability Alignment & Customer Engagement**
* Work closely with:
* Product Managers
* Engineering and Operations leaders
* Learning / Talent teams
* Align training priorities to:
* Observed capability gaps
* Strategic product priorities
* Influence through expertise and facilitation, not formal authority
## **Scope & Accountability**
* Leads **training delivery programmes** with significant autonomy
* Personally delivers a meaningful proportion of product training
* Influences multiple product areas without line management responsibility
* Accountable for the **quality, effectiveness, and credibility** of product management training
## **Skills & Experience**
**Essential**
* Senior experience in product management (Senior PM, Lead PM, Head of Product or equivalent)
* Validated experience **crafting and delivering training** to product or delivery professionals
* Strong facilitation skills with senior, experience‐rich audiences
* Deep practical knowledge across product discovery, strategy, and delivery
* Credibility to challenge, coach, and teach experienced Product Managers
## **Strongly Desirable**
* Experience running **formal product bootcamps or academies**
* Train‐the‐trainer or facilitation accreditation
* Experience embedding learning in large, sophisticated organisations

Manager

* Identify material cyber risks, control weaknesses and remediation opportunities, ensuring treatment plans are owned, prioritised and tracked to completion.
* Assess inherent and residual risk, considering threat relevance, control effectiveness, business impact and risk appetite.
* Drive proportionate risk treatment by communicating exposure, options, recommendations and decision consequences, with acceptance considered only where other strategies are inappropriate.
* Provide accurate cyber risk reporting, key risk indicators and management information.
* Help business and technology teams understand their accountability for security risk management and remediation.
**Technical Security Review and Challenge**
* Assess security controls across applications, infrastructure, cloud services, data platforms and third-party services.
* Evaluate the secure use of AI-enabled tools, including their effectiveness, limitations, data handling and impact on control design and security operations.
* Review security architecture, solution designs and material technology changes to identify security risks, control gaps and attack paths.
* Challenge vulnerability prioritisation, penetration testing findings, severity ratings, remediation plans and risk treatment decisions.
* Review privileged access, identity controls, service accounts, workload identities, secrets management, exceptions and compensating controls.
* Assess cyber implications of legacy technology, technical debt, obsolescence and major transformation initiatives.

* Work with Cyber Intelligence and Security Operations teams to understand threats relevant to the assigned portfolio.
* Assess how credible threat activity could exploit weaknesses or combined control gaps to create material attack paths.
* Translate technical threat scenarios into potential business consequences, including service disruption, data loss or compromise, customer impact, regulatory or contractual exposure, financial loss and reputational harm.
* Use threat information to influence risk prioritisation, control investment and remediation decisions.
* Help leadership distinguish between theoretical technical weaknesses and credible, material business risk.

* Explain technical issues without unnecessary detail while preserving the substance and severity of the risk.

* Provide balanced advice that supports informed decisions rather than relying solely on compliance statements or technical severity ratings.
* Communicate uncertainty, assumptions and evidence limitations clearly.

* Become a credible and accessible security partner who is engaged early in business, product and technology decisions.
* Develop a detailed understanding of the assigned portfolio’s strategy, services, technology environment, delivery priorities and business objectives.

* Work collaboratively with engineers and architects to translate security requirements into practical, sustainable technical outcomes.
* Maintain a partnership-first relationship with central Cyber, aligning the assigned portfolio with Group strategy, policies, standards and capabilities.
* Represent the assigned portfolio’s business and engineering context clearly to central Cyber without weakening Group security requirements.
* Align business, engineering and central Cyber partners on material risks, accountabilities, treatment plans and decisions.
* Influence outcomes across organisational boundaries without relying solely on formal authority.
* Challenge decisions and raise material risk with independence and sound judgement while preserving productive relationships.
**Candidate Profile**
An experienced and qualified information or cyber security professional, able to operate credibly in a large, sophisticated technology environment. A strong technical background and/or previous consulting experience advising senior team members on complex cyber security or technology risk matters is highly beneficial.
* Strong security knowledge and risk judgement, with the ability to understand complex technical topics, challenge assumptions and assess credible threats, attack paths, control weaknesses and business impact.
* Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to translate complex technical security matters into clear, concise and decision-focused messages for non-technical and senior participants.
* Proven ability to build trusted relationships across business leadership, product, engineering and central Cyber, influence across organisational boundaries and maintain productive relationships while providing constructive challenge.
* Experience in relevant areas such as cloud, security engineering or operations, architecture, vulnerability management, identity and privileged access, application or data security, resilience and third-party security.
* Able to form an independent, evidence-based risk view and communicate exposure, treatment options, recommendations and required decisions.
Desirable Certifications
* CISSP
* CISM
* Equivalent industry-recognised technical or security risk qualifications, such as OSCP or OSCE, are beneficial.
* Certifications complement, but do not replace, technical credibility, practical risk judgement and executive communication capability.
Knowledge
* NIST Cybersecurity Framework
* ISO 27001 and ISO 27002
* CIS Controls
* Relevant regulations such as DORA
* Security architecture principles
* Cyber threat and attack-path analysis
* Cloud security and cyber resilience
* Cyber risk management and control assurance
* Regulatory expectations in a highly regulated financial services environment
* Knowledge of, and a strong interest in, AI technologies and their security, risk and business implications will be highly beneficial.

**Internship Summary**
The Strats team is responsible for designing, building, implementing and maintaining the algorithms at the heart of our services. This typically involves working on models for linear or convex optimisation problems and interpreting the solution of those problems as a set of financial transactions that should be executed to improve some aspect of a derivatives portfolio. It also involves implementing all the data pre-processing logic as well as the postprocessing validation checks and proposal generations, which require the handling of large data sets.
The successful candidate will work as part of a small team of 4-6 financial engineers to design and implement improvements to our optimisation services. They will work directly with the Product Development team to enhance the product, based on feedback from clients and analysis of runs, as well as on strategic projects. * Developing a new scaling scheme to improve reliability and performance
* Introducing a mix integer model to achieve rounded solutions
* Investigating how sensitive the solution is to small changes in the data to understand which constraints we should relax for maximum impact.
* Refactoring some parts of the code to share functionality and business logic across assets
* Improving the runtime performance by investigating and adding heuristics to reduce the data set and solution search space.
* Developing new functionality to better validate incoming client data prior to optimisation.

* **Forecasting and predictive modelling.** Research that helps anticipate crime patterns and inform where resources go.
* **AI and automation.** Tools such as automated meeting transcription, analysis of large public consultations and chatbots, all of which depend on reliable, well-governed data.

Our ambition is to build an industry-leading operating system for our suppliers: bringing together onboarding, day-to-day management and the insights partners need to make better commercial decisions. You’ll help turn that ambition into a clear product direction. Your initial focus will be simplifying hotel onboarding and improving how effectively we turn direct hotel supply into bookings.
You’ll be part of the Direct Hotels team, reporting to the Head of Product for Supply Platform. Working closely with Engineering, Design, Commercial, Operations and Analytics to build capabilities for hotel partners that support our broader supply strategy. The team sits within Platform, which provides shared technology and tools to help teams across loveholidays deliver the outcomes that drive value for our suppliers and experiences that delight our customers.
Your day-to-day:
Own the product direction and roadmap. Translate the Direct Hotels ambition into prioritised opportunities, clear outcomes and achievable delivery increments. Make informed trade-offs between supplier needs, commercial value and technical investment.
Understand the people using our products. Work directly with hotel partners, contracting teams and loading operations to uncover problems, test ideas and understand what will drive adoption.
Improve the journey from onboarding to bookable supply. Simplify how information is collected, checked and maintained, using automation and self-service where they make the experience easier to navigate and more reliable.
Build towards supplier self-service. Develop capabilities that progressively give hotels more control over their relationship with us, working towards connected management tools and useful commercial insights.
Take products from discovery through to measurable impact. Work closely with Engineering and Design to prototype, test, deliver and iterate. Explore practical applications of AI, define success measures and use evidence from adoption, supplier feedback and commercial performance to guide what comes next.
Your skillset:
Product ownership and strategic delivery: A track record of taking complex problems from discovery through to delivery and demonstrating meaningful user and business outcomes. The ability to connect a long-term vision to the next useful improvement, navigate uncertainty and drive delivery.
Supplier and user understanding: The ability to understand different users’ goals and turn complicated workflows into useful, intuitive products. Experience with B2B, supplier, partner or marketplace products would be particularly valuable.
Commercial and analytical judgement: Confidence connecting product decisions to growth, margin and operating costs, while considering value for both hotel partners and holidaymakers. Experience defining success measures, investigating performance and using data alongside qualitative research to make decisions.
Communication and technical fluency: Clear communication and the ability to align commercial, operational and technical colleagues around priorities, decisions and outcomes. Comfortable discussing APIs, integrations, data and platform constraints with Engineering.
Experimentation and AI curiosity: A practical approach to testing ideas and applying new capabilities, including examples of how you have used or evaluated AI to improve products or ways of working.
Experience in hotel distribution or travel technology would be welcome, but is not essential. We’re also interested in people who have solved comparable supplier, marketplace or operational challenges in other industries.

* Lead and manage the site maintenance team and maintenance contractors.
* Develop and deliver the planned preventative maintenance programme.
* Reduce reactive maintenance, repeat failures and unplanned downtime.

* Support audits, inspections and compliance reviews.
* Ensure environmental, fire, electrical and statutory obligations are effectively managed.

* Improved asset reliability and availability.

Made Tech is seeking a Senior Security and Data Engineer to join our Cyber Practice. The core mission of this role is to bridge technical execution with operational compliance while working effectively alongside UK Government Civil Servants. You will be responsible for delivering security engineering within a Security Operations Centre (SOC) environment, translating complex technical requirements into actionable data flows to support detections and alerts. The position maintains a dual focus: hands-on security engineering, including SIEM and detection logic development, and streaming data engineering; specifically, the optimisation and manipulation of high-volume streaming data pipelines. You will support outcomes so that high-quality security engineering is an enabler of delivery rather than a bureaucratic hurdle.
## Key responsibilities
**Data Engineering & Ingestion**
* **Pipeline Optimisation & Enrichment:** Manage log ingestion pipelines on a Cribl cloud platform. You will intelligently help route, collate, filter, and normalise logs, ensuring data is tagged as soon as possible and enriched at the edge.
* **AWS Cloud Telemetry Integrity:** Support the end-to-end flow of AWS security telemetry (CloudTrail management and data events, VPC Flow Logs, GuardDuty findings, EKS/container audit logs, and IAM activity) into the centralised log architecture.
* **Stream Processing & Pipeline Optimisation (Cribl Stream):** Leverage stream processing (ideally Cribl) to parse, route, mask sensitive fields, and filter out high-volume, low-value debug noise before indexing into Splunk to maximise detection visibility.
* **Data Normalisation:** Build and maintain efficient Splunk data models, accelerated searches, and field extractions mapped to OCSF, ensuring fast query performance and portable detection logic.
* **Troubleshooting Pipeline Bottlenecks:** Diagnose and resolve systemic transport failure modes: SQS/S3 ingestion lag, universal forwarder dropouts, unparsed JSON structures, Cribl pipeline backpressure, and source type schema mismatches.
* **Advanced Log Management:** Optimise log sources by summarising NetFlow data, trimming bulk data to remove unnecessary payloads, deduplicating identical logs, and pre-parsing complex regex strings.
* **Storage Architecture:** Manage real-time streaming technologies (e.g., Kinesis) and security data storage solutions including S3 buckets and Amazon Security Lake.
* **Data Tiering:** Support the classification of data into appropriate storage tiers—Hot (security events), Warm (application and performance), and Cold (compliance)—to reduce volume overhead and optimise costs.
* **Secure Ingestion:** Verify that all data in transit and at rest is fully encrypted (KMS & TLS). Ensure all fields are normalised into standard schemas (OCSF) while enforcing least-privilege access controls.

* **Detection Quality Assurance:** Act as an enabler to establish and maintain regular monitoring cycles for detection rules, helping calculate Signal-to-Noise Ratios and rule trust scores to ensure high-fidelity alerting.

* **Data Tools & Protocols:** Hands-on experience with Cribl, Kinesis, S3 buckets, and SQS Queues. Understanding of OCSF schemas and data normalisation.

# Group Transformation – AI Strategic Implementation Lead
## Lead the Group AI Implementation Pod: a multidisciplinary, agile team at the heart of Mark Allen, supporting our wider Group transformation programme.
**Group****Transformation****–****AI****Strategic****Implementation****Lead**
**Location:** London, minimum 4 days per week onsite across Herne Hill and Carter Lane, with travel to other Group offices as required **Salary:** Competitive, dependent on experience plus company benefits **Contract:** 18-month fixed-term transformation contract, with potential to extend
At Mark Allen, we create specialist content, events, data and insight for professional communities across sectors such as healthcare, agriculture, education and finance.
As AI Strategic Implementation Lead, you will lead our four-person AI Implementation Pod, a multidisciplinary, agile team at the centre of Mark Allen Group, helping turn our wider Group transformation ambitions into practical, measurable change. You'll bring together existing initiatives, identify opportunities to improve how we work and lead the implementation of solutions that deliver genuine business value, whether through AI, automation, better integration or simpler processes. This is not a pure strategy role, nor is it a technical engineering role. It sits at the intersection of **strategy, transformation and implementation**.
Reporting to the Group COO, you will provide strategic direction, prioritise opportunities and lead business implementation, working alongside an AI Technical Implementation Lead who brings hands-on engineering expertise and technical leadership. Together, supported by a Programme & Adoption Manager and Transformation Fellow, you will connect business needs, technical delivery and sustained adoption.
The Pod will work closely with managing directors, functional leaders and our development and data teams to understand and redesign workflows, improve processes and establish the systems and foundations needed for effective implementation.
For someone who has spent the early part of their career advising organisations on transformation, this is an opportunity to move in-house and **own one end-to-end**. You will have the autonomy and resources to shape and deliver a major Group-wide programme, supported by a dedicated AI Implementation Pod and selected external specialists.
**What you’ll be doing**
**Lead and connect Group Transformation**
* Set the strategic direction and priorities for the AI Implementation Pod within the wider Group transformation programme, taking accountability for its outcomes and ensuring the integrated delivery roadmap supports these objectives.
* Bring existing pilots, tools, experimentation and initiatives into the central programme where appropriate, identifying duplication, gaps and conflicting approaches.
* Connect workflow transformation, tooling and licensing, governance, policy, training, adoption and technical implementation, ensuring individual initiatives remain aligned with Group strategy and priorities.
* Provide leadership and oversight across the programme, resolve strategic priorities and escalated issues, and keep workstreams aligned with Group objectives.
**Turn opportunities into practical transformation**
* Work discipline by discipline and workflow by workflow to understand how work is currently undertaken and identify pain points, duplication, manual activity and opportunities for redesign.
* Prioritise opportunities according to strategic relevance, impact, feasibility and scalability, translating business needs into practical implementation plans.
* Lead the redesign of priority workflows, including the appropriate division of work between people, AI, automation and agentic systems.
* Identify what those changes mean for roles, responsibilities, skills and organisational structures.
**Create the framework for safe, responsible implementation**
* Ensure AI activity operates within agreed Group governance and policy, identifying where further policies, standards or guidance are required and continually developing these as technology and organisational needs evolve.
* Work closely with relevant colleagues on security, data protection, intellectual property, content protection, legal and ethical considerations, intervening or escalating where activity falls outside agreed guardrails.
* Maintain an active view of developments in AI technology, regulation, publishing, information services and the wider competitive landscape, translating these into implications and opportunities for Mark Allen.
* Work with the Technical Lead and Fellow to maintain a structured approach to horizon scanning, helping ensure the Group remains proactive rather than responding after the market has moved.
**Turn implementation into measurable value**
* Manage relationships with external consultants, partners and suppliers, ensuring their expertise and solutions support Group transformation priorities and deliver measurable value.
* Build internal capability so that Mark Allen benefits from external expertise without becoming dependent on consultancy support.
* Work with the Programme & Adoption Manager to establish meaningful baselines and measures of value.
* Ensure implementation priorities reflect commercial as well as operational value, identifying productivity gains, capacity release, structural opportunities and new growth opportunities.
* Report progress and implications clearly to the Group COO and ExCo.
**What you will be here to achieve**
Over the first 18 months, your focus will be to:
* Establish a coherent Group-wide AI implementation model.
* Bring fragmented AI activity into an aligned and governed programme.
* Establish a repeatable discipline-by-discipline transformation methodology.
* Move priority workflows from experimentation into embedded ways of working.
* Establish effective Group-wide governance, policy and implementation standards.
* Deliver measurable organisational and commercial value through productivity improvements, capacity release, simplification and growth opportunities.
* Build strong relationships across the Group and create confidence in the programme.
* Help Mark Allen progressively move from responding to AI change to operating ahead of the curve.
Success will not be measured by the number of pilots launched or tools purchased. It will be measured by whether the Group has moved from fragmented experimentation to a coherent implementation model, whether workflows and ways of working have materially changed, whether AI is being deployed safely and systematically, and whether the programme creates demonstrable organisational and commercial value.
**Must-haves:**
* Experience delivering complex transformation programmes involving people, process, technology and operating model change.
* Practical experience applying AI or automation to business workflows, with an understanding of its limitations, controls and adoption challenges.
* Proven ability to translate strategy into practical implementation and delivery.
* Strong structured problem-solving and analytical capability.
* Confidence working directly with senior executives and constructively challenging established thinking.
* Experience leading complex, cross-functional programmes, setting priorities and providing strategic oversight across multiple workstreams.
* Strong commercial judgement and an instinct for prioritising value.
* The ability to move comfortably between ExCo-level discussion and detailed implementation.
* Experience working effectively with specialist technical teams and external consultants.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* A highly proactive, pragmatic and delivery-oriented working style.
**Nice-to-haves:**
* A background in management consultancy, transformation, strategy implementation or an equivalent environment. This role is likely to particularly suit someone with approximately 5–8 years' experience who wants to move in-house and take genuine ownership of a significant transformation programme.
* Experience in media, publishing, information services or another content-rich business.
*If you do not meet every requirement but bring transferable skills, sound judgement and fresh thinking, we encourage you to apply.*
**Why join Mark Allen Group?**
Mark Allen is a specialist media business with more than 40 years of experience building trusted brands for professional audiences. You will join us at an important point in our AI transformation, with the opportunity to influence how work is designed and how AI is embedded safely, commercially and effectively across the Group.
What makes this opportunity different is the breadth of ownership. Rather than advising from the outside or delivering one workstream within a wider transformation, you will be able to connect strategy with implementation and follow the programme through from priorities and workflow redesign to adoption, governance and measurable value.
You will work directly with senior decision-makers, supported by a dedicated AI Implementation Pod and specialist external expertise, with the remit to turn AI from fragmented experimentation into an embedded organisational capability.
**We offer:**
* Significant ownership of a Group-wide transformation programme.
* Direct exposure to the Group COO, ExCo, Managing Directors and functional leaders.
* The opportunity to work alongside a dedicated AI Implementation Pod and external specialists.
* Company benefits.
* Exposure to specialist markets and loyal professional audiences.
* A culture shaped by our values - **Passionate, Creative, Nurturing and Fair**.
**How to apply**
Apply through our careers site with your CV, including a cover letter sharing what attracted you to the role and what you would bring to it.
A video introduction is **completely optional** and will not disadvantage your application.
**Right to work:** Applicants must have the legal right to live and work in the **UK**. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Meta is seeking Security Engineers with Privacy and Data protection expertise to join our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AAI) organization. You will apply deep privacy engineering expertise to hard, real-world problems in how systems collect, use, retain, expose, and delete data. Your work is AI-augmented from day one: you leverage AI tools and agents to accelerate your impact, and where the models fall short, your expertise directly drives their improvement. The problems that matter here are the ones a capable engineer cannot solve by reading the code in front of them: which jurisdiction's deadline applies to a deletion request, whether a derived dataset clears an anonymity threshold, where a deletion has to cascade. Models already handle the privacy obligations that are stated as ordinary good engineering practice, so the work is the obligation they cannot derive. This role is for privacy engineers who want to operate at the intersection of deep privacy expertise and frontier AI, not just applying AI to privacy work but shaping what it is capable of.
Responsibilities
Identify and solve ambiguous problems within the privacy and data protection space where the solution and requirements are initially unknown, driving solutions that affect multiple teams
Architect privacy capabilities and evaluation infrastructure that sets the standard across teams; drive platform-level decisions for AI-driven privacy solutions at Meta's scale
Lead the strategy and methodology for the privacy problems AI cannot yet reason about: jurisdictional and regulatory obligations, de-identification standards, data lifecycle controls, and data access reasoning
Shape how privacy expertise translates into AI capabilities: define the methodologies that make model improvement systematic and scalable
Drive cross-organizational partnerships that define how privacy and AI intersect: influence technical direction beyond the immediate team
Break down problems into smaller scoped work streams, owning the most technically complex pieces while enabling others to execute against the overall solution
Mentor other engineers across the organization, build a community, and act as a role model for privacy engineering practices and Meta values
Disseminate findings through internal publications, knowledge sharing, and contributions to the broader privacy and security community
Minimum Qualifications
B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related field, or equivalent experience
8+ years of hands-on engineering experience in technical privacy, data protection, or privacy-adjacent security engineering
Deep expertise in at least one privacy subdomain with demonstrated ability to advance the state of the art: purpose limitation, retention and deletion, data access control, jurisdictional obligations, de-identification, consent, or ML and model privacy
Experience implementing privacy obligations in production systems, in addition to reviewing or advising on them
Software engineering proficiency, including code review and maintenance, with experience coding in Python, PHP, Java, C/C++, or an equivalent language
Track record of architecting privacy systems, controls or programs that operate at scale and influence how others build
Demonstrated ability to define and drive complex, ambiguous problem spaces with group-level impact
Preferred Qualifications
Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
Experience improving AI model performance through expert feedback, red teaming, or evaluation design
Experience with pseudonymization lifecycle, including deletion of the user-to-pseudonym mapping
Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
Experience implementing obligations conditioned on jurisdiction, age band, or cohort: regional carve-outs, regulatory deadlines, minor and parent-initiated request handling
Contributions to the privacy or security community (original research, tools, conference presentations, publications)
Experience applying differential privacy, k-anonymity, or other formal de-identification techniques in production rather than in research only
Experience with privacy review or privacy incident response at scale

People Management

* Assess and forecast financial performance, including comparison of actuals to budget, consider outlook and manage activity to deliver agreed financial outcomes.
* Control and maintain the asset management databases.
* Drive cost management initiatives across facilities operations and real estate activities.
* Identify and deliver efficiency opportunities while maintaining appropriate service standards.
* Ensure robust financial governance over facilities expenditure, contracts and capital investments.
Corporate Real Estate and Workplace Management
* Lead the planning and execution of the EU real estate strategy, ensuring alignment with business priorities, governance requirements and cost objectives.
* Develop workplace and occupancy plans to support business requirements across the UK and EMEA entities.
* Identify opportunities to optimise office footprint, space utilisation and facilities operating costs.

* Maintain accurate departmental space utilisation records.

* Primary contact for all security related incidents and FM crisis controller.
* Manage the Company’s Business Continuity Site and all associated aspects.

**Warehouse Operative** Permanent | Bracknell HQ
**Be part of what happens before we go live**
At NEP UK, we help bring some of the world’s biggest live sporting, entertainment and broadcast events to audiences everywhere. Behind every successful production is a huge amount of preparation, and that starts with our teams at base.
We’re looking for a **Warehouse Operative** to join us at our Bracknell HQ and play an important part in getting our people, equipment and technology ready to go on the road.
This is much more than moving equipment around a warehouse. You’ll work hands-on with professional broadcast kit, help prepare our outside broadcast trucks and flypack systems, and make sure everything needed for a production is checked, organised and ready to perform when it reaches site.
If you enjoy practical work, like being part of a busy team and have an interest in technology, logistics or live events, this could be a great opportunity to build your experience within the broadcast industry.
**What will you be doing?**
**Getting our productions ready**
No two productions are quite the same, and you’ll play a key part in making sure the right equipment gets to the right place, in the right condition and at the right time.
You’ll:
* Prepare broadcast equipment and technical kit against production load lists and requirements
* Carry out pre-deployment checks, making sure equipment is complete, clean and ready to use
* Help load and unload our outside broadcast (OB) vehicles, ensuring equipment is handled and secured safely
* Support the preparation of flypack systems and other production equipment before they head to site
* Help return OB trucks and flypacks to their standard configuration after productions, testing, restocking and preparing equipment for its next job
**Keeping everything moving**
Our warehouse is a busy operational hub supporting productions across the UK and beyond. You’ll help keep it organised, accurate and running smoothly by:
* Receiving, checking and storing incoming equipment
* Using our asset management systems to scan, register and track broadcast equipment
* Supporting stock control and ensuring equipment is stored correctly
* Preparing shipping and dispatch documentation
* Coordinating deliveries, collections and equipment movements with colleagues and external suppliers
* Helping maintain a safe, organised and efficient working environment
**Working as one team**
You won’t be working in isolation. You’ll be part of a wider team of people who make live production happen, working closely with colleagues across Base Operations, Engineering and Technical Maintenance.
You’ll learn from people with significant experience in broadcast and live production, support the preparation of our technical facilities and have opportunities to get involved in wider projects and improvements to how we work.
**What are we looking for?**
You don’t necessarily need a background in broadcasting. We’re interested in people who bring the right attitude, enjoy practical work and are keen to learn.
You’ll ideally be someone who:
* Is practical, organised and hands-on, with strong attention to detail
* Takes pride in getting things right and looking after equipment
* Can work effectively in a busy environment where priorities can change
* Is proactive and willing to get stuck in and help the wider team
* Communicates well and enjoys working collaboratively
* Is comfortable using basic IT systems and willing to learn our specialist equipment and asset-management systems
* Can prioritise different tasks and manage their time effectively
* Brings a positive, flexible approach to both the work and the people around them
Experience within a warehouse, logistics, technical, events or equipment-handling environment would be useful, but it isn’t essential if you can demonstrate the right skills and attitude.
A forklift licence would be an advantage, although training can be provided. A full UK driving licence would also be useful.
**What’s in it for you?**
**Your work goes further than the warehouse** The equipment you prepare at our Bracknell base could go on to support some of the most exciting live productions in the UK and beyond. You’ll be contributing directly to the technology and infrastructure that makes those broadcasts possible.
It’s also an opportunity to join an industry where there is always something new to learn. Broadcast technology continues to evolve rapidly, and you’ll be working around specialist equipment, experienced technical teams and a wide range of production environments.
**Learn, develop and grow**
We want people to be able to build their knowledge and develop their careers with us. You’ll have opportunities to:
* Gain hands-on experience with professional broadcast equipment and technology
* Learn from experienced colleagues across our operational and engineering teams
* Develop your understanding of OB trucks, flypacks and live production workflows
* Build broader technical, operational and logistics skills through experience on the job
* Access online learning and development resources
* Undertake relevant training, including forklift training where required
* Explore opportunities to develop and progress as your skills, experience and interests grow
Whether you already have warehouse experience or you’re looking for a way into the world of broadcast and live production, this is an opportunity to learn from people who know the industry inside out and build skills that can take you further.
**The Practical Details**
**Location:** NEP UK, Downmill Road, Bracknell
**Working pattern:** Monday to Friday, working shifts between 8am and 8pm, with occasional weekend cover. You would normally be expected to work no more than one weekend in four.
If you’re looking for a hands-on role where you can see the impact of your work, learn about some incredible technology and be part of the team behind major live productions, we’d love to hear from you.

# Senior Optimisation Engineer
Full-time
Engineering
Hybrid
A flexible grid connection can bring a data centre online years sooner, but the network can restrict it when it is congested. We make that connection firm with a battery and software, and the software comes down to three optimisation problems: how big the battery must be, how to run it every few minutes, and how much risk is left to price. You’ll own all three, and set how we build, test and defend every model behind them.
## What you’ll do
* Size under uncertainty: choose battery power and duration with a two-stage stochastic model, capacity first, then dispatch across scenarios of curtailment, load and price, so the site holds its firm limit to a stated reliability at the lowest cost per firm MW.
* Model curtailment risk: turn a connection offer, network history and live active network management (ANM) signals into calibrated distributions of how often, how long and how deep restrictions will be.
* Run the battery live: a rolling-horizon optimiser re-solved every few minutes, with a reserve floor that rises with the curtailment forecast and is never traded.
* Stack the rest: GB wholesale markets, the Balancing Mechanism, the Capacity Market and DNO flexibility, priced net of degradation.
* Bring cooling into the problem: treat the chiller plant and the building’s thermal mass as a second battery, within comfort and equipment limits.
* Turn results into numbers lenders can use, and defend them: P50 and P90 outcomes, downside cases, and a reconciliation of what each site delivered against what we underwrote.
* Keep it fast and honest: tight formulations, decomposition and warm starts where solve time matters, and backtests on measured data for every model we ship.
* Lead the technical work: choose methods and tools, review the models others build, and help hire and mentor the engineers who join you.
## What we’re looking for
* Depth in optimisation: a PhD or master’s in operational research, applied mathematics, power systems or control, or the equivalent from industry.
* Typically five years or more building models that run in production or drive real decisions: LP and MILP as a minimum, and stochastic, robust or chance-constrained formulations ideally.
* Experience leading technical work: setting direction, reviewing other people’s models and mentoring engineers.
* Fluent Python and a modelling layer such as Pyomo, JuMP, CVXPY or gurobipy, and a working feel for how solvers like Gurobi, HiGHS or Xpress behave.
* Probabilistic forecasting, scenario generation and reduction, Monte Carlo, and checking that a P90 really is a P90.
* Physical intuition for power and storage: MW against MWh, efficiency, degradation, ramp limits and state-of-charge constraints.
* Production habits you can set for a team: tests, code review, reproducible experiments and clean data pipelines.
* Useful but not required: GB power markets, non-firm connections and ANM, battery trading, or data centre power and cooling.
## Who you might be
You might have a doctorate in stochastic optimisation or power systems, and have spent the years since building optimisers that run real assets. You might lead dispatch or trading optimisation for batteries today, work on a solver, or work on energy and capacity problems at a hyperscaler. What matters is depth: a model you built that you can defend line by line.
## In your first six months
* Ship improvements to the sizing engine in your first month.
* Own the curtailment-risk model end to end: data, method, calibration and the error bars we quote.
* Run the dispatch optimiser on a live site and close the gap between plan and outcome.
* Set how we review, test and release models, and help hire the engineers who join you.

Its purpose is to turn the Digital strategy into a technical strategy that delivers it: deciding what gets built, in what order and to what standard, so the business can sell what it has committed to sell. A decision taken in one team should still work in another, our promises to customers on access, security, reliability and cost should hold on every channel, and the hardest problems should get solved once.

Design and build the hardest parts of the platform, hands on: how customers get to the right data and products, how that access is controlled, and what it costs us to serve. Stay close enough to the code that the design still holds once it’s built

Extensive experience building and running production software end to end, from system design through to operating it live
Technical leadership beyond a single team: a track record of influencing engineers and teams you don’t manage, and building agreement across them

AI-native in how you build: you use AI tooling with judgement, stay current with how agentic development is evolving, and help make effective agentic practices the norm across the team

## **Our Mission**
At Omnea, we’re reinventing how enterprise businesses operate, starting with the most painful parts: **procurement** – where a single purchase can drag on for months, trigger **50+ emails**, and pull in **Finance, Legal, Security, and IT** just to get something approved.
We’ve raised **$75M from Khosla Ventures, Insight Partners,** and **Accel** to change that. Our AI-native platform connects every person, step, and system so buying is fast, safe, and efficient – one place to request, automated approvals and renewals, real-time supplier risk, and complete spend visibility.
The opportunity is massive. **Every enterprise on the planet has this problem and nobody has solved it**. We’ve 10x’d ARR to double-digit millions in 18 months and are trusted by global enterprises like Spotify, MongoDB, Monzo, and Albertsons. We’re now the **4th fastest growing startup** in Europe & the Sunday Times' #1 Best Medium Sized Tech Company To Work for.
**Our team previously scaled Tessian** (**cybersecurity tech,** backed by Sequoia, Balderton, Accel**,** acquired post-Series C), and our team includes ex-founders operators who’ve grown unicorns, shipped world-class products, and executed at the highest levels. You’ll work alongside leaders like **Ben**, **Abs**, **Sabrina**, and **Rebe**.
## **Find out more about the team and life at Omnea** **here****.**
## The Role
AI is changing what "technical support" means at a fast-growing SaaS company. The old model was reactive: wait for a ticket, dig through logs, escalate up a chain until someone senior enough could unblock it. Increasingly, the first pass on an integration failure or a broken workflow can be directed rather than done line by line by hand: AI can trace through logs, draft hypotheses, and suggest fixes fast.
The job shifts with it. Instead of grinding through every stack trace yourself, you direct AI to accelerate the investigation and apply what AI can't: judgment on whether a fix is safe to ship into a live enterprise environment, whether the root cause is actually fixed or just patched, and whether this is a one-off or a pattern worth escalating to Product.
As Omnea's Technical Solutions Engineer, you're the senior technical presence sitting between Customer, Product, and Engineering. You own Omnea's most complex customer-facing technical problems end to end - gnarly integrations, cross-system issues, escalations nobody else can crack. You're the person the team calls in when something's on fire, and you're just as comfortable stepping into a customer's implementation when it gets technical.
This is a foundational hire. You'll set the technical bar for how Omnea supports enterprise customers, and help define how the function grows from here.
## What You'll Do
* **Own the hardest technical problems:** Lead investigation and resolution of Omnea's most complex customer issues - integrations, configuration edge cases, cross-system bugs. Direct AI to accelerate the first pass, then apply the judgment AI can't: is this safe to ship, is the root cause actually fixed.
* **Be the SWAT team between Customer, Product, and Engineering:** Act as the senior escalation point when an issue is beyond what the Customer team can resolve alone, and the technical voice in the room when Product and Engineering need to understand what's really happening on the ground.
* **Get technical inside implementations:** Step into live implementations when they hit technical complexity - tricky integrations, custom logic, unusual data flows - and work directly with the implementation team to get them unstuck.
* **Feed the product roadmap:** Spot patterns across the issues you resolve and turn them into clear, well-scoped input for Product and Engineering, so the same problem doesn't need solving twice.
* **Build the standards as you go:** Document what you learn, build the tooling and playbooks for triaging and resolving complex technical issues, and raise the bar for technical quality as the team grows around you.
## What's Different About This Role
* You'll spend more time directing AI through the first pass of an investigation than manually tracing every log line yourself. AI narrows down the likely cause fast; your job is confirming it's right and safe to act on.
* Writing a sharp, specific brief for what you want AI to investigate or fix is now a core skill, not a nice-to-have.
* Judgment on production risk matters more, not less: AI can suggest a fix in minutes, but you decide whether it's safe for a live enterprise environment.
* You'll keep experimenting with AI tooling as it evolves, and bring what works back to the rest of the team.
## About You
We don't expect you to have done this exact job before. TL;DR: you're a technical, customer-facing problem-solver who's as comfortable elbow-deep in an API integration as you are explaining what went wrong to a CFO's technical lead.
* 3-8+ years in a customer-facing technical role - technical support engineering, solutions engineering, implementation, or similar - at a fast-growing SaaS company
* A technical background: a Computer Science or Engineering degree, prior experience as a software developer or engineer, or strong hands-on experience with SQL, APIs, and system integrations
* Strong systems intuition: comfortable diving into unfamiliar platforms, reasoning about architecture, and figuring out where in a complex system something's actually broken
* Comfortable directing AI tools to speed up investigation and first-draft fixes, with the judgment to know what to trust and what to double-check
* An excellent communicator who can flex between a technical deep-dive with an engineer and a clear explanation for a non-technical stakeholder
* Entrepreneurial and comfortable with ambiguity: you want to help build the standards and playbook for this function, not just follow one that already exists
* High ownership: when something's broken, you own it through to resolution, and you raise your hand for the hard problems rather than waiting to be assigned them
At Omnea, we embrace diversity. To build a product that's loved by everyone, we're best served by a team with all sorts of backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. * You've built things with LLMs, even side projects or prototypes, and understand concepts like prompting, tool calling, embeddings, and RAG.
* You've integrated a model API (e.g. OpenAI) and have at least a working feel for cost, latency, context windows, and rate limits.
* An awareness of how building and evaluating LLM systems differs from traditional software, and an interest in getting good at it.
* Familiarity with, or genuine curiosity about, vector databases, embeddings, and retrieval techniques such as semantic and hybrid search.

* Genuine curiosity and a tinkerer's instinct. You build with AI because you find it interesting, not just because it's the job.
* A bias for shipping: you'd rather get something working in front of people than polish it indefinitely.
* Valuing good engineering practices: fast feedback, testing, and simple design; and wanting to get better at them. You might already follow the people who champion XP-style ways of working; if you don't have deep experience with them yet, the enthusiasm to learn matters more.
* You pick things up fast across unfamiliar domains and can build enough understanding of someone else's problem to be useful.
* You communicate clearly and can explain trade-offs to engineers and non-engineers alike.

**Job Title - Software Engineer III (Innovation Engineering)**
**Description -** Turn ambitious ideas about the future of learning into working evidence, fast. Join Pearson Labs to prototype with AI and emerging technology, test what matters with real users and help shape where Pearson invests next. **Also known in the market as: Innovation Engineer; Prototyping Engineer; Applied AI Engineer; R&D Software Engineer.**
**About Pearson Labs**
Pearson Labs is the applied R&D function within the Office of the CTO. Our job is to explore, experiment with, and prototype emerging technologies that could transform how the world learns, is assessed, and works. Under Pearson's newly approved Innovation Architecture, Labs is part of a shared innovation capacity that business units across the company draw on to get new concepts moving fast, with rapid prototyping, early-stage technical support, and evidence that helps leaders make confident continue, pivot, or stop decisions.
This is real work with real reach. In the last year the team has run an eight-week beta with university physics educators, filed patents from prototype work, placed in company hackathons, and built everything from AI tutors and interactive learning objects to haptic hardware for skills training, smart-glasses learning experiences, room-scale immersive environments, multi-agent assessment systems, knowledge graphs, and voice agents, demoing that work to executives and customers around the world. The lab itself operates as a working customer surface: sales teams, product teams, and customers come through the space, and what we build gets used in front of them. We are customer-centric, technology-first, systems-focused, and relentlessly curious about what's next.
**About the role**
Most software roles are defined by a specialism. This one is defined by a contribution: taking an idea about the future of learning and turning it into working evidence, fast. Jobs across product and engineering are reshaping in the age of AI, and we think the interesting roles now organise around what you move forward rather than which discipline you sit in. In Labs, that contribution is the prototyper's: discovering what's possible, building the version that proves it, and handing it over well.
As an Innovation Engineer you will work across the Labs portfolio, building prototypes and running experiments with emerging technologies. Some weeks that means a scrappy proof of concept to answer a single question; other weeks it means carrying a validated prototype toward pilot quality with real users. You will help us answer big questions, such as:
* What will the future of learning look like?
* How can we create meaningful experiences for learners and educators through new technology?
* Which technologies will make the biggest impact in learning, assessment, and work over the next decade?
You will get unusual visibility for an engineering role: your prototypes will be seen and used by senior leaders, business units, and customers, and your evidence will directly shape where Pearson invests next.
**What you'll do**
* Design, build, and ship prototypes that test hypotheses about learning, assessment, and work, from quick demos to multi-technology systems piloted with real users.
* Run experiments properly: framed around a validated story, user-first, with measurable objectives and honest findings, whether the answer is yes or no.
* Work hands-on with emerging technologies, currently including AI agents, multimodal models, immersive and spatial computing, and knowledge graphs, and help the team understand what they mean for learning.
* Get to a minimal viable system quickly, keep it simple, and add complexity only when the evidence earns it.
* Tell the story of the work: demos, showcases, short technical notes, and contributions to our public portfolio site.
* Treat innovation as a team sport. You will build alongside our Learning Science teams, who ground prototypes in how people actually learn, with the other innovation teams around the business, including AI research, Ventures, and the innovation teams inside each business unit, with product teams who take our work forward, and with the business units who bring us their hardest problems.
* Document and hand over cleanly, so validated work can move into product engineering without losing what made it work.
**How we work**
We are an AI-native team. We build with coding agents and agentic workflows daily, and we treat AI as leverage that lets a small team cover ground that used to need a much larger one. Our stack is pragmatic and moves fast: Claude Code and Cursor, Railway, internal hosting platforms developed by our colleagues and dedicated to rapid prototyping use cases, and cloud deployment patterns designed for speed. None of it is precious; the right tool is the one that gets to evidence fastest.
Our method draws on innovation engineering practice: start with a story worth validating, put the user before the system architecture, work from the resources in front of you, break systems into simple parts, reduce the downside rather than optimise the upside, and measure progress with objectives you can actually check. Every programme runs on a hypothesis and closes with an explicit scale, pivot, or stop decision, and we record the stops as proudly as the wins, because a weak proposition stopped in time frees capacity for a strong one. Labs owns the earliest stages of Pearson's innovation funnel, from sensemaking through proof of concept, with a defined graduation into product development, so prototypes here are judged on the decisions they enable.
**About you**
We're looking for entrepreneurial technologists who are excited to tackle ambiguous problems with ingenuity and energy. You should have:
* **Technical excellence:** strong programming and prototyping skills, with working fluency in modern software design, APIs, and cloud deployment. You can take an idea to a working system on your own.
* **AI fluency:** genuine hands-on experience building with AI, whether that's LLM-powered applications, agents, or AI-assisted development workflows, and an appetite to keep pace as the field moves.
* **Creative problem-solving:** you generate original approaches to loosely defined problems and know when to test several cheaply rather than commit to one.
* **Customer focus:** a desire to understand the problems learners and educators actually face, and to let their feedback beat your assumptions.
* **Systems thinking:** a knack for seeing how technologies, products, and ecosystems interconnect.
* **Rigour:** disciplined tracking, documentation, and communication of the innovation process. Fast does not mean sloppy.
* **Curiosity and passion for learning:** you tinker, you read, you build things nobody asked for, and education is a domain you actually care about.
**What seniority looks like here**
We are open to a range of experience levels, and we will shape the level of the role around the person. As a guide:
* Earlier in your career, you'll own well-scoped experiments end to end: building functional prototypes, running usability tests, and presenting findings to the team and stakeholders.
* With more experience, you'll lead multi-technology prototypes at higher maturity, drive experiments from hypothesis through validated outcome, mentor other engineers, and influence which ideas the lab pursues.
* At the most senior level, you'll act as a technical advisor across the portfolio: setting engineering standards for applied research, carrying prototypes toward production readiness with product teams, and generating invention disclosures and patents from the work.
If you're unsure whether you're "senior enough", apply anyway. We care more about what you've built and how you think than about years served.
**Nice to have**
* Experience communicating complex technical ideas to broad audiences, through demos, presentations, writing, or social media.
* Familiarity with design thinking, rapid prototyping, or lean startup methodologies.
* Interest in learning science, neuroscience, or human-computer interaction.
* A network of technologists, designers, and builders, especially in EdTech.
* Patents, publications, hackathon wins, or a portfolio of side projects.
**What sets you apart**
* You're a hands-on maker who loves to prototype and tinker with new tools.
* You thrive in ambiguity and adapt quickly as priorities shift with the evidence.
* You're as comfortable deep in code as you are demoing your work to customers and senior leaders.

About us
Re-architecting Engineering for the Age of Intelligence
PhysicsX is the physics AI company for industrials. The company’s mission is to accelerate hardware innovation by overhauling what industrial engineering and manufacturing look like today. PhysicsX is building a new simulation software stack to deliver deep physics AI enablement across the entire engineering lifecycle. The company partners with leading organisations in aerospace & defence, automotive, semiconductors, materials, and energy & renewables, supporting them on some of their most critical and complex challenges. PhysicsX is headquartered in the United Kingdom, with offices in London, New York, and Singapore and an expanding presence in the Bay Area.
The Role
PhysicsX is building a platform that enables Data Scientists and Simulation Engineers to build, train, and deploy Deep Physics Models. The platform handles massive volumes of complex simulation data and enables high fidelity multi physics simulation through AI inference.
We are looking for a Senior (potentially Staff level, depending on the candidate) Software Engineer to join the AI Workbench platform team. This is a software engineering role, not an ML research role. You do not need to be a practising ML engineer, but you do need to be fluent in the language of ML and data platforms, ideally through prior hands on experience with ML platforms or data science work.
The team sits in a highly infrastructure heavy domain without being an infrastructure team itself. A large part of the role is building strong working relationships with the infrastructure team and owning the work that falls in the space between the two, where ownership is not always clearly defined. You will also play a key role in mentoring and developing engineers across the team, some of whom are early career and some mid career.
Note for candidates: PhysicsX is currently going through a team reorganisation. The scope of this role may evolve as team structures settle, and we have kept this description intentionally broad rather than narrowly tailored to today's team shape.
What You Will Do
Design and build distributed systems, services, and APIs for high dimensional simulation data across the machine learning lifecycle, from data processing and model training to inference services.
Own work end to end in a domain where responsibilities often sit between the AIWB platform team and the wider infrastructure team, and proactively build the relationships needed to manage that ambiguity well.
Build tools that enable data scientists and engineers to create automated, robust pipelines for data ingestion and processing, powering active learning loops.
Architect and integrate storage solutions, data warehouses, and data lakes to handle the demands of complex simulations, multimodal data, and deep learning workloads.
Deploy and support services across more than one production environment, including cloud and on premises or air gapped customer environments.
Define system architecture for new capabilities, making trade offs across performance, reliability, cost, and developer experience.
Author and review Technical Decision Records and contribute to Technology Radar reviews.
Mentor and support the growth of engineers across the team, including those earlier in their careers, and act as a technical role model.
Remain genuinely hands on. Writing code stays part of the job at every level, this is not a purely managerial track.
Communicate clearly and confidently with a wide range of stakeholders and personalities across engineering, delivery, and customer facing teams.
What You Bring to the Table
A passion for the craft. You are driven by engineering excellence and enjoy building things properly, not just shipping quickly.
Strong Kubernetes experience. This is a must have, including comfort with CRDs, Operators, and infrastructure configuration tools such as Helm or ArgoCD.
Strong command of Go, plus working knowledge of Python. Comfort with Rust is also valued. Experience across Kubernetes, Go, Python, and Rust is ideal.
Experience deploying and supporting services in more than one production environment, not just a single deployment target.
An ML platform background or prior data science experience, even if you have since moved into pure software engineering. You understand how ML practitioners and researchers think and talk about problems.
Intellectual curiosity and a proactive approach. You do not need to be told what to do next.
Strong communication and organisational skills, with experience operating at a senior or staff level, or equivalent people leadership experience, in a comparable engineering organisation.
Comfort with ambiguity and an adaptable, startup minded approach. PhysicsX moves quickly and priorities shift, and we are looking for people who thrive in that environment rather than finding it difficult.
Prior experience mentoring or developing other engineers.
Ideally
Experience at an ML focused startup or platform company, or a strong infrastructure background from a larger organisation such as a bank, provided you can demonstrate adaptability to a smaller, faster moving environment
Side projects, open source contributions, or things you have built for their own sake. Not a requirement, but a nice signal of genuine engineering passion.
Understanding of what it takes to build and support software across cloud, on premises, and air gapped environments.
Experience with big data systems and analytics at scale in production.
What We Offer
Equity options, share in our success and growth.
10% employer pension contribution, invest in your future.
Free office lunches, great food to fuel your workdays.
Flexible working, balance your work and life in a way that works for you.
Hybrid setup, enjoy our new Shoreditch office while keeping remote flexibility.
Enhanced parental leave, support for life's biggest milestones.
Private healthcare, comprehensive coverage.
Personal development, access learning and training to help you grow.
Work from anywhere, extend your remote setup to enjoy the sun or reconnect with loved ones.

We take more photos than ever, but most of them end up buried in camera rolls, mixed in with screenshots, receipts and where we parked the car. The moments that matter most are often the hardest to find.
Popsa turns that clutter into something worth keeping. Our memory curation platform uses on-device intelligence and generative AI to find the stories in your photo library, suggest themes, write captions and lay out designs. Then we turn them into beautiful, covetable photo books, prints and more, so anyone can make something they're proud of, no design skills needed.
And it's working. More than 13 million people across 50+ countries have used Popsa, our apps are localised into 12 languages, and most of our orders now come from outside the UK. Recently, we've been focused on curation: building tools that understand your photo library and make it fast to find, rediscover and choose the stories worth keeping. The next chapter is about levelling up how those stories are told.
We want to honour people's memories. That means helping them make something sophisticated, deeply personal and genuinely covetable.

* **Rethinking how our customers make designs with AI.** Our current approach works, but new AI technologies give us a chance to make the process of creating a beautiful object more intuitive, and make the finished design more sophisticated. * **Raising the standard of the whole experience.** We're in a crowded market, and as a consumer app, people need to choose us again and again. The experience has to be easy, empowering and lovable, every time.
