# Senior Android Engineer
Join our team at the Guardian and be a part of a diverse and inclusive global organisation that delivers fearless, investigative journalism and holds power to account. Our team of award-winning journalists, cutting-edge commercial professionals and industry-leading digital experts are committed to making a difference and represent a wide range of backgrounds and perspectives. We offer a challenging and exciting environment for career development, with a focus on training, growth and fostering an inclusive culture.
We are now looking for a **Senior Android Developer** to join our Apps Experience team. Development of digital products is central to the Guardian. We create our award-winning Android app primarily in Kotlin and Java using Android Studio. We're focussed on providing a fast and stable experience to our users, and our Play Store rating of 4.7 stars is testament to that.
You'll work on major new features, as well as improving and maintaining existing functionality for The Guardian's Android app. As a Senior Developer you'll take the lead on projects and offer encouragement and guidance to help others to grow.
**About the role**
* Building and testing major new features, as well as improving and maintaining existing functionality for the app.
* Working 90%+ in Kotlin, but you may be required to work with Java too.
* You won't be coding in isolation - our culture is strongly collaborative, whether pair programming with other developers or working closely with other stakeholders.
* You can expect to work closely with iOS, server-side, and web engineers, and designers, product managers, editorial and commercial colleagues.
* You'll take on a leadership role in some of the teams projects
* You'll be encouraged to help others grow - you will pass on your expertise to other developers, whilst continuing to grow yourself.
* Sometimes deciding what code to write is as hard as writing the code itself. As an engineer you'll be involved in product decisions as well as technical ones.
* You'll strive to be innovative on a daily basis, as well as at our regular hack days.
**About you**
* You have demonstrated expertise in Android development and you have a strong interest in growing your skills.
* You have strong competence in one or more of modern Android development tools, including Jetpack Compose, Coroutines/Flow, MVVM, Webviews, other Jetpack libraries, and modular app architectures.
* You test your code and promote a culture of testing. Demonstrate experience with some of JVM unit testing, instrumented testing, and UI regression testing
* You are comfortable working with both cutting edge technologies as well as legacy code
* You have experience of, or are willing to take on a leadership role in some team projects
* You have a rough idea of how iOS development works and you'd like to know more, perhaps even try it yourself.
* Familiarity with Swift and ObjectiveC for iOS, or Scala and Typescript for server side development is useful.
**We actively encourage applications from groups traditionally underrepresented in the UK media**
Our developers operate in a hybrid environment working 1 day a week from our offices in Kings Cross and 4 days remotely. If you'd like to come in more than that, that's great too.
We strive for transparency in remuneration where possible. The salary for new Senior Android Developers at the Guardian is £82,000 per year.
We value and respect all differences (seen and unseen) in all people. We aspire to have inclusive working experiences and an environment that reflects the audience we serve, where our people have equal access to career development opportunities, their voices are heard and can contribute to our future. We actively encourage applications from people of all backgrounds. Many of our staff work flexibly and we will consider all requests for flexible working arrangements.
**How to apply**
To apply, please upload your latest CV. We don't require a cover letter but we'll ask you a question about our android app as part of the application questionnaire. This question should take no longer than 5 minutes to answer, so please factor in the extra time when applying.
We appreciate the time taken to prepare each application we receive. We do not use AI-assisted technology to review applications; every application is reviewed by a member of our recruitment team. Thank you for bearing with us during the screening process.
The closing date for applications is **Monday 26th October 2026.**
All roles at the Guardian are open for everybody to apply. It is important to us that you feel supported and comfortable throughout your recruitment process, in order to perform your best. Please let us know if there are any changes we could make to help your application, this includes providing documents in accessible formats or personalising the process to better support your needs. Please contact Anna Vipers on anna.vipers@theguardian.com to discuss further so we can work with you to support you through your application.
**Benefits at the Guardian**
You'll have 30 days of annual leave per year (plus bank holidays) with the option to purchase an additional 5 days. Our pension scheme is generous; if you contribute 5% then we will contribute 8-12% (depending on your age). We believe in giving back, which is why employees are given 2 volunteering days annually and the option of payroll giving. Season ticket loans are also available.
You are entitled to private healthcare, life cover, income protection, and eye tests. You can also opt in to dental insurance.
We have enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental leave policies in place. We also support our employees by offering an IVF, menopause, baby loss, and trans equality policy.
**Culture and wellbeing**
We want everyone to feel like they belong at the Guardian and we champion diversity of thought. Our various employee forums provide a platform to use their voice to foster an inclusive workplace. We became the first major media organisation to achieve B Corp status.
We offer tools to help you prioritise your wellbeing including access to our employee benefits platform which provides tailored support for health and wellbeing. In addition, we also offer free yoga and pilates classes. These run alongside our corporate gym membership and cycle to work scheme.
Our canteen has views overlooking the Regents Canal and caters for breakfast, lunch and dinner.
**Learning and development**
We encourage personal and professional growth. Employees have access to a broad range of tools and solutions, and we are happy to support the pursuit of professional qualifications through vocational courses and apprenticeships.
**We value honesty in your application.**
AI generated content must not be presented as your own work. Please review our guidance on the use of AI in your application here.

### ABOUT THE TEAM:
The Tide Security Engineering team is made up of three core areas: Product Security, Threat Detection & Response, and Identity.
**Product Security** (this role!) consists of application and cloud security experts. Their mission is to protect the products we build, covering everything from secure design reviews to threat modelling and penetration testing, ensuring security is embedded from the ground up.
**Threat Detection & Response** focuses on protecting the company by building a robust detection and automation platform. We’re proactive in our defence, constantly hacking ourselves to improve our security posture and staying ahead of emerging threats. Our goal is to make Tide resilient against the ever-evolving threat landscape.
**Identity** is responsible for managing Tide's staff identity platform, ensuring that access to systems and infrastructure is secure, seamless, and aligned with modern security practices. The team uses strategies like zero trust, multi-factor authentication, and granular role-based access controls to safeguard our internal operations.
While each area has its own focus, collaboration is key - it's why we share the same Slack channel and hold our standups together as one cohesive team, ensuring alignment and seamless communication across all security functions.
### ABOUT THE ROLE:
**As a Senior Product Security Engineer you’ll:**
* Regularly dive deep into mobile, web app technologies in order to understand feature development and proactively hunt for vulnerabilities
* Be proficient in securing cloud-native applications, ensuring that security best practices are applied consistently across our cloud environment
* Be proficient in threat modelling and guide developers in secure design principles to prevent vulnerabilities from being introduced in the first place
* Help remediate vulnerabilities through strategic initiatives, writing patches, or creating understandable and actionable vulnerability tickets.
* Be the subject matter expert across a wide range of security areas, particularly in Application Security.
* Make security invisible when possible, believing that gatekeeping and blocking product teams should be avoided in favour of enabling secure development.
* Mentor and coach junior engineers, sharing your knowledge to help raise the security bar across the organisation
* Leverage automation and security tools to seamlessly integrate security into our CI/CD pipelines, ensuring vulnerabilities are caught early without disrupting development.

* You have excellent spoken and written communication skills to articulate vulnerabilities clearly and persuasively, advocating for their remediation even when faced with competing production pressures.

* You’re comfortable writing proof-of-concept (POC) scripts to demonstrate your findings and their potential impact, as needed.

## About Tigris
Logistics still runs on emails, Excel and phone calls. Every company in the logistics chain keeps its own version of the truth, and billions of dollars move on data nobody can fully trust.
That’s about to change!
Tigris connects all those scattered systems into one live picture of vessels, cargo and schedules, so every company in the chain can work from data it can trust. On top of that, AI agents read the documents, watch the ships, predict what’s coming and make the calls people still make by hand today. It’s a mix of AI, data and real-world operations that almost nobody is building yet.
We’re starting in maritime, the hardest place to get it right, and building it for any company to run on. If you want to build something that doesn’t exist yet, this is the place.
## Why we’re hiring now
After three years of building, Tigris is live with its first customer and has a growing pipeline of logistics businesses behind it. We’re a small, hands-on team in the City of London, and we’re now hiring the people who will turn a working platform into a scaling business. This is our first Product Manager, so you’ll join early enough to shape how product works here, not just execute inside it.
## The role
We have a powerful platform, a live customer, and a large market that already knows it has this problem. What we need now is someone to own what we build and why.
As our Product Manager, you’ll turn customer needs and the company’s vision into a prioritised product roadmap, clear requirements and measurable outcomes. It’s a commercially minded product role inside a technical company: you’ll spend as much time with customers and operators as with engineers, working out how logistics businesses really run, where our building blocks create the most leverage, and what earns a place on the roadmap.
You’ll work closely with our COO and our Industry Engagement & Strategic Partnership Lead, who lead our customer relationships and industry network; our CTO, who owns the technical roadmap and architecture; and a Technical Program Manager who drives delivery. You own the what and the why; engineering owns how it’s built.
## What you’ll do
* Own the product roadmap and its milestones, deciding what we build next, what we leave out, and why, aligned with the technical roadmap our engineering team owns
* Own backlog prioritisation, deciding what the team works on first, with the Technical Program Manager running sequencing and delivery
* Talk to customers, prospects and operators on an ongoing basis, alongside our COO and Industry Engagement & Strategic Partnership Lead, to learn how their workflows really run, what holds them back and what they’d pay for
* Turn what you hear into clear product opportunities, each with a defined problem, user and measure of success
* Write product requirements and user stories that give engineering clear intent and leave them room to design the solution
* Define the scope of each feature as part of the requirements, and agree it with engineering so everyone knows what’s in and out before work starts
* Partner with our UI/UX designer to shape flows and interfaces that make complex system capabilities easy to use
* Own user acceptance testing (UAT): set the acceptance criteria, run testing with customers and users, and sign off that delivered work solves the problem it was built for
* Work hand in hand with engineering and our Technical Program Manager to keep scope, feasibility and delivery honest with each other. They own the architecture, sequencing, triage and release; you own intent, UAT and acceptance
* Lead the research on pricing, packaging and positioning for the modules you own, and make the recommendation
* Run POCs and lightweight pilots from start to finish, leading the customer side while engineering leads any integration or deployment work
* Own demos and customer workshops, delivered with our Industry Expert, and feed what you learn straight back into the roadmap
* Define and track the metrics that show whether what we shipped worked: adoption, retention and operational impact
* Lead launches end to end, from internal enablement to customer-facing documentation
## What we’re looking for
* Experience as a Product Manager on a technical B2B product, ideally one sold to operators rather than consumers
* A track record of taking products from an ambiguous problem space to shipped, adopted software
* Strong written communication: you create clarity, and you can make a case on paper
* Technical fluency: you don’t need to write code, but you’re comfortable discussing APIs, data models and system architecture with engineers
* Real customer curiosity: you go and find out rather than assume, and you’re as comfortable in ports, warehouses and control rooms as on calls
* Commercial instinct: you understand how the product makes money and design for it
* Comfort making decisions with incomplete information, and changing them when the evidence says so
* The ability to influence without authority across engineering, design, leadership and customers
## Nice to have, but not essential
* Background in logistics, supply chain, freight, maritime or operations technology
* Experience with platform or infrastructure products where the customer builds on top of you
* Exposure to data-heavy or algorithm-driven products (graph data, predictions, anomaly detection)
* Experience in an early-stage company where you built the product function
* A technical background (engineering, data or similar)
## Why join us
* Real ownership. Every role here makes an impact. As our first standalone Product Manager, you’ll define the product function and shape how we work.
* A hard, unsolved problem. We’re not building a feature. We’re building infrastructure that an entire industry can run on.
* Close to leadership. A small, hands-on team with direct access to leadership: your work is visible, and so is your impact.
* AI-native from day one. We use the best AI tools every day, so a small team can move fast and ship in weeks, not quarters.
## Compensation & benefits
* Competitive salary
* Private health & dental cover
* 25 days' holiday
* Enhanced parental leave
* Best-in-class hardware
* Extensive perks, including WeWork office benefits and regular team building
* Great culture & monthly socials
* Learning and development opportunities

Send your CV to careers@tigris.systems. Read the Candidate Hub for how we hire, then come back to this role.

## Build a Safer World.
TRM Labs provides AI-powered intelligence solutions that help public and private sector agencies investigate and disrupt crime. TRM's platforms enable investigators to trace illicit activity, build cases, and construct operating pictures of threat networks. Leading agencies and businesses worldwide rely on TRM to make the world safer and more secure.
## About the Role
Sextortion — extorting money or further imagery from victims, disproportionately minors, under threat of releasing explicit images — has been named a national emergency by the FBI and NCMEC, and financial sextortion cases have been directly linked to a rise in teen suicides. In parallel, CSAM distribution networks increasingly monetize through cryptocurrency, using crypto's speed and pseudonymity to move money across borders faster than any single agency can follow.
TRM's Severe Harms pod exists to close that gap. We fuse on-chain and off-chain intelligence to trace the financial rails behind this abuse, working alongside Law Enforcement and Government Partners, and TRM's financial-institution and exchange partners to identify offenders, disrupt activity, and support victim identification and safeguarding. It is some of the most consequential and difficult work at TRM.
As a **Severe Harms All-Source Investigator**, you will be one of the investigators running that flywheel every day — tracing the financial rails behind sextortion and CSAM monetization, building the target packages and legal-process returns that lead to disruption, and working cases from referral through to an actionable outcome.
This is an individual-contributor role for someone who wants to do the work directly, not manage it. You will build genuine casework skill on some of the most consequential and difficult material at TRM, with a manager and a Lead Investigator supporting your growth.
## The Impact You Will Have
* Work your caseload. Run point on target packages from referral to disruption: legal process → on-chain/off-chain fusion → targeting, on your own cases under normal review.
* Run all-source collection. Combine OSINT, link analysis, and direct engagement with subjects and sources to identify and attribute actors — not just trace the money.
* Build defensible, actionable outputs. Every attribution write-up and legal-process return you produce should hold up when tested by Law Enforcement and Government Partners, or a court — with growing independence over time.
* Map networks, not just events. Build a picture of how a network actually operates, rather than a catalogue of isolated indicators.
* Use AI to accelerate your own casework. Apply it where it genuinely speeds up or sharpens your work, and know where human judgment has to stay in the loop given the sensitivity of the material.
* Partner across the ecosystem. Work directly with legal, engineering, and external partners on the specific leads and referrals in front of you.
* Practice victim-centered, trauma-informed investigative work, and follow TRM's protocols for evidence handling, escalation, and mandatory reporting.
* Take care of yourself and your teammates. Actively manage your own content exposure and psychological well-being, and know when and how to ask for support.
## What We're Looking For
* You are an operator. 3–5 years of relevant investigative or casework experience — illicit-finance, financial-crime, cybercrime, trust & safety, all-source intelligence, OSINT, or direct human-source engagement, or a comparable law-enforcement/intelligence-adjacent background. You have taken a body of information and driven it to a real outcome, not just written a report about it.
* Real collection capability, whether that's hands-on experience building or adapting tools to pull signal from open web, social, and forum sources, or direct experience engaging subjects and sources yourself. Ideally you've done some of both, but real strength in one is enough.
* You know how to work a case with other people, not just alone. You can point to investigations you've co-run with another investigator, or handed off cleanly without losing momentum.
* You're comfortable working to someone else's clock. You've delivered real answers under RFI-style pressure — a partner or requester needing something in hours or days, not on a self-paced research timeline — and can point to examples.
* Genuine interest in, and some exposure to, child exploitation, sextortion, or closely adjacent investigative work, including CT or Serious Organised Crime. We will teach you the ecosystem specifics; we are looking for the instinct and resilience for this material, plus at least some track record adjacent to it.
* AI fluency (required). You use AI in your own work today and have a clear, honest view of where it helps and where it does not — especially given the sensitivity of this material.
* Working knowledge of legal process — subpoenas, warrants, preservation requests — or a fast willingness to learn it. You do not need to be a lawyer; you need to understand how high-quality investigative documentation supports downstream action.
* Solid written communication. You can produce a clear, defensible written package under review.
* Sound judgment with difficult material. The maturity to work with emotionally demanding content without it compromising your judgment or your well-being.
* Fully remote, US- or UK-based. Expect occasional travel, unevenly distributed, with periodic DC-based working sessions.
## Nice-to-Have
* Crypto or on-chain experience. A genuine advantage, but we teach on-chain tradecraft — we cannot teach the instinct built from years investigating crimes against children.
* Sextortion/CSAM-ecosystem familiarity. Direct experience with financial sextortion schemes, CSAM distribution networks, or platform-based grooming and extortion patterns will shorten your ramp considerably, but the team knows this ecosystem well and can bring you up to speed on it.
## Vetting
Given the sensitivity of the material and data handled, successful completion of an enhanced background check is required as a condition of employment.
## About the Team
* The Severe Harms pod operates within TRM's Primary Intelligence organization, alongside the other threat categories comprised of threat intelligence analysts, on-chain investigators and data scientists.
* Distributed team with an async-first approach via Slack and Notion, plus structured syncs for alignment.
* High autonomy, high standards, low bureaucracy — you work directly with engineers, analysts, legal counterparts, and the partners and customers who depend on the team's output.
## Team Operating Rhythms
* Weekly 1:1 with your manager
* Weekly team sync covering active work, throughput, and escalations
* 6-week performance pulse check-in
* Quarterly career-pathing conversation
* Mandatory wellness check-ins and access to specialized counseling/EAP resources, on a standing cadence
* Primary time-zone overlap: US Eastern / Central
* Surge availability expected during time-sensitive referral and disruption windows
## **Application Instructions**
If you’re interested in joining TRM, we encourage you to apply directly. Every application is reviewed by our Talent team.
Before applying, review the job description carefully and highlight the experience and impact that best demonstrate the required qualifications. Please also provide thoughtful and accurate answers to the application questions, as these will be used to evaluate your skills and qualifications for the role.
If you send your resume directly to someone at TRM, we can’t guarantee it will reach the appropriate hiring team. Applying directly is the best way to ensure your application will be considered.
## **Interviewing with TRM**
Our process is designed to understand how you think, solve problems, and deliver impact, while allowing you to evaluate TRM. Most interview processes include a case study, an AI skills assessment, and a Leadership Principles interview.
* **Recruiter Intro:** Qualifications, motivations, and alignment with the role.
* **Hiring Manager:** Deep dive into your relevant experience, skills, and impact.
* **First Round:** 1–2 interviews focused on the skills most critical to the role.
* **Final Round:** Hands-on case study. This is usually a panel-style session where we go deeper into your craft, problem-solving, and alignment with TRM.
* **References:** Former colleagues who can provide insight into your work and impact.
* **Offer:** Congrats! Your recruiter will present the offer and compensation details.
* **Welcome to TRM:** We're excited to build a safer world with you!
Your recruiter will share your specific interview plan and preparation guidance along the way.
## **AI Fluency at TRM**
AI fluency is a baseline expectation at TRM.
We believe AI meaningfully changes how top performers operate. We expect every team member to use AI to accelerate and reimagine their craft, not just automate surface tasks.
At TRM, AI fluency means you are among the top 10 percent of operators in your function in how you apply AI to:
* Accelerate repeatable workflows
* Structure and solve problems
* Improve output quality
* Increase speed and leverage
You will be evaluated on applied AI fluency during the interview process.
## **Life at TRM**
We are building a safer world. That promise shows up in how we work every day.
TRM moves FAST. We are a high-velocity, high-ownership team that expects clarity, follow-through, and impact. People who thrive here are energized by hard problems, experimentation, and continuous feedback. If something takes months elsewhere, it will ship here in days.
Our work sits at the intersection of AI, national security, and fighting crime. The problems are complex, the stakes are real, and the environment evolves quickly. The pace and intensity of the work reflect the importance of the mission. As a result, the way we operate requires a high level of ownership, adaptability, collaboration, and creative problem-solving.
At TRM, you should expect:
* Priorities and targets to change quickly
* Operating with a high degree of ambiguity
* A high level of personal ownership and accountability
* Close collaboration across teams and functions
* Frequent, high-touch communication
* Creative problem-solving and out-of-the-box thinking
* A pace that rewards urgency, adaptability, and outcomes
This environment is energizing for people who enjoy building, solving hard problems, and making progress in situations that are not always fully defined. It also requires thriving in ambiguity, adjusting course as new information emerges, and maintaining focus and positivity in a fast-moving and intense environment.
We also recognize that this style of operating is not for everyone. If you are primarily optimizing for predictability or a consistently balanced workload, we encourage you to use the interview process to pressure-test whether this environment is truly the right fit. We want teammates who thrive here, not just survive here.
If you are excited by meaningful problems, motivated by ambitious goals, and energized by working alongside mission-driven colleagues, there is a good chance you will find TRM to be an exceptional place to grow and contribute.
## **Leadership Principles**
We hire and grow against three leadership principles. They’re the standards for how we operate, treat each other, and make decisions.
* Impact-Oriented Trailblazer: We put customers first and move with speed, focus, and adaptability. We treat every plan like an experiment – test, ship, measure, and iterate quickly.
* Master Craftsperson: We care deeply about our craft. We balance speed with high standards, own outcomes end‐to‐end, and invest in getting better everyday.
* Inspiring Colleague: We add clarity and energy, not noise. We bring humility, candor, and a one‐team mindset — giving and receiving feedback to make the team stronger.
## **Join our Mission**
At TRM, we care deeply about our craft. We are looking for individuals who want their work to matter, who experiment with speed and rigor, and who take pride in building a safer world for billions of people. If you’re excited by TRM’s mission but don’t check every box, we encourage you to apply — we hire for slope, judgment, and the will to learn fast.
TRM is a Series C company with $220M in total funding, backed by Goldman Sachs, Bessemer, Y Combinator, Thoma Bravo, and others. Headquartered in San Francisco, TRM operates as a distributed-first company with hubs in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New York, Washington D.C., London, and Singapore.
## **Privacy Policy and Additional Information**
By submitting your application, you agree to allow TRM Labs to process your personal information in accordance with our Privacy Policy.
We collect the information you provide (such as your resume, work history, and contact details) solely for the purpose of evaluating your candidacy for current and future roles at TRM.

In this role, you'll leverage blockchain analytics, cyber threat intelligence, and cryptocurrency attribution to trace ransomware proceeds, identify threat actor infrastructure, and generate actionable intelligence that supports investigations, disruption efforts, and evidentiary workflows.
This is not a people-management role. We're looking for an experienced analyst who can independently lead complex investigations, develop high-confidence assessments, uncover novel attribution, and elevate the team's tradecraft through technical expertise, mentorship, and example.
You should be equally comfortable tracing funds across blockchains, identifying laundering and cash-out infrastructure, correlating technical, financial, and behavioral signals, and synthesizing fragmented data into clear, defensible intelligence that enables internal and external partners to make informed operational decisions. **The Impact You Will Have:**
* Produce impactful finished intelligence on ransomware actors, affiliates, facilitators, and laundering pathways, including actor profiles, lead packages, attribution assessments, and operational reporting suitable for investigative, executive, and partner audiences.
* Lead complex end-to-end blockchain investigations from initial seed indicators such as victim payment addresses, deposit addresses, transactions, exchange exposure, infrastructure leads, or IP-linked activity through to full attribution and actionable recovery or disruption opportunities.
* Trace ransomware-related funds across multiple blockchains, bridges, mixers, peel chains, and nested services, identifying controllers, counterparties, cash-out services, and recovery touchpoints.
* Correlate on-chain activity with OSINT, threat intelligence, attribution partner data, and off-chain identity or infrastructure signals to build a complete picture of adversary behavior within the broader cybercrime ecosystem.
* Own investigative workstreams from discovery through validation, escalation, and written production, including drafting intelligence products that are source-cited, auditable, and operationally useful.
* Support TRM’s ransomware asset recovery mission by surfacing high-quality leads, identifying seizure or freeze opportunities, and helping partners move quickly before funds are off-ramped.
* Drive analytical leadership across active ransomware investigations by prioritizing work, maintaining rigorous standards, and mentoring other analysts without formal people management responsibilities.
* Partner closely with internal and external stakeholders, including investigators, threat intelligence teammates, product teams, and public-sector or private-sector partners, to ensure analytical outputs reflect real investigative tradecraft and support cross-functional operations.
* Help strengthen TRM’s ransomware coverage by contributing new attribution, refining investigative methodologies, and improving repeatable workflows for lead generation and asset recovery support.
* Support external briefings, customer or partner engagements, and capability-building sessions where ransomware tracing, attribution, and recovery tradecraft must be explained clearly and credibly.
## **What Success Looks Like:**
* You generate meaningful attribution, investigative leads, and recovery opportunities in ransomware cases where the answers are not obvious, and the financial trail is deliberately obscured.
* You consistently produce finished intelligence that partners trust and use in operational, investigative, and strategic contexts.
* Your work helps TRM and its partners move faster on high-priority ransomware activity without sacrificing rigor, auditability, or defensibility.
* You improve team capability by mentoring peers, refining tradecraft, and strengthening repeatable workflows for ransomware investigations and asset recovery support.
* You help make blockchain-enabled financial intelligence a differentiator in how TRM understands, attributes, and disrupts ransomware activity across the cybercrime ecosystem.
## **What We’re Looking For:**
* **5-8+ years of professional experience** in blockchain intelligence, crypto investigations, cybercrime analysis, threat intelligence, financial crime investigations, or a comparable senior analytical role.
* **Blockchain tracing expertise** — Deep hands-on experience tracing funds across multiple blockchains and through laundering or obfuscation techniques such as mixers, chain-hopping, bridges, peel chains, and layered cash-out behavior.
* **Extensive investigative tradecraft** — Demonstrated ability to independently run complex investigations and synthesize findings into clear written intelligence products, including investigative assessments, lead packages, fund-flow analysis, and attribution reporting.
* **Ransomware domain expertise** — including a deep understanding of the broader cybercrime ecosystem and the relationships among ransomware operators, affiliates, initial access brokers, malware developers, laundering networks, and cash-out services.
* **Excellent written and verbal communication** — especially the ability to turn technically complex tracing findings into understandable, actionable intelligence for government and private-sector audiences.
* **Judgment and execution** — Strong judgment, curiosity, and the ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving, high-stakes environment where timing matters and outputs must still stand up to scrutiny.
* **AI fluency** — Experience leveraging AI tools and large language models (LLMs) to accelerate research, surface insights, and augment analytical workflows, with the ability to critically evaluate AI-generated outputs for accuracy and relevance.
## **Preferred Qualifications:**
* Experience in government, national security, law enforcement, incident response, or mature private-sector investigative or threat intelligence programs.
* Familiarity with OSINT, cybercrime infrastructure research, and cross-domain analytical methods that combine blockchain activity with off-chain signals and adversary behavior.
* Comfort with modern investigative tooling, including AI and structured data environments such as TRM, Maltego, Palantir, or similar platforms.
* Experience conducting HUMINT collection and engaging threat actors via dark web forums and encrypted messaging platforms.
* Experience mentoring peers, shaping analytical standards, or improving investigative workflows without formal people management.
* Advanced practitioner-level knowledge of crypto forensics concepts such as manual demixing, smart contracts, bridges, Ethereum- and TRON-based investigations, and OSINT-based data extraction.
* Recognized subject matter depth, broader organizational influence, and a track record of shaping methodology or high-priority investigative strategy beyond individual case execution.

* Weekly team syncs to align targeting priorities and review disruption opportunities
* Daily async standups via Slack on active work, returns, and target packages in flight
* Primary time zone overlap: US Eastern / Central
* All output documented in Notion and TRM’s investigative tools
* Surge availability expected during time-sensitive disruption windows

**Job Title:** Senior Quantum Scientist (AMO) **Salary:** Band E S1 £58,346 **Location:** RAL - Oxfordshire **Contract Type:** Permanent **Hours:** Full Time *(We understand the importance of work-life balance, and are happy to discuss the possibility of flexible working with applicants)*
Come and do the kind of science that made you want to become a scientist. Explore the unknown and get to grips with the biggest challenges in Big Science. And, alongside world class engineers, technicians and technologists, use everything you've learnt to find real-answers that shape society and improve lives.
Put simply, discover the kind of impact you can make when you work with some of the best facilities and brightest scientists in the world.
**About Us:**
As part of the UK’s National Quantum Technologies Programme (NQTP), UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) is leading a programme to establish a National Quantum Computing Centre (NQCC). This includes a commitment of £93m over 5 years, dedicated to drive development in the field of Quantum Computing and to place the UK at the forefront of the field.
Our primary purpose is to fill a key gap in the research and innovation landscape addressing the challenge of scaling quantum computing.
**About the Role:**
The NAQC team’s mission is to:
• Design, build and deploy cutting-edge open-source NAQC hardware. • Build capability to act as UK’s trusted authority on NAQC. • Convene the UK NAQC community and train the future NAQC workforce.
As Senior Quantum Scientist (AMO), you will work as part of the NQCC's Neutral Atom Quantum Computing (NAQC) team. The role is suitable for candidates with strong experimental or engineering skills and experience who are looking to develop into system-level roles. You will contribute to development and deployment of NQCC’s open-source quantum computing platforms to support our technology roadmap, integrating components into scalable quantum computers and pushing the boundaries of platform performance in the UK.
The role offers the opportunity to influence the technical direction of the national NAQC programme whilst remaining closely engaged with hands-on experimental and engineering work in the lab.
**Key Responsibilities:**
System and Sub-System Development:
• Design, develop, assemble, and optimise neutral atom quantum computing sub-systems (e.g. QPU, laser systems, control systems). • Develop and run experiments to characterise performance and improve qubit fidelity, stability, and scalability. • Contribute to the integration of sub-systems into full-stack quantum computing platforms.
System-Level Planning and Architecture:
• Contribute to system-level design, including requirements, interfaces, and performance targets. • Support the development of scaling strategies and system architectures. • Explore trade-offs across subsystems and their impact on overall system performance.
Open Architecture and System Blueprinting:
• Contribute to the development of open-architecture policy & vision documents, system definitions, and system performance reports. • Ensure work is documented to support reproducibility and knowledge transfer.
Collaboration and Ecosystem Engagement:
• Work closely with internal teams across the NQCC (hardware, software, applications). • Collaborate with external partners including academia, industry, and national laboratories. • Participate in site visits, technical exchanges, workshops, and community engagement activities, contributing to the development of the UK quantum computing ecosystem and supply chain.
Technical Leadership and Contribution:
• Take ownership of technical areas or sub-systems. • Provide technical input into project direction, planning, and delivery. • Influence internal and external collaborators through clear communication of technical results.
Dissemination:
• Publish results in peer-reviewed journals. • Present work at conferences, workshops, and internal reviews.
The successful candidate will demonstrate a pragmatic, delivery-focused approach and work effectively in a collaborative, multidisciplinary environment. They will have strong attention to detail and the ability to interpret and clearly communicate technical performance data at both component and system levels. They will be comfortable developing quantum technologies in a laser lab.
**Person Specification:**
We offer significant development opportunities at the NQCC, but as a starting point you should be able to demonstrate some of the following;
*The below criteria will be scored during Shortlisting (S), Interview (I) or both (S&I).*
• Educated to a PhD - level (or equivalent experience) in a physics, engineering, computing or a related discipline. (S&I) • Strong technical knowledge and understanding of the principles of quantum computing and / or closely related quantum technologies. (S&I) • Experience working with neutral atom quantum computing systems & hardware, or significant experience in a closely related quantum technology which may include publication. * Revenue Integrity — Act as the gatekeeper of data hygiene and opportunity data, partnering with GTM and Finance on audits for revenue recognition, financial reporting, and forecasting.
* Insights & Enablement — Analyze deal performance and market trends to develop new sales motions, deal levers, and training materials that increase sales velocity and reduce business risk, in partnership with the Pricing and Field Enablement teams.

* 4+ years of experience in deal desk, pricing, quote-to-cash, contract management, or a related Revenue Operations or Sales Operations function within the technology sector.
* A proven record of partnering effectively with Sales and cross-functional teams to move complex deals forward.
* Demonstrated experience in project management and process improvement.
* A collaborative team member who consistently delivers excellent sales support.
* A resourceful self-starter with strong critical-thinking and creative problem-solving skills.
* You think naturally about operational implications and downstream impact.
* You thrive in fast-paced, high-growth environments and operate effectively amid change and ambiguity.
## Nice to have
* Hands-on experience with Salesforce CPQ (or a comparable CPQ platform)
* A track record of using AI or automation to improve operational workflows.

At Verda, we're building a full-stack AI cloud, covering everything from data centers and hardware to our own cloud platform that the world's leading AI teams use to do serious AI work.
We strive to make a positive mark on the world through the infrastructure we build and give leading teams a service they can truly depend on. Headquartered in Helsinki, we operate globally with offices in London and San Francisco.
Join Verda while it’s still being built - not once it’s finished.
About the role
As Head of Product you own product direction and priorities for the cloud platform: which problems deserve our attention, what success looks like, and what we should stop doing. Your scope spans the experience that brings our cloud together: console, APIs, SDKs and CLI, identity and access, billing, and the shared capabilities behind our products.
Product managers report to you, and you’ll build out the product team as we grow. Engineering leads across our products align with you on product questions. You take an active part in shaping product decisions and agree priorities and sequencing with engineering leaders, who own technical direction. You’ll work closely with Design, Data Analytics, Sales, Customer Support, and Product Marketing.
We're looking for someone who knows this market, stays close to customers, and can turn that understanding into clear product priorities. You'll help us improve the platform, develop new capabilities, and grow the business by making Verda a product customers choose and keep using.
Your responsibilities
Set clear product goals: Translate company strategy into a small number of measurable cloud outcomes, then connect those outcomes to team roadmaps. Give teams enough clarity to make good decisions themselves.
Stay close to customers and the market: Build a continuous loop of customer conversations, usage data, support feedback, and competitive research. Understand why people choose us, where they get stuck, and why they leave.
Prioritise aggressively: Make the case for what comes next and what waits. Revisit assumptions as evidence changes, while keeping teams focused on stable goals. Make the commercial case for building, buying, or integrating capabilities with engineering.
Own the business questions: Evaluate target users, demand, differentiation, pricing and packaging, and the economics of the opportunities we pursue. Work with commercial teams to turn those choices into a product customers adopt and pay for.
Build out and lead the product team: Shape how product management works at Verda, and help leadership and teams see what good product work looks like.
Stay involved through delivery: Turn opportunities into clear problem statements, scope, and success criteria. Work with engineering to sequence releases, expose dependencies, resolve trade-offs, and act on risks early. Track results during and after launch, and change course when they fall short.
Improve the whole customer journey: Work with Design and engineering to make the platform work well for people and agents, from discovering capabilities and deploying workloads to managing access, understanding failures, and controlling spend. Partner with Product Marketing on launches, and use adoption, retention, usage, and revenue to assess the outcome.
Use AI to multiply your impact: Make agents and AI tools part of how you research, analyse, prototype, and communicate. Keep improving your own workflows and share what works with the people around you.
Your key competencies
Direct product experience on an inference or AI developer platform, GPU cloud, or AI training infrastructure. You understand the customers, competitors, buying decisions, and economics of this industry, and have a clear view of where it’s heading.
A numerical, data-driven approach to product management. You define success with concrete metrics, track them, and use them to make decisions.
Broad product and business judgement, and a real interest in engaging with users. You can connect a platform-wide strategy to the details of an individual customer problem.
Good product taste and a track record of making difficult prioritisation decisions and improving measurable customer or commercial outcomes.
Experience building or leading a product team, and driving change in an organisation that is still learning what product management means.
Strong execution skills. You turn ambiguous goals into scoped work, coordinate across teams, and follow through on commitments.
Clear writing, good listening, and the ability to influence strong technical colleagues and senior leadership.
Hands-on experience with AI tools and agentic workflows, including what agents need to use a cloud platform successfully. Some of our users are people, others are agents, and you can turn the needs of both into concrete product decisions.
Nice to have
A background in engineering or technical founding
Experience improving a self-service developer product from first use through paid adoption and expansion
Why Verda
Cash and equity compensation along with local benefits.
40+ nationalities, with 6 different ones on the management team.
A real chance to make an impact and work alongside world class engineers, researchers, and partners across the global AI ecosystem.
Practicalities
Work mode: Hybrid in London (UK) or Helsinki (Finland), or remote from other country. We also offer relocation support if you’d like to move to Helsinki or London.
Employment type: Full time and permanent
What's next
We're building fast and this role needs the right person behind it. There's no artificial deadline, but when we find who we're looking for, we move. If this sounds like your next move, apply now.
Please submit your application through our Careers page. We don't accept applications sent by email.

## Grow Actemium’s automation business across Nottingham, building trusted client relationships and winning high-value projects, with up to £80,000, bonus and excellent benefits.
📍 **Nottingham** | 💼 *Permanent, Full‐time* | 🕒 *Flexible Working* 💰 ***Up to £80,000 p.a. (DOE)*** ***+ Bonus + Benefits* | 🚗 *EV Car Scheme* | 💷 *Share Scheme* | 🏥 *Healthcare***
**Actemium Automation Nottingham**, part of **VINCI Energies**, is seeking a Business Development Manager to grow our automation services and solutions within manufacturing, process and regulated sectors. You will be responsible for developing new client relationships, managing strategic accounts and supporting commercial growth across the region. This role combines technical understanding of industrial automation with commercial acumen and will suit an experienced, commercially focused professional comfortable engaging with senior stakeholders.
## **The Role**
* Identify, pursue and win new business opportunities for Actemium’s automation, controls and systems integration services.
* Develop and maintain strong relationships with existing and prospective clients, acting as the primary commercial contact and trusted advisor.
* Lead proposal development, including preparing commercial bids, quotations, statements of work and value propositions in collaboration with technical teams.
* Manage the sales pipeline and forecast revenue to achieve regional growth targets and business plan objectives.
* Work closely with engineering, project management and delivery teams to ensure commercial commitments align with technical scope and delivery capability.
* Represent Actemium at client meetings, industry events and conferences to raise our profile and generate leads.
* Negotiate commercial terms and contractual arrangements, ensuring company policies and risk controls are applied.
* Contribute to continuous improvement of sales processes, CRM usage and marketing initiatives.
## **About You**
* Proven track record in business development, sales or account management within industrial automation, controls, engineering or related sectors.
* Solid understanding of systems like PLC, SCADA, HMI and MES, with the confidence to work closely with technical teams.
* Strong commercial and negotiation skills with experience preparing bids, commercial terms and contractual documentation.
* Excellent communication and presentation skills; able to influence senior client contacts and internal teams.
* Self‐motivated, able to manage a sales pipeline, prioritise activity and work to targets.
* Proficient with CRM systems and standard office tools (MS Office).
* Full UK driving licence and willingness to travel to client sites across the region.
**Desirable:** Experience working within VINCI Energies, an understanding of regulated sectors (food, pharmaceutical, energy, chemical) or familiarity with procurement and tender processes for industrial projects.
## **What We Offer**
* Competitive salary, annual bonus, pension and comprehensive benefits package.
* Company share scheme, EV car scheme and healthcare provision.
* Flexible and hybrid working arrangements where operationally possible.
* Ongoing professional development, training and clear progression opportunities within VINCI Energies.
* Supportive team culture and the chance to work on high‐value, technically interesting projects.
---
**About Actemium Automation Nottingham**
We deliver safe, sustainable and innovative automation solutions to industrial clients. As part of VINCI Energies, we combine local agility with global capability. We are an equal opportunities employer and welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds.
**How to apply**
Please submit your CV and a covering statement detailing relevant experience and why you’re interested in this role. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview and a commercial assessment. We welcome applications from all suitably qualified candidates; however please note that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK at the time of application and throughout their employment.

## Surf Interface Lead Engineer Services
**Comsip**, a subsidiary of **VINCI Energies Oil & Gas**, specializes in providing **highly qualified technical resources** to support the most ambitious industrial projects around the world.
**Our mission for over 75 years** : to support the largest operators and engineering companies in the successful delivery of their complex projects, by providing key skills in **Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Operations and Maintenance**.
With more than **120 experts available worldwide**, Comsip operates with a **responsible and sustainable** approach, in perfect alignment with the **values of the VINCI Energies group**.
**Job Title:** Surf Interface Lead Engineer Services
**Sector:** Oil & Gas
**Start Date:** January 2027
**Duration:** 1 year minimum to 3 years
**Renewable:** Yes
**Location:** United Kingdom, London
**Status:** Residential
**Languages:** Fluent English
**MISSIONS CONTEXT**
The Service Provider will:
•be responsible for all Interface activities related to the Venus project, for the SURF scope
•supervise all interfaces exchanges between the SURF EPC and the other Contractors (SPS, FPSO, Drilling)
•manage all CPI to be delivered by other parties to SURF Contractor and SURF Contractor items to be delivered to other contractors and ensure proper and timely handover of these items between the different contractors.
**ACTIVITIES**
· To provide high level support services to ensure compliance with the Company Ethics and “Code of Conduct” policy, promote and enforce the Anti-Corruption Program within the Project
· To ensure adequate execution and supervision of all interface activities between SURF contractor and the other contractors
· To follow up all interface activities performed by SURF Contractor and ensure completeness and timely update of the interface register
· To ensure timely issuance by SURF Contractor of interface deliverables and interface data to other parties
· To ensure SURF Contractor compliance with the interface battery limit and the interface design data
· To propose solutions and ensure resolution and timely close-out of technical interfaces between SURF Contractor and other contractors
· To organize and follow-up technical workshops between SURF Contractor and other contractors
· To highlight immediately any deviation and inadequate designs impacting SURF contractor or any other contractor
· To ensure the adequate and timely preparation of SURF contractor items delivery to other contractors
· To ensure proper handover of SURF contractor items to other parties
· To ensure adequate and timely preparation and handover of CPIs delivered to SURF Contractor
· To ensure timely mobilization of other contractors’ personnel on SURF yards or SURF vessels
· To set up and manage the interface control system (New Prodom module) for the SURF package
· To support the Project Interface Manager and the SURF manager on interfaces and CPIs management
· To support the SURF technical teams as and when necessary, and obtain their support on all interfaces and CPIs deliveries
· To gather lessons learned and provide feedback to TotalEnergies entities when necessary
**HSE Role & Responsibilities**
· Adhere to Project H3SE&Q Site Instructions and Policies.
· Report anomalies, incidents, near misses to HSE.
· Demonstrate leadership in HSE behaviors, implementation and reporting.
· Shall comply with TotalEnergies' HSE programs (Golden Rules, Our lives First...)
**CONTEXT & ENVIRONMENT**
The Venus project for TotalEnergies is an ultra-deepwater development (~3,000 m water depth), producing oil through subsea production systems tied back to an FPSO in Namibia. It is designed to process 160,000 bbl./d of oil with advanced systems to manage large volumes of associated gas, which will be re-injected to maintain reservoir pressure. The development includes multiple wells, subsea production systems, extensive SURF infrastructure, and complex tie-in connection activities requiring precise interface management between SPS, SURF, and FPSO systems.
International and multi-cultural environment with multiple Contractors and fabrication sites worldwide. With high H3SE requirements and focus.
**QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE REQUIRED**
• Qualification: Master’s degree in engineering,
• Experience within project: at least 10 years in same or equivalent position with strong experience in deepwater oil projects (EPCI in execution phase). Very strong SURF experience and technical experience with SPS and FPSO scopes (risers’ / umbilicals hook-ups, pre-commissioning). Work with key industry SURF EPCI contractors.
• Experience with TotalEnergies systems and specifications
Additional features:
• Positive, constructive, proactive and pragmatic mindset.
• Ability to work within large teams with other parties (EPCI operator SURF team and other packages, Contractors, suppliers, HQ technical teams, etc).
• Previous experience within a complex and multicultural working environment.

## Flow Assurance Engineering Services
**Comsip**, a subsidiary of **VINCI Energies Oil & Gas**, specializes in providing **highly qualified technical resources** to support the most ambitious industrial projects around the world.
**Our mission for over 75 years** : to support the largest operators and engineering companies in the successful delivery of their complex projects, by providing key skills in **Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Operations and Maintenance**.

**Job Title:** Flow Assurance Engineering Services
**Sector:** Oil & Gas
**Start Date :** October 2026
**Duration:** 1 year minimum to 4 years
**Renewable:** Yes
**Location:** United Kingdom, London with periodic travel to France (Paris)
**Status:** Residential
**Languages:** English
**MISSION/SERVICES DIMENSIONS**
The Service Provider will be responsible for all the flow assurance engineering activities related to the Venus project.
The service Provider shall oversee all Flow Assurance subjects with regards to Sub-Surfaces, Topsides, SURF and SPS equipment packages of the Venus Field Development Project during the EPSCC phase and supervise the studies performed by the EPSCC SURF Contractor and anticipate/supervise need for additional third-party engineering checks on critical items.
The Service Holder will report to the SURF Technical Manager and support primarily the SURF team and liaise with other project teams (SPS, FPSO & Field Operations).
**ACTIVITIES**
· Promote & comply in all activities with applicable safety instructions and other company H3SE&Q rules, implement and control H3SE rules and requirements within his area of responsibility. Ensure all flowlines technical documentation and SURF Contractor activities comply with H3SE&Q requirements and highlight any potential deviations. Ensure safe working practices are implemented along all phases of project.
· Provide high level support services to ensure compliance with regards to the Company Ethics and “Code of Conduct” policy, promote and enforce the Anti-Corruption Program within the Project
· Ensure adequate execution and supervision of Flow Assurance studies and provide timely and adequate Flow Assurance assistance to the FPSO, SURF and SPS packages in cases of technical and / or design conflicts/problems to ensure equipment specification meets the project requirements. The field being a very deepwater oil field with a high GOR content it is expected that the Service Holder will be proactively suggesting ideas and taking decisions to solve the flow assurance challenges that are expected to happen throughout the different project phases.
· Liaise with Reservoir, well performance, Field Operations, Process and Subsea engineering teams to update them of the changes in Flow assurance requirements that may impact on the project as well as to assist them in any studies or technical queries.
· Perform Flow Assurance studies ensuring they are validated when required, providing timely information of any modifications which may arise during the project Flow Assurance review studies.
· Participate in operations engineering of the project, including the definition of main principles, policy, and operating means.
· Follow the day-to-day progress of engineering activities related to Flow assurance by the EPSCC SURF contractor and EPFS SPS contractor. Validate and guarantee the technical expertise of the Flow Assurance studies and the optimization of the Flow Assurance design. Provide technical assistance in decision-making due to any proposed Flow Assurance changes and recommend solutions to optimize the existing designs.
· Define, develop, issue and maintain all necessary technical documentation related to the flow assurance activities. Support and participate in the development and maintenance of Project Management main documents (SOR, FDP, PEP, PQP, Risks, etc.),
· Ensure follow-up / review / validation of progress performed by SURF EPSCC Contractor and its Suppliers with regards to his/her disciplines and analyze/report drifts that could occur and propose remedial solutions.
· The Service Holder shall proactively provide alternative designs or technical solutions whenever required, accounting for the various constraints of project packages, such as reducing as much as possible the preservation and start-up phases, etc...
· Supervise and control the detailed engineering by timely reviewing the disciplines-related documentation issued by SURF EPSCC Contractor (technical documentation / queries / derogation requests...), in order to ensure compliance with Project Specifications and Procedures (when applicable), international norms and standards with the objective to ensure respect of the schedule and to optimize costs without impacting required level of Quality and Safety
· Raise consequently necessary comments and highlight unsafe design, deviations, unacceptable / unjustified design choices, constructability issues
· Ensure that his/her work is in line with flow assurance specialists of Company Headquarters,
· Liaise with other package teams (SPS, FPSO) for interface matters with the support of Interface Managers and leads,
· Organize and participate in Project Reviews,
· Assist the production team in preparation for facilities start-up (operating procedures and guidelines)
· Assist and support the SURF Technical Manager and the Subsea Manager on all aspects of the flow assurance activities related to project execution and contracts management, and with the relations with Partners
· Coordinate with other Team Members including the SURF contract engineer for the follow-up of correspondence and contract activities throughout the Project Execution
· Assist the field operation team for preparation and optimization of start-up, shut-downs, restarts, steady state and transient sequences and operations.
· Take part in acceptance of certain items of equipment on constructor premises and is involved in commissioning and start-up operations.
· Any other responsibilities/activities within the limit of the Service Holder capabilities.
· Participate in / support the Final Thermal Performance Tests and well start-up, assisting, as necessary, the Field Operation Team during all the offshore work campaigns.
· Gather ‘lessons learnt’ and provide feedback to the client entities as required. Assist in the formalization of the close-out report
**CONTEXT & ENVIRONMENT**
The activity takes place in the context of Project Execution Phase of a major very large ultra Deep Water greenfield Project in Namibia. The Venus Project is a multidisciplinary team that coordinates the development studies managed by the client One Tech on the Deep-Water discoveries of offshore Namibia Block 2913B.
The technical challenges the Project will face are the reservoirs development and management, the subsea production/injection system definition in a challenging environment.
The Venus Project will be developed with the objectives to maximize economical results by optimizing the reserves, the schedule, reducing the costs and the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emission, while maintaining the technical quality of the installations, with high H3SE requirements and focus.
**QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE REQUIRED**
· Qualification: BSc in Engineering or equivalent
· Professional Experience: minimum 15 years’ experience in flow assurance engineering studies during detailed engineering for a deep-water oil production offshore field
· Skills required: Strong knowledge and ability to run Olga
**OTHER OBSERVATIONS**
· Very strong understanding of flow assurance challenges in ultra deepwater environment for high pressure / high temperature oil production. Very good expertise and production loops shutdown and re-start challenges
· Good knowledge of relevant codes (DNV), and preferably of the client General Specifications, procedures and policies.
· Previous experience with Major SURF Contractors and/or Operators during project execution for deepwater project or specialist engineering companies
· Positive, constructive, proactive and pragmatic mindset.
· Proactive, autonomous.
· Previous experience within complex multicultural working environment.

Joining us means the assurance of becoming part of a large group within a human-sized company!

· To propose actions for use of the SURF contract HSE Incentive scheme
· To analyze incidents, perform investigations, organize feedback to management and personnel and propose mitigations and way forward to improve situations and avoid re-occurrence
· To ensure that the safety reviews are conducted in a timely and proper manner to comply with Project H3SE targets
· To participate, as far as possible, to site HSE visits, premob reviews, audit... and prepare Package management HSE visits.
· To ensure actions from reviews, audits, etc. (external and internal) are implemented and completed
· To define and implement H3SE training plan for COMPANY SURF team and ensure adequate H3SE training of SURF Contractor and its subcontractors’ teams
· To support the package manager and Project H3SEQ Manager on all H3SE matters
· To ensure readiness of all H3SE documentation and follow-up as necessary with all parties, including Local Authorities when required
· To gather ‘lessons learnt’ and provide feedback to the client entities as required

The VENUS deep offshore Project is a key project for Total as the first Oil & Gas facilities to be installed in Namibian waters with 3,000 m water depth and uncommon reservoir characteristics with a CAPEX > 10 BUSD. 38 wells to be drilled and completed (19 OP and 19 GI) with a DRILLEX > 3 BUSD; out of ~2/3 to be ready before First Oil date.
The Venus Project will be developed with the objectives to maximize economical results by optimizing the reserves, the schedule, reducing the costs and the Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emission, while maintaining the technical quality of the installations, with high H3SE requirements and focus.
International and multi-cultural environment.
Many suppliers’ locations, several fabrications, preparation / testing / servicing sites worldwide

## About The Role
The Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust (WWT) launched its Blue Recovery work in 2021: a major initiative to deliver transformational environmental change in the UK. There is growing evidence showing the significant role that wetlands can play in four critical areas: storing carbon, reducing flooding, benefiting wellbeing and improving water quality, but these benefits are not widely understood.
WWT has brought together a consortium of sector leading organisations to help unlock and demonstrate the value of wetland creation, facilitating the creation of a network of wetlands that will deliver lasting impact and act as a catalyst for wider action. Its approach draws on the model used by the Sustainable Markets Initiative launched by our Patron, HRH King Charles III.
At the heart of WWT’s proposals is an ambition to create and restore 100,000 hectares of healthy wetland in the UK, conceived of as four networks:
* A carbon storage network, consisting of wetlands to sequester and store carbon
* A flood management network, consisting of wetland features to reduce flooding
* An urban wellbeing network, consisting of wetlands to improve wellbeing
* A water treatment network, consisting of wetlands to support biodiversity
This Blue Recovery will make a vital contribution to the UK’s environmental and climate change goals. **Role Outline**
You will be responsible for working with WWT’s Blue Recovery Leaders Group to drive forward this partnership leading to the delivery of projects that fulfil WWT’s Blue Recovery workstream. By building and maintaining close relationships with the Blue Recovery Leader’s Group drawn from industries including the water, construction, finance, agriculture and engineering sectors, you will support the group to develop projects that demonstrate the multiple benefits that wetlands provide to society.
You will act as WWT’s main lead on supporting the Blue Recovery Leaders Group and work with them to develop project ideas and proposals that fulfil WWT’s strategic ambitions. You will liaise between our Philanthropy & Partnerships, UK Programmes and Conservation Evidence Teams, coordinating input from them to ensure successful delivery of The Blue Recovery Leaders contribution towards WWT’s Strategic Plan.
**Hours:** This is a fixed-term contract for up to 12 months, working 22.5 hours per week. The hours will be worked across Monday – Friday.
**Location:** Hybrid working considered, based between Home and WWT Headquarters at Slimbridge, Gloucestershire
## About You
The key skills we are looking for are:
* Strong project development and project management skills
* Excellent stakeholder and partnership management
* Influencing and leadership without direct authority
* Strategic and creative problem-solving
* Outstanding communication and facilitation skills
You will be a committed person who cares deeply about the success and impact of your work. You will be a key advocate for multi-benefit wetlands, be enthusiastic about what you believe in, and can work closely and get the best from people across multiple disciplines within WWT.
You will be, able to nurture trusted relationships with colleagues in other teams and counterparts in other organisations. You will also be a great communicator, advocating your work successfully to a wide range of stakeholders.
You will have experience in developing successful projects and will understand the importance of following a project management framework.
If this sounds like you then we would very much like to hear from you. Come and join us in delivering our vision of a world where healthy wetland nature thrives and enriches lives.
## About Us
We’re WWT, and we’re on a mission to restore the super-powered ecosystems we call wetlands. There’s never been a more important moment for our work, and we’ve got some phenomenal people on the case.
Whether they’re taking a new visitor under their wing, or conducting ground-breaking research further afield, our team are second to none. And there’s nothing we love more than watching them soar.
Whatever you do here, you’ll be helping to restore wetlands and unlock their power. So, the only question left is, what role will you play?
**Why you’ll love working at WWT**
* Wake up every day knowing your work is helping to restore wetlands, and our world

* Life Assurance of three times your salary, for peace of mind for your loved ones

## About The Role
Do you enjoy being surrounded by old documents and seeing an administrative task through to completion? This is an excellent opportunity to support WWT by ensuring that our site documents are preserved and safe, in a logical order, and easily accessible when needed.
We are looking for a Volunteer Archivist to help us manage the large collection of physical records, files, and documents kept at WWT Slimbridge. You will be supporting our work by assisting site staff in sorting through boxes of site plans, maps, and other important documents. Once digitised, the files will be an excellent resource that can be shared and easily accessible by staff across WWT.
You will need a good eye for detail and enjoy systematically organising and cataloguing documents, identifying documents that need keeping, and ones that are either duplicates or no longer relevant or useful. This is an important role in capturing and recording information about our sites and buildings, ensuring our heritage of the last 80 years is preserved, and freeing up much-needed space.
This is a hands-on role that cannot be done remotely, although there may be a prospect in the future to undertake remote desk-based uploading and sorting of scanned documents. We are aiming to develop and expand a team of volunteer archivists across WWT who can inform and assist our other sites with their archiving needs. There would be opportunities to assist in the development of the framework for this, and opportunities to work at other sites if so desired.
Volunteers are an essential part of the WWT team, and we wouldn’t be able to maintain our internationally important wetland sites without their help. You will receive a very warm welcome, full induction & training, and be provided with any necessary equipment, uniforms, and anything else needed to thrive in your role.
**Main tasks**
* Organising and cataloguing boxes of site plans, maps, documents, and files
* Identifying documents of note
* Photocopying and digitising documents if needed
* Preparing and sending documents to be sent off-site for scanning
* Packing returned documents into archive boxes, labelling them, and preparing them to be taken off-site for safe storage
## About You
No previous experience is required for this role as full training will be provided, and a willingness to learn new skills is more important.
This role would suit you if:
* You can work independently using your own initiative and are self-motivated
* You are methodical and highly organised, with have good attention to detail
* You have excellent written communication skills
* You have (or are willing to develop) experience in filing and archiving administration
* You have an interest in and enthusiasm for the work of WWT
* You have a good understanding of using Microsoft Word and Excel
* You can save and organise electronic documents in a sensible consistent format
* You have experience of using commercial printers, photocopiers, and scanners (training provided)
**Additional notes**
* We are looking for volunteers who are available to help out one day a week (days and times flexible)
## About Us
We are WWT, and we’re on a mission to restore the super-powered ecosystems we call wetlands. There’s never been a more important moment for our work, and we’ve got some phenomenal people on the case.
Whether you’re looking to meet new people, learn new skills or spend time in our wildlife-rich wetlands, there’s a volunteer role for you. Just a few hours spent volunteering can really make a world of difference to our wildlife, and to you.
So, come surround yourself with the wonder of wetlands, and the people who inject their energy and passion into them. Whatever you do here, you’ll be helping to restore wetlands and unlock their power. The only question left is, what role will you play?
**Why you’ll love volunteering at WWT**
* Make a real contribution to the conservation and engagement work of WWT
* Work at one of our beautiful and internationally important wetland sites
* Be surrounded and inspired by like-minded nature lovers who bring energy, passion, and expertise to their role
* Make new friends and become part of a friendly and inclusive community
* Gain volunteering experience and learn & develop new skills
* Get volunteer discounts for WWT shops, café, and membership
* Get free entry to all our UK wetland centres, including for your family
* Receive access to wildlife talks, webinars, and practical information to help you manage your volunteer role & daily life
* Keep informed about what’s happening in our organisation and the positive change you are helping to make happen

1. OVERVIEW
Xstrahl has manufacturing facilities in the UK and USA and operates globally through its international network of distributors. Xstrahl is a leading designer and manufacturer of Superficial and Orthovoltage Medical X-ray Systems used in the treatment of cancers and dermatological disorders, as well as a pioneer in the development of advanced X-ray systems for pre-clinical radiation biology research.
The Production Quality Engineer is a new full-time graduate role in Xstrahl's UK production team. The role creates and maintains the build manuals and work instructions for Xstrahl's systems, carries out system sign-off checks, develops production jigs and test equipment, and manages production quality paperwork — non-conformance reports (NCRs), change requests (CRs) and production feedback reports (PFRs) — so that production issues are recorded, followed up and resolved.
Working alongside an experienced Production Project Engineer and spending regular time on the production floor, the job holder learns how Xstrahl's medical and research X-ray systems are built, tested and commissioned, and captures that knowledge so it is documented, repeatable and shared across the team. Build Documentation:
Owns the build manuals and work instructions for Xstrahl's systems, capturing build knowledge so every system can be built consistently from documented instructions. Work Instructions Proven

Carries out system sign-off activities, including electrical and mechanical checks, so every system leaves production verified and documented. NCR, CR, PFR & CAPA Management

**About Us**
YMCA is the oldest and largest youth charity in the world, founded in England in 1844. Today it's a global movement supporting more than 58 million people across 119 countries. In England & Wales, we operate as a federation of 80 local YMCAs, working independently to help young people belong, contribute and thrive in their communities. YMCA England & Wales acts as the national council — supporting local YMCAs, developing national programmes, and championing young people's voices with government.

We're looking for a Fundraising Database Assistant to join our Data, Insight and Supporter Experience (DISE) Team, part of our wider Fundraising Team.
